papers.title: Thermocatalytic transcarbonation with diethyl carbonate for valorization of glycerol : recycling siliceous bauxite residue waste components and exploring the potential of sodalite hydroxide reservoir
papers.journal: Repository of the Academy's Library (Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences)
papers.abstract: Bauxite residues contain katoites and desilication products (sodalite and cancrinite), which are excellent candidates for Earth-abundant heterogeneous base catalysts from industrial waste sources. For the first time, they were tested in synthetizing the renewable and promising fuel or fuel additive glycerol carbonate for the purpose of recycling glycerol by-products from biodiesel production. Incorporation of silicate was found to enhance the previously established excellent catalytic activity of tricalcium aluminate (Si-free katoite). Performance of sodalites containing four different cage anion-designed (OH, CO3, SO4, Cl) and carbonated cancrinite was determined to a much greater extent by their Brönsted OH content than by the basicity of the caged anions. Direct catalytic use of bauxite residue resulted in a glycerol carbonate yield of over 80%, but it was quickly deactivated due to the limited reusability of many of its most active components (i.e., Si-free and Si-containing katoites, chloride sodalites). However, hydroxysodalites showed excellent reusability, with a glycerol carbonate yield of around 80% even after 5 reuses. The activity of katoites and sodalities overtook that of many complex systems containing relatively rare metals, such as Ni, Cu, Zr, and Ce. Their excellent activity has made it possible to use diethyl carbonate solvent/reagent, which is more favourable in terms of sustainability, instead of the more widely applied dimethyl carbonate, even with as short reaction times as 30–60 min.

papers.title: Hypoxia-responsive supramolecular systems based on macrocycles and self-assembly structures.
papers.abstract: Hypoxia is closely associated with tumor progression, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and diagnostic challenges. The timely detection of hypoxia in live cancer cells is critical for early cancer diagnosis and for monitoring the effectiveness of anticancer therapies. Recently, there has been growing interest in non-covalent supramolecular design strategies for the development of hypoxia-sensitive sensors and prodrugs. Unlike the widely employed covalent approach, supramolecular chemistry eliminates the need for complex and time-consuming synthetic processes. Instead, the individual components of the sensor autonomously self-assemble into the desired structure. This review provides an overview of hypoxia-targeted and hypoxia-activated supramolecular probes, along with their mechanisms of action in tumor diagnosis and therapy. The supramolecular systems considered are classified according to the use of certain classes of macrocycles. The role of macrocyclic derivatives in the various proposed approaches and the response patterns of hypoxic targets will also be analyzed. Various representatives of the macrocyclic platforms, namely cyclodextrins, cucurbiturils, pillararenes, (thia)calixarenes, due to their properties such as molecular recognition, are used as molecular containers-carriers for pharmaceuticals and bio-organic fluorescent dyes. As a result of complex formation, the photostability and the signal-to-noise ratio of dyes increase. In addition, the solubility of hydrophobic guests in water improves, cytotoxicity is reduced, and targeted delivery promotes the accumulation of drugs/dyes in tumor cells.

papers.title: Nitric oxide in the occurrence and development of ischemic cerebrovascular disease.
papers.abstract: Since nitric oxide is a chemically highly reactive free radical that can act as both an oxidizing agent and a reducing agent, it is assumed that it has diverse effects on biological tissues. Nitric oxide is fundamentally important for the regulation of immune, reproductive and neuromuscular system functions and is the main signaling molecule and effector that can dilate blood vessels and modulate energy metabolism. This review examines the key role of nitric oxide in the mechanisms underlying the response to hypoxia, as well as in the effects of factors induced by hypoxia. The available conflicting information allowed us to conclude that at present, there is no consensus about the role of endogenous nitric oxide in the processes occurring after ischemic cerebrovascular disease.

papers.title: Hyperbaric oxygen for the treatment of traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.abstract: The therapeutic efficacy of hyperbaric oxygen therapy for traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury remains a subject of debate. To comprehensively evaluate the impact of hyperbaric oxygen on motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis. We performed a comprehensive search across PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and major Chinese databases for randomized controlled trials published through June 2025. A total of 15 randomized controlled trials were included. The pooled results indicated that hyperbaric oxygen therapy significantly improved the American Spinal Injury Association motor score (mean difference = 10.30, 95% confidence interval: 7.70-12.90), the total American Spinal Injury Association sensory score (mean difference = 29.29, 95% confidence interval: 18.82-39.75), the American Spinal Injury Association light touch score (mean difference = 9.84, 95% confidence interval: 6.15-13.53), and the American Spinal Injury Association pinprick score (mean difference = 8.75, 95% confidence interval: 4.40-13.11). Furthermore, hyperbaric oxygen therapy was associated with significant enhancements in the Barthel Index (mean difference = 16.60, 95% confidence interval: 10.51-22.68) and the Functional Independence Measure (mean difference = 17.41, 95% confidence interval: 10.83-23.98). In conclusion, adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy appears to improve motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury compared to conventional treatments alone. However, due to methodological limitations and potential publication bias in the included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution, and further high-quality, multi-center randomized controlled trials are warranted.

papers.title: High levels of nitric oxide and peroxynitrite with protein nitration: a new therapeutic target for gliomas.
papers.abstract: The gap junction signaling pathway is a core hub mediating intercellular communication, which plays a vital role in maintaining tissue homeostasis, and its dysfunction is closely related to glioma. Nitroproteomics studies have shown that protein tyrosine nitration plays an important role in the progression of glioma, and gap junction is one of the significantly enriched nitroprotein signaling pathways in glioma; proteoformics reveals that nitration can produce various proteoforms of related proteins, which have different functional states in different subtypes of glioma, suggesting that nitration may alter the functional states of related proteins in gap junction pathways. When levels of nitric oxide and peroxynitrite (ONOO-) rise, they induce the tyrosine nitration of key proteins in the gap junction pathway; this nitration not only interferes with the function of the gap junction pathway, but also affects other gap junction-linked signaling networks. Forming an attack network on the gap junction pathway through multi-pathway cross-regulation has great potential for therapeutic strategies targeting the gap junction pathway. We recommend in-depth studies of the gap junction signaling pathway and potential drugs targeting gap junction signals, including drugs that target gap junction communication activators, nitration inhibitors, and drugs that directly target specific nitroproteins, combined with conventional chemotherapy or immune checkpoint inhibitors, as well as the construction of personalized medical frameworks as important future research directions.

papers.title: Antitrust Regulation of Algorithmic "Platform-Driven Involution'': From Governing the Corporate Person to Governing the Platform Ecosystem
papers.abstract: Digital platforms increasingly govern competition through algorithmically administered rules that allocate visibility, subsidies, commissions, participation opportunities, and sanctions. This article reconstructs ``platform-driven involution'' as a testable, portfolio-based theory-of-harm framework rather than a freestanding antitrust offense. Its application remains anchored in market definition, dominance, identified conduct under Article 22 of China's Anti-Monopoly Law, causal proof, competitive effects, and objective justification. The article clarifies that ecosystem analysis supplements rather than replaces relevant-market analysis and develops an evidence architecture for separating platform-induced effects from macroeconomic, demand, cost, and merchant-specific confounders. It then distinguishes preventive measures already supported by Chinese hard law or voluntary compliance guidance from compulsory competition-specific filing and pre-deployment assessment that would require clearer future authorization. The 2026 Trip.com decision is used to show how traffic allocation, exclusivity, lowest-price requirements, technical monitoring, and sanctions can form an integrated abuse architecture while liability remains tied to established statutory categories. Comparative analysis of EU platform regulation and Google Shopping supports calibrated procedural prevention, meaningful explanation, and causal discipline without protecting inefficient competitors or condemning aggressive competition.

The 2026 Trip.com decision is used to show how traffic allocation, exclusivity, lowest-price requirements, technical monitoring, and sanctions can form an integrated abuse architecture while liability remains tied to established statutory categories.

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.abstract: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-performance validation.

The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-performance validation.

papers.title: Current status of room temperature magnetic compensation in impurity-doped Mn4N epitaxial thin films
papers.abstract: Mn4N, a ferrimagnet that does not contain rare-earth elements, possesses attractive properties for spintronics applications. In particular, Mn4N epitaxial films exhibit a small spontaneous magnetization of about 100 kA m(-1), a large spin polarization (p = 0.8), and large perpendicular magnetic anisotropy with a magnetic anisotropy constant of approximately 10(5) J m(-3). More importantly, achieving magnetic compensation at room temperature is possible through impurity doping. This property is particularly significant for spin-torque-based spintronics applications. In the vicinity of the magnetization and/or angular momentum compensation points, magnetization dynamics can be substantially accelerated, enabling high-speed switching and domain wall motion. This article surveys the magnetic properties of impurity-doped Mn4N epitaxial films grown on SrTiO3(001) substrates, highlighting recent results obtained with Cu-, Ag-, Au-, and Pd-doped Mn4N films in comparison with Ni- and Cr-doped Mn4N films. Furthermore, with a view to device applications of Mn4N, we present the formation of ultrathin (similar to 4 nm) Pt epitaxial films with a <100> orientation on MgO (001), which is essential for injecting spins into Mn4N-based overlayers by utilizing the spin Hall effect of heavy metals. papers.title: Reproducible chiroptical activity from aggregated chiral thienopyrroledione-fluorene π-conjugated polymers
papers.abstract: Chiral pi-conjugated polymers have attracted considerable interest because their chiral-aggregated structures can generate pronounced chiroptical responses. Here, we report the design, synthesis, and chiroptical characterization of fluorene - thienopyrroledione polymers bearing a single chiral center in each repeating unit, (R)- and (S)-PFTPD, prepared via direct arylation polycondensation to minimize structural defects. Although only weak chiroptical activity was observed in the solution, the addition of 1-butanol to CHCl3 solutions of the polymers induced the formation of stable aggregates that exhibited strong circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL). Systematic examination of the sample preparation parameters revealed that the mixing process critically influences the chiroptical properties. Dropwise addition of 1-butanol under controlled stirring provided the most reliable results, yielding highly reproducible CD spectra. Under these optimized conditions, the aggregates exhibited an average dissymmetry factor (|g abs|) of 1.5 & times; 10-2 and a CPL dissymmetry factor (|g lum|) of 1.9 & times; 10-2. These values rank among the highest reported for pi-conjugated polymer aggregates bearing only a single chiral source per repetition unit. This study demonstrates that precise control over the solvent-mixing process is essential for the reproducible emergence of chiroptical properties and highlights the chiral TPD unit as a promising platform for chiroptical polymer materials.

papers.title: Somatosensory phenotyping in women with persistent genital arousal disorder: a case-control study.
papers.abstract: Introduction: Persistent genital arousal disorder (PGAD) is a rare and distressing condition characterized by persistent, unwanted genital arousal in the absence of sexual desire or stimulation. Persistent genital arousal disorder is increasingly recognized as a disorder of abnormal genital sensory processing, but objective neurophysiological data remain limited. Methods: We conducted an exploratory case-control study to characterize somatosensory function in women with PGAD. Thirty women with PGAD and 30 age-matched healthy controls were recruited at Leiden University Medical Center. Participants underwent quantitative sensory testing (QST) at hand and external genital sites, conditioned pain modulation, and corneal confocal microscopy. Results: Hand QST values were within normal range in both groups. In the genital region, PGAD participants showed altered thermal pain processing, with cold and heat hyperalgesia compared with controls. Mechanical pain thresholds did not differ between groups; however, PGAD participants reported higher pain intensity ratings to mechanical stimuli and showed significantly greater temporal summation of pain in genital regions. Genital dynamic mechanical allodynia occurred more frequently in PGAD participants but did not differ significantly at the group level. Conditioned pain modulation magnitude did not differ between groups and showed substantial interindividual variability. Corneal confocal microscopy abnormalities were observed in a proportion of participants in both groups without significant between-group differences. Discussion: These findings show that QST is feasible in women with PGAD and indicate that PGAD is associated with altered somatosensory processing demonstrating genital thermal hypersensitivity and central pain sensitization in a subset of patients.

papers.title: Designing an Integrated Play Therapy Program Based on the Cognitive-Behavioral Approach and Sensory Integration for Children With Autism
papers.journal: The Psychological Research in Individuals with Exceptional Needs
papers.abstract: The present study aimed to design an integrated play therapy program based on the cognitive-behavioral approach and sensory integration for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). In terms of purpose, this was an applied study, and in terms of methodology, it employed a qualitative research design. Using thematic analysis based on Braun and Clarke’s (2006) six-phase framework, valid and up-to-date theoretical and empirical evidence was systematically reviewed and coded. A step-by-step framework illustrating the process of structuring and designing the integrated play therapy program based on the cognitive-behavioral approach and sensory integration for children with autism was developed according to Intervention Mapping (IM). The integrated cognitive-behavioral play therapy and sensory integration program was subsequently presented to 10 faculty members from the University of Tehran and experienced therapists working in a university clinic for children with neurodevelopmental disorders who were professionally involved in the field of autism spectrum disorder. They were asked to provide expert feedback on the developed intervention package to facilitate its refinement. Quantitative assessment of the content validity of the integrated play therapy program was conducted using the Content Validity Index (CVI) and Content Validity Ratio (CVR). The results indicated that the integrated program resulted in the development of a valid 12-session protocol. The inductive thematic analysis process progressed from 52 initial codes to 22 axial codes, 14 subthemes, and 8 main themes. These eight themes constituted the conceptual pillars of the protocol and integrated the cognitive-behavioral and sensory integration approaches within a spiral, play-based structure, thereby empirically demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed program design. Another finding of the present study was that the integrated program demonstrated satisfactory validity. The CVI calculated for each of the 12 items corresponding to the intervention sessions ranged from .80 to .90, with all values exceeding the accepted threshold of .79. Internal validity was confirmed through member checking and calculation of the CVI. The developed integrated program constitutes a valid intervention for improving sensory responses in children with sensory modulation disorder. Based on the findings, it is recommended that psychologists working with children with special needs use the 12-session integrated protocol developed in this study as a standardized intervention package.

In terms of purpose, this was an applied study, and in terms of methodology, it employed a qualitative research design. The results indicated that the integrated program resulted in the development of a valid 12-session protocol.

papers.title: Enhancing mass transport in redox flow batteries with 3D-printed triply periodic minimal surface electrode structures
papers.abstract: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures offer a compelling route for designing porous electrodes with tunable architectures for electrochemical applications such as redox flow batteries. In this study, we fabricated carbonaceous TPMS electrodes, including gyroid, diamond, IWP, and cubic geometries, using digital light processing, and evaluated their performance in single-electrolyte flow cells using an organic redox couple. The printing process and subsequent thermal treatment produced conductive porous electrodes that closely replicated the intended TPMS geometries, preserving the characteristic features of each design. Through a detailed analysis of pressure drop, surface area, and electrochemical behavior, we identified the diamond design as particularly effective in enhancing mass transport while maintaining low hydraulic resistance. We further assessed gyroid structures, selected for being the most well-known among TPMSs, across a range of porosities, finding that higher porosity improved flow performance despite a reduction in surface area, an advantageous trade-off for electrolytes with facile kinetics and low ionic conductivity. Comparison with a commercial carbon felt electrode revealed comparable ohmic resistance and favorable flow characteristics, though reduced electrochemical surface area limited the achievable current densities. To isolate mass transport effects, a kinetically facile organic redox couple was employed, after which a representative 3D-printed gyroid electrode was evaluated in a proof-of-concept full-cell vanadium redox flow battery. A full-cell test demonstrated the feasibility of printed electrodes, achieving a voltage efficiency of 76% at a current density of 50 mA cm−2. These findings demonstrate the potential of architected 3D printed electrodes for future redox flow batteries and highlight the importance of tuning geometry and porosity to balance power output, mass transport, and system-level pumping losses.

papers.title: Airdrop Sybil Attack detection framework supported by machine learning
papers.journal: International Journal of Electronics and Telecommunication Systems
papers.abstract: A skilled hunter may earn thousands of dollars in tokens from a single airdrop, making airdrop Sybil assaults a profitable endeavor. In this situation, Sybil assaults are not always wanted by projects and are often seen as improper behavior by honest individuals, which may negatively impact a project's image. It is thus to be anticipated that detection methods for Sybil assaults would be continuously enhanced. This study presents a multistep structure. Its concept is to sort blockchain addresses and give each one a score that indicates whether it belongs to the Sybil or regular class. Topologies were classified using a graph isomorphism network, whose parameters were adjusted using a dataset that the authors labeled. In subsequent phases, the account clustering operation was performed using a DBSCAN. Ultimately, 76% of the examined accounts were classified as Sybils. Compared to the official ZK sync eligibility list, we found 342 addresses that received airdrop tokens but were marked as Sybil by our solution.

papers.title: Large-Tiny Spin-Stripe SDW Order in La 3 Ni 2 O 7 via 139 La-NQR Spectroscopy: Reconsideration Based on the Am 2 m Structure
papers.journal: Journal of the Physical Society of Japan
papers.abstract: The lower-symmetry Am2m structure was recently proposed as the intrinsic ambient-pressure phase of La 3 Ni 2 O 7 based on synchrotron x-ray diffraction, whereas earlier studies investigated its properties assuming the commonly accepted Amam structure. Here, we reexamine the crystal structure in La 3 Ni 2 O 7 and the spin configuration of spin-density-wave (SDW) state via 139 La nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR). The observation of two distinct La(2) sites in the NQR spectra is naturally accounted for by the Am2m structure without any special assumptions, whereas it cannot be reconciled within the Amam framework. Within the Am2m framework, we reanalyze the spin configuration of the SDW phase and identify it as a large-tiny spin-stripe structure, arising naturally from two inequivalent Ni sites with large and tiny magnetic moments. These results establish the itinerant nature of the SDW order at ambient pressure in La 3 Ni 2 O 7 , providing a basis for understanding its relationship to the emergence of high-T c superconductivity under high pressure.

papers.title: Sorbates from 1,1-Dialkylsubstituted Alkenes and 3-Haloacrylic Esters via Pd(II)-Isohypsic Catalysis: Focus on Terpenes
papers.abstract: Limonene and other 1,1-dialkylsubstituted alkenes undergo a regioselective Pd(II)-catalyzed C-H/C-X coupling with (E) and (Z)-3-bromoacrylates affording 4,4-disubstituted sorbate derivatives as mixtures of geometrical isomers (16 examples). This coupling, unknown to date for the synthesis of 1,3-dienes, follows a mechanism distinct from the well-known Mizoroki-Heck, and works where the Mizoroki-Heck fails. Density functional theory (DFT) computations allowed to propose a plausible mechanism for this transformation.

papers.title: Acute Kidney Injury Disrupts Cardiac Remodeling via SerpinA3N
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
papers.abstract: Background Cardiorenal syndrome type 3 describes cardiac injury triggered by acute kidney injury (AKI). AKI caused by ischemia reperfusion injury represents a model for kidney injury during kidney transplant. It is well known that kidney transplant recipients are at increased risk to develop cardiac fibrosis; however, the molecular mechanisms linking renal injury to myocardial remodeling or cardiac fibrosis remain unclear. Methods Using a C57BL/6J mouse model of ischemia reperfusion injury–AKI, we combined proteomics and RNA seqencing transcriptomics to define early cardiac responses. We validated the proteomics and RNA sequencing data with quantitative polymerase chain reaction, ELISA, cytokine array, and western blotting for profibrotic and injury markers. We assessed SerpinA3N function using a granzyme B activity assay kit and XAV939, an inhibitor of SerpinA3N. Ingenuity pathway analysis further confirmed serine protease activity inhibition and increased expression of cardiac fibrosis–related genes after AKI. Results Successful establishment of renal ischemia reperfusion injury causing AKI, followed by significant induction of cardiac injury. AKI significantly upregulated SerpinA3N in the heart while suppressing serine protease (granzyme B) activity. Concomitantly, AKI hearts displayed elevated profibrotic genes ( FN1, COL1A1, TGF‐β1 ), mitochondrial dysfunction, and heightened inflammatory signaling. In vitro, inhibition of SerpinA3N with XAV939 restored granzyme B activity, confirming direct suppression by SerpinA3N. Conclusions We conclude that SerpinA3N serves as a key mediator of cardiorenal syndrome type 3 pathogenesis, by inhibiting granzyme B, which promotes profibrotic remodeling in the heart following AKI. Targeting SerpinA3N could be a potential therapeutic approach that restores balanced extracellular matrix turnover and mitigates cardiac fibrosis.

papers.title: No evidence of elevated mercury in sessile coastal biota exposed to Greenland glacial runoff
papers.abstract: Abstract Melting glaciers have been claimed to be a significant and unaccounted-for source of mercury (Hg) in Greenland, raising concerns for communities, ecosystem health, and economics. Here we demonstrate, however, consistently low Hg concentrations in sessile organisms across >100 km spatial gradients and decadal time scales in three Southwest Greenland fjords exposed to glacial melt. Average Hg concentrations ranged 21.6–53.4 ng g −1 dw in the blue mussel Mytilus edulis , <7 ng g −1 dw in the macroalga Fucus vesiculosus , and 5.7–20.2 ng g −1 dw in Ascophyllum nodosum . These Hg concentrations in biota are low relative to international thresholds and detection limits and showed no temporal relationship with glacial and freshwater runoff. Our results therefore provide no evidence that Greenland glacial runoff is associated with elevated Hg concentrations in sessile coastal biota. Combined with previous studies on Hg in Greenland’s coastal zone, there is now substantial evidence against the claim that the Greenland Ice Sheet has implications for Hg budgets and coastal ecosystems.

papers.title: Toward chemically accurate quantum simulations on quantum hardware: A quantum-HPC hybrid approach
papers.abstract: We report one of the most comprehensive experimental demonstrations to date of quantum-computing-based molecular simulation on IQM's Sirius 24-qubit superconducting quantum processor, using up to 16 operational qubits. We employ Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD) with the Local Unitary Cluster Jastrow (LUCJ) Ansatz to compute ground-state energies of benchmark molecular systems, including H2, LiH, BeH2, H2O, and NH3. We further introduce the linear-CNOT unitary coupled-cluster singles and doubles Ansatz within the SQD framework, reducing the classical pre-computation overhead at the cost of increased quantum circuit depth and demonstrate its effectiveness by accurately recovering the ground-state energies of H2, LiH, and BeH2. A comparative analysis of the two Ansätze is presented, highlighting their respective merits, demerits, and practical use cases in near-term quantum simulations. In addition, we perform one-dimensional potential energy surface (1D-PES) scans for H2 and HeH+ using STO-3G and 6-31G basis sets and for LiH and BeH2 using STO-3G. We also report the first experimental generation of a full two-dimensional potential energy surface (2D-PES) map, consisting of a 32 × 32 grid in bond length and bond angle, for the water molecule in the STO-3G basis on IQM quantum hardware. Beyond small-molecule benchmarks, we integrate Density Matrix Embedding Theory (DMET) with SQD(LUCJ) to obtain chemically accurate 4-electron-in-4-orbital active-space energies for eight ligand-like molecules, as well as for the pharmacologically relevant amantadine molecular system, representing the first of such experimental demonstrations. Across all studies, the majority of quantum-computed energies agree with reference full configuration interaction results and with DMET-complete active space CI energies for embedded systems, to within chemical accuracy for the chosen basis sets. These results demonstrate the robustness of quantum sampling-based classical diagonalization approaches while highlighting the promise of hybrid embedding strategies combined with near-term Ansätze for advancing quantum chemistry toward classically intractable molecular systems and establishing their practicality on current quantum hardware.

papers.title: Controlled Component Segregation in Vapor-Deposited Organic Semiconductor Glass Mixtures
papers.abstract: Abstract Multicomponent vapor-deposited organic glasses are essential in organic electronic applications, but achieving controlled component segregation at the nano/mesoscale remains a challenge, hindering the rational development of high-performance devices. In this study, we investigate binary organic semiconductor mixtures of TPD (N,N′-Bis(3-methylphenyl)-N,N′-diphenylbenzidine) and TCTA (Tris(4-carbazoyl-9-ylphenyl)amine). Despite being miscible in the bulk liquid state, the co-deposited glassy films of these two organic semiconductors exhibit a range of segregation behaviors, from homogeneous to clearly phase-separated structures. We employed differential scanning calorimetry and resonant soft X-ray scattering (RSoXS) to study the component segregation behavior and used the National Institute of Standards and Technology RSoXS Simulation Suite, paired with Atomic Force Microscopy, to interpret the energy-dependent RSoXS spectra. Our results indicate that component segregation in co-deposited TPD/TCTA films is due to a kinetically-arrested nucleation-and-growth mechanism, in contrast to the segregation mechanism of a previously reported TPD/DO37 (disperse orange 37) mixture which is strongly immiscible in bulk. This work provides a demonstration of tunable molecular aggregation in organic semiconductor glasses, enabling access to a continuum of morphologies from homogeneously mixed to segregated phases.

papers.title: Energy-efficient atmospheric water harvesting using MOF-801 and microwave-synthesized Al-fumarate: linking micro–mesoporous structure to sorption and regeneration behavior
papers.abstract: Abstract Atmospheric water harvesting (AWH) has emerged as a promising route to mitigate freshwater scarcity in arid and semi-arid regions. Existing studies typically evaluate individual metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) under limited conditions, leaving a gap in comparative assessments that link pore architecture to sorption behavior. This work aims to establish a direct, climate-relevant comparison between MOF-801 and Al-fumarate, for AWH applications. The sorbents were synthesized and characterized using XRD, FTIR, BET, SEM, and TGA to elucidate their structural and textural properties. Water vapor adsorption–desorption performance was quantified under controlled relative humidity and temperature, supported by thermodynamic analysis of the isosteric heat of adsorption. MOF-801 demonstrated higher water uptake at moderate humidity (0.247 g H 2 O g − 1 at 40% RH and 20°C), while Al-fumarate showed enhanced performance under more humid conditions (0.278 g H 2 O g − 1 at 80% RH and 25°C). Both sorbents were regenerated at ~ 80°C, corresponding to an energy requirement of 1.2–1.5 MJ L − 1 . Thermodynamic analysis indicated a higher initial isosteric heat of adsorption (Q st ) for MOF-801, consistent with stronger water-framework interactions in drier atmospheres, whereas Al-fumarate exhibited a flatter Q st profile favorable for humid conditions. Both materials were further evaluated in four-month field tests in contrasting humid (Rasht) and arid (Isfahan) climates to assess cycling stability. The results providing practical guidelines for selecting energy-efficient MOFs tailored to specific climatic conditions

papers.title: Plasticize Me Sweetly: Sugar-Based Plasticizers for Poly(lactic acid)
papers.abstract: Abstract Carbohydrates are among the most abundant biopolymers in the world and offer a promising source for the synthesis of value-added chemicals. Galactaric acid is an attractive biobased building block that has not yet been fully exploited. Currently, regulatory, sustainability, safety-by-design, and performance requirements for polymer additives are becoming increasingly strict. As a result, innovation in this field must be accelerated to develop new materials with enhanced properties. With this objective, new sugar-based plasticizers based on galactaric acid have been synthesized. Poly(lactic acid) (PLA) was selected as a brittle, biobased polymer, to evaluate the ability of these additives to improve its mechanical properties. The best additive led to an increase of the elongation at break up to 260% when compared to the starting PLA. Experimental results have been supported by computational studies and show how small modifications in the molecular structure can influence both the synthesis and the performance of these additives.

papers.title: In silico evaluation of multilocus DNA barcodes for Aspergillus species identification
papers.abstract: Accurate species-level identification of Aspergillus is clinically important because closely related species may differ in virulence and antifungal susceptibility. However, quantitative comparisons of commonly used DNA barcode loci remain limited. This study compared the discriminatory capacities of the internal transcribed spacer (ITS), β-tubulin ( benA ), and calmodulin ( CaM ) loci across selected Aspergillus reference genome assemblies using an in silico multilocus approach. Whole-genome sequences representing 180 Aspergillus species were retrieved from the NCBI RefSeq and GenBank databases. Barcode regions were extracted in silico using published primer pairs, and 57 species meeting the inclusion criteria for all three primary loci were evaluated for sequence variation and candidate-species reduction patterns. Principal coordinate analysis was used to visualize genetic relationships, while cyp51A was examined as an illustrative supplementary analysis for the selected Aspergillus flavus/A. austwickii reference-sequence pair, which remained indistinguishable across the three primary loci. PCoA revealed clustering associated with Aspergillus section classification, with the first two coordinates accounting for 20.4% and 18.2% of the variation represented by positive eigenvalues. PERMANOVA of the combined multilocus distance matrix showed that section membership accounted for 82.7% of the variation (R 2 = 0.827, pseudo-F = 17.475, P < 0.001). Reference-based candidate-species analysis using a ≥99% operational sequence identity threshold demonstrated differences in discriminatory performance among loci, while sensitivity analyses at ≥99.5%, ≥99.8%, and 100% showed that resolution was partly threshold-dependent. ITS showed the lowest discriminatory capacity. At ≥99%, benA and CaM each resolved 43 of 57 species to a single candidate, although benA yielded a smaller mean candidate-set size. The combined use of benA and CaM provided the strongest resolution, resolving 47 of 57 species to a single candidate, while performance at more stringent thresholds was marker-dependent. An illustrative cyp51A analysis revealed additional nucleotide differences between the selected A. flavus/A. austwickii reference sequences. Overall, discriminatory performance depended on the locus, targeted region, primer pair, reference database composition, and analytical approach, suggesting that in silico assessment may help prioritize informative barcode regions for subsequent sequence-based studies.

papers.title: Analysis of heat transfer due to steady MHD flow in a porous channel with Navier slip and convective boundary
papers.journal: Multiscale and Multidisciplinary Modeling Experiments and Design
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the flow and heat transfer characteristics of a magnetohydrodynamic fluid flow in a porous channel. Model equations are derived from the Navier-Stokes equation and the energy equation. The energy equation in this study incorporates viscous dissipation, internal heat generation/absorption, and Joule heating. By applying suitable transformations, the conservative momentum and energy equation are transformed into non-linear ordinary differential equations (ODEs). A closed form solution to the model equations was obtained. By taking into account characteristics like Biot number, Reynolds number, Brinkman number, Magnetic parameter, and others, the investigation on the normalized shear stress at the walls, temperature profiles were possible with aid of Tables and graphical presentations. For practical and engineering purposes, local Nusselt number, skin friction and mass flow rate of the physical constraints was tabulated. This gives important insights about the systems behavior under various settings. The graphical results indicate that the velocity profile exhibits a decrease as the magnetic parameter, Reynolds number and upper wall slip increase. Temperature decreases as Peclet number and slip parameters increase. Heat source/sink and Joule heating were observed to significantly influence the temperature field while the Biot number acts as a modifier in the temperature field as it dictates points of reversals near the convective wall.

papers.title: Prolonged static aging of olefin-based inverse emulsion drilling fluids: temperature–time effects on rheology, stability, and filtration
papers.abstract: Abstract Synthetic-based drilling fluids (SBFs) formulated as olefin-based inverse emulsions are widely used in deepwater operations, where prolonged static intervals expose the fluid to high temperatures without shear. This study investigated the coupled effects of aging temperature (100–150 °C) and static exposure time (24–168 h) on the rheological behavior, emulsion stability, and filtration performance of an olefin-based synthetic drilling fluid using a Central Composite Design. The response surface models for the Herschel–Bulkley parameters were statistically significant (p≤0.05, R 2 =0.978–0.992). Yield stress exhibited a nonlinear response, decreasing by ~12% at intermediate conditions (125 °C, 96 h) relative to the unaged fluid, but dropping near zero at experimental boundaries. The consistency index reached values up to seven times higher at 142.7 °C after 147 h, while the flow behavior index decreased from 0.70 to 0.44. At a shear rate of 8 s⁻ 1 , apparent viscosity increased by 8% after 45 h and 18% after 147 h at 142.7 °C, reaching 30% at 150 °C after 96 h. Prolonged aging also promoted macroscopic phase separation and brine manifestation. Filtration behavior was nonlinear, and an additional test using the filtration-control additive aged at 150 °C for 96 h yielded only 1 mL of filtrate, suggesting thermal changes in the additive favored pore plugging and restricted fluid loss. Thermogravimetric analysis indicated thermal susceptibility of emulsifier and filtration-control components at approximately 102–120 °C. These results show that aging time is a critical factor governing the long-term performance of olefin-based synthetic drilling fluids.

papers.title: Frailty and the incidence of major ocular diseases: a prospective cohort study integrating proteomic mediation analysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Background The long-term association between frailty phenotype and major vision-threatening ocular diseases (age-related macular degeneration (AMD), diabetic retinopathy (DR), glaucoma, and cataract), as well as the underlying molecular mechanisms, remain unclear. Methods Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the association between frailty status (classified as non-frail, prefrail, or frail) and the risk of four ocular diseases. Olink proteomics identified plasma proteins signatures associated with frailty status and ocular diseases. Mediation analysis assessed the overall and stage-specific (prefrail vs. frail) proteins as potential mediators. Results During a median follow-up of 15.7 years, prefrailty and frailty were associated with significantly elevated risks of AMD (Prefrail: HR = 1.17; Frail: HR = 1.49), DR (Prefrail: HR = 1.96; Frail: HR = 3.91), glaucoma (Prefrail: HR = 1.13; Frail: HR = 1.61), and cataract (Prefrail: HR = 1.16; Frail: HR = 1.49) (all P < 0.001). Proteomic profiling revealed 1,068 and 1,387 proteins associated with prefrailty and frailty, respectively, enriched in immune-inflammatory pathways (e.g., leukocyte migration). Similarly, proteins associated with all four ocular diseases were enriched in inflammatory and cell adhesion pathways. Mediation analysis further demonstrated that a spectrum of plasma proteins partially explained these associations, with a stage-specific escalation in the proportion of harmful mediators observed in DR. Conclusions These findings establish a significant link between frailty and common ocular diseases, unveiling a mediating role of systemic inflammatory and extracellular matrix proteins, with a progressive, stage-specific pattern in DR. These results highlight frailty as both a marker of shared pathways in systemic and ocular aging, and a potential integrated biomarker for interventions aimed at preventing vision loss.

papers.title: Geoeconomic fragmentation and the erosion of TRIPS flexibilities in technology access and distributive justice in the Global South
papers.abstract: Abstract The rise of geoeconomic fragmentation and techno-nationalism is fundamentally reshaping the global intellectual property (IP) regime. While the TRIPS Agreement was originally presented as a carefully balanced bargain that preserved flexibilities for developing countries, contemporary security-driven export controls, investment screening, industrial subsidies, and strategic technology restrictions are increasingly constraining those flexibilities. This paper critically examines how the securitisation of technology and the weaponisation of supply chains are eroding the policy space of Global South countries to access, adapt, and diffuse critical technologies in pharmaceuticals, green energy, digital infrastructure, and artificial intelligence. Drawing on international trade law, political economy, and distributive justice frameworks, the paper analyses the interplay between TRIPS Articles 7, 8, 31, and 66.2 and the expanding use of national security exceptions. It argues that the current trajectory risks transforming IP from a development tool into an instrument of technological hierarchy and proposes pathways for reclaiming regulatory sovereignty and reconstructing a more equitable technology governance architecture in a multipolar world.

papers.title: Toward Property-Directed Catalytic Skeletal Editing of Functional Organic Materials
papers.abstract: Abstract Late-stage skeletal editing has emerged as a useful strategy in synthetic and medicinal chemistry for altering molecular frameworks by atom insertion, deletion, replacement, or bond reorganization. Functional organic molecules and materials are commonly optimized through peripheral substitution and de novo framework construction. Direct modification of an existing skeleton provides a complementary means of tuning electronic structure, molecular shape, chirality, packing, and processability. Herein we examine catalytic skeletal editing with an emphasis on functional organic materials, specifically π-conjugated molecules, dyes, polymers, and covalent frameworks. Representative examples are evaluated in terms of catalytic status and experimentally demonstrated properties. Key requirements for broader application include site selectivity, element transfer, catalyst compatibility, and control of editing extent in extended materials. The emerging opportunity is to move skeletal editing from reaction-centered diversification toward catalyst-controlled, property-directed modification.

papers.title: Mechanisms of Surface Degradation and Mechanical Property Deterioration in Haynes 230 Under High-Temperature Ultrahigh Vacuum
papers.abstract: Abstract Haynes 230 alloy is widely used as a high-temperature structural material in hot-end components. To investigate the mechanisms underlying surface-defect evolution and mechanical-property degradation under high-temperature ultrahigh-vacuum conditions, exposure tests were conducted for up to 2000 h. Tensile tests were performed on as-received and exposed specimens at room temperature and 900 ℃. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) revealed selective volatilization of alloying elements from the material surface at high temperature, accompanied by M 6 C carbide precipitation and grain-boundary sinking. Voids were also observed beneath the M 6 C carbide precipitates, while M 23 C 6 carbides precipitated along internal grain boundaries. After exposure, the yield strength and elongation decreased slightly at room temperature. This degradation was primarily attributed to preferential cracking of brittle M 6 C carbides and debonding of M 23 C 6 carbides from the matrix during loading, both of which promoted microcrack initiation. By contrast, pronounced mechanical degradation occurred during tensile testing at 900 ℃. Cr depletion inhibited the formation of a protective oxide scale, leaving the surface susceptible to continued oxidation. Concurrently, local stress concentrations associated with grain-boundary sinking promoted preferential cracking along grain boundaries. Once initiated, the cracks propagated readily, while oxygen diffused rapidly along the grain boundaries; together, these processes severely degraded the overall mechanical performance of the alloy.

papers.title: Mechanical and Thermal Characterization of Natural Composites for Sustainable Applications
papers.journal: Journal of Research and Applications in Mechanical Engineering
papers.abstract: This study explores the development and mechanical characterization of sustainable hybrid composites reinforced with rockwool, conch shell powder, and flax fibers within an epoxy matrix. Two distinct composite formulations were fabricated: Rockwool/Conch/Epoxy (C-1) and Rockwool/Flax/Epoxy (C-2), each comprising 30 wt.% reinforcement (15 wt.% rockwool fibers and 15 wt.% conch powder or flax fibers) and 70 wt.% epoxy resin. The composites were produced using the hand lay-up method followed by compression molding. Comprehensive mechanical tests, including tensile and flexural strength assessments, were conducted in accordance with ASTM standards. Additionally, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), water-absorption testing and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) were employed to evaluate thermal stability, moisture affinity, and microstructural characteristics. The results indicated that C-2 exhibited superior tensile and flexural strengths compared to C-1, attributed to the enhanced fiber–matrix bonding facilitated by flax fibers. Conversely, C-1 demonstrated better thermal stability but also higher water uptake, reflecting the porous, hydrophilic nature of conch shell particles. SEM analysis revealed effective dispersion of reinforcements and strong interfacial adhesion in C-2, whereas C-1 showed minor voids around conch particles. These findings highlight the potential of integrating natural and industrial waste materials to develop high-performance, eco-friendly composites with tailored mechanical, thermal, and moisture-management properties suitable for various structural applications.

papers.title: Numerical Simulation and Thermal Performance of a Novel Parabolic Solar Collector Panels
papers.journal: Journal of Research and Applications in Mechanical Engineering
papers.abstract: This study investigates the design of a novel parabolic solar collector. It examines the effects of solar radiation on the collector panels and the flow characteristics of water through the system. The design incorporates two solar collector panels, each measuring 2×1.5 meters, with 2-inch diameter water pipes extending 11 meters in total. The parabolic panels have a focal point positioned 0.25 meters above the collector surface. A computational fluid dynamics (CFD) analysis was performed for flow rates of 0.25, 0.50, 0.75 and 1.00 liters per minute. The computational domain consisted of 1,520,000 mesh elements for analyzing solar thermal energy and 130,000 elements for simulating heat transfer from the radiation panels to the water within the pipes. The optimal flow rate was found to be between 0.50 and 0.75 liters per minute. The results show that the designed parabolic heat collector achieves maximum thermal efficiencies of 36.03% and 41.57%, respectively.

papers.title: Constructed a stable coordination polymer for highly efficient and selective capture of thorium
papers.abstract: Abstract The efficient separation of thorium (Th) from chemically similar rare earth elements (REEs) is technically challenging. In this work, a stable coordination polymer (Ni-tfc-CP) was fabricated by adopting the strategy of in-situ incorporation of hydrophobic groups. Ni-tfc-CP exhibits excellent structural stability over a wide pH range of 2–11 and under high-temperature conditions up to 247°C. The abundant carboxyl oxygen active binding sites on the surface of Ni-tfc-CP, provides favorable environment for Th(IV) uptake. The maximum adsorption capacity was calculated to 518.9 mg g⁻¹, by fitting the equilibrium data to the Langmuir model. Moreover, it showed an ultra-fast adsorption rate and reached equilibrium within 5 minutes. Notably, competitive tests confirmed the superior selectivity of Ni-tfc-CP for Th(IV), with a high distribution coefficient of 6×10⁵ mL g⁻¹. This study provides meaningful guidance for the rational development of functional materials toward nuclide separation.

papers.title: Microwave assisted extraction and Mannich type modification of date palm trunk lignin: Structural, surface, and thermal characterizations
papers.abstract: This study involves the extraction of the lignin from the date palm trunk biomass using natural deep eutectic solvent (NADES) followed by microwave assisted method. The extracted lignin is first alkalized and modified using anhydrous ethylenediamine and formaldehyde at different mass ratios (alkalized lignin: EDA: formaldehyde), i.e., 1:1:1.08 (M1), 1:1:3.5 (M2), and 1:1:9 (M3). Different characterization techniques such as, FTIR, XRD, TGA, DTG, DSC, XPS, SEM, SEM-EDAX, and UV-DRS are used to evaluate the influence of progressive modification. FTIR analysis exhibited that modification results in changes in the functional groups, i.e., hydroxyl, ether, and amine. SEM analysis shows morphological transformation from the rough/fractured surface of control lignin to the progressively dense and agglomerated structures of modified lignin. SEM-EDAX observed the presence of nitrogen after modification. XPS analysis showed that after modification an increased surface nitrogen is observed consistent with amination. The XRD analysis showed that all samples are amorphous in nature and controlled by broad diffuse halos. The UV-DRS study exhibited that all samples possess the broad UV absorption of lignin. The progressive changes observed in the 280–300 nm and 300–400 nm. Hence, date palm trunk lignin can be potentially valorized using EDA: formaldehyde modification to get nitrogen functionalized lignin. The potential applications of the modified lignin may be suggested in adsorbents, bio-based resin, coatings, and lignin based advanced composites are considered as possible directions assuring steadfast performance testing.

papers.title: Printable Monolayer of Binary Polymer-Co-Grafted Au Nanoparticles for Nano-Floating-Gate Transistor Memory
papers.abstract: Abstract Nano-floating-gate organic field-effect transistor (NFGOFET) memories are promising candidates for flexible, low-cost, and solution-processable nonvolatile memory devices. Their performance relies critically on the construction of a uniform nano-floating-gate/tunneling-dielectric (NFG/TD) layer, in which discrete nanoparticles serve as charge-storage sites and the surrounding polymer matrix functions as the tunneling dielectric. However, the solution processing of the upper organic semiconductor layer often causes solvent-induced erosion of polymer tunneling layers, disrupting the nanoparticle distribution and degrading charge transport and storage. Here, we report a solvent-resistant NFG/TD layer based on binary polymer-co-modified gold nanoparticles and in situ SiO2 interfacial engineering. Gold nanoparticles co-grafted with polystyrene and poly(4-vinylpyridine) form a printable monolayer in which polystyrene serves as the tunneling dielectric and poly(4-vinylpyridine) provides anchoring sites for TEOS hydrolysis. The SiO2 layer preserves the nanoparticle monolayer during active-layer printing and provides a stable inorganic tunneling barrier and a modifiable interface for improving semiconductor crystallization. This work establishes a general and scalable interfacial regulation strategy for the solution-process of printable multi-layered organic thin-film devices.

papers.title: Predictive modeling of biochar pH using pyrolysis conditions and biomass elemental composition through machine learning approaches
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of biochar pH prior to pyrolysis is critical for designing customized environmental materials, yet traditional black-box machine learning models fail to capture the complex, non-linear thermochemical mechanisms dictating alkalinity. This study aims to develop a highly accurate, mechanistically interpretable predictive framework for biochar pH by coupling ensemble machine learning algorithms with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). A comprehensive dataset of 248 diverse biomass samples was curated, utilizing initial elemental compositions and pyrolysis conditions (temperature and residence time) to train, optimize, and cross-validate seven predictive algorithms. The optimized Random Forest model significantly outperformed other architectures, demonstrating robust generalization and precision on unseen test data (R 2 of 0.703, MSE = 0.737, AARE% = 5.8%). Crucially, SHAP analysis moved beyond simple feature ranking to reveal specific directional impacts: elevated pyrolysis temperatures positively drive biochar pH by accelerating acidic functional group volatilization and concentrating basic ash minerals, whereas higher initial biomass carbon contents and prolonged residence times inversely suppress pH generation by promoting structural graphitization and reducing reactive basic sites. By translating statistical feature importance into actionable physical chemistry, this interpretable framework equips process engineers with a transparent, highly accurate tool to pre-determine and optimize biochar alkalinity without relying on exhaustive, energy-intensive experimental trials.

papers.title: Aligned graphene frameworks enabling high-thermal-conductivity phase-change thermal storage composites
papers.abstract: Phase change materials (PCMs) offer high thermal storage density, but their low intrinsic thermal conductivity limits rapid thermal charging and discharging. Incorporating thermally conductive fillers can enhance heat transfer but generally reduces latent heat capacity, creating a trade-off between thermal conductivity and energy storage density. Constructing continuous and aligned heat-transfer pathways offers a promising strategy to alleviate this trade-off by improving thermal conductivity at lower filler loadings. Graphene, with its high in-plane thermal conductivity, is an attractive building block for such pathways. However, the effective thermal conductivity of graphene-based phase change composites (PCCs) remains far lower than the theoretical value owing to multiple limiting factors. Focusing on this challenge, this review adopts an integrated multiscale analytical framework to explore how the intrinsic thermal transport potential of graphene can be more effectively utilized in aligned graphene-based PCCs. It first examines graphene’s intrinsic thermal transport properties and their influencing factors, then systematically summarizes aligned assembly strategies and introduces a loading-normalized metric for supplementary assessment of graphene utilization efficiency. Furthermore, strategies for reducing thermal resistance at intersheet junctions and graphene–matrix interfaces are discussed to address another key limitation of macroscopic thermal transport. Recent applications in energy storage and conversion and advanced thermal management are also reviewed. Finally, it highlights key challenges and future research directions for improving thermal performance, ensuring long-term reliability, and enabling scalable fabrication.

papers.title: A Binuclear Ruthenium–Phenformin Compound: Synthesis, Characterization, and Inhibition of the DHFR Enzyme
papers.abstract: Abstract The Ru-phenformin compound Ru80 was synthesized and characterized by NMR and UV/Vis spectroscopies, as well as by SCXRD, HRMS, and elemental analysis. Enzymatic assays confirm that Ru80 is effective in reducing the catalytic activity of DHFR enzyme. Ru80 retains its inhibitory activity under macromolecularly crowded conditions designed to mimic cellular environments, requiring slightly higher concentrations to achieve comparable levels of inhibition. Thermodynamic analysis demonstrates that Ru80 significantly weakens the binding affinity of NADPH cofactor to DHFR enzyme. Enzyme kinetic analysis also suggests a mixed (noncompetitive) inhibition mechanism where Ru80 binds to the free enzyme as well as the enzyme substrate complex. Ru80 binds to DHFR enzyme in a time-dependent and nonspecific manner.

papers.title: The Blessings and Curses of Carbonaceous Deposits in Ferrierite-Catalyzed Skeletal 1-Butene Isomerization
papers.abstract: Conspectus Carbonaceous deposits have long been cast as the villain in zeolite catalysis: clogging pores, poisoning active sites, and gradually strangling catalyst performance during hydrocarbon conversion. Yet in a fascinating paradox, these same “poisons” can enhance catalyst performance in several industrially important reactions through synergistic interactions with zeolite acidity. Two prominent examples stand out: methanol-to-hydrocarbon/olefin reactions (MTH/MTO) and skeletal isomerization of linear butenes to iso-butene. Understanding this counterintuitive behavior has been a challenge in zeolite catalysis for decades. Skeletal butene isomerization requires a Brønsted acidic catalyst of intermediate acid strength. Zeolites with 10-ring (10-R) windows deliver high selectivity to iso-butene while suppressing oligomerization reactions. Ferrierite (framework type FER, with perpendicularly intersecting 8-R and 10-R channels) emerged as the superior catalyst, exhibiting the highest iso-butene selectivity and remarkable resistance to deactivation. The catalytic behavior of FER presents a remarkable contradiction. Within 24 h, around 6 wt % carbonaceous deposits accumulate and reduce the accessible micropore volume by up to 98%. One would expect immediate deactivation. Instead, catalyst performance continues to improve for up to 100 h, reaching peak activity only after the pores are effectively inaccessible. Deactivation finally occurs after 100–200 h on stream. This led Guisnet and colleagues in 1995 (Guisnet, M.; et al.J. Chem. Soc., Chem. Commun.1995, 31, 1685−1686, 10.1039/c39950001685.) to propose that carbocationic deposits themselves are the active species. However, the formation mechanism, precise location, and nature of these deposits and their interaction with zeolite acidity have remained points of debate. In this Account, we describe our systematic investigation of the reaction location, reactive species, and mechanisms governing catalyst activation and deactivation. Through probe molecule adsorption, operando spectroscopy, and operando titration experiments, we demonstrate that catalysis occurs at the pore mouths, where monoaromatic carbonaceous deposits interact with internal Brønsted acid sites. Rather than functioning as classic carbocations, these deposits are presumed to act as weakly acidic “proton-on-demand” reservoirs that mediate proton transfer to reactants outside the pores. This mechanism explains why conventional Brønsted acid sites become undetectable by ex situ methods after just 2 h, yet catalytic activity not only persists but improves far beyond this point. We further reveal that catalyst deactivation stems from external carbonaceous deposits that compress the zeolite structure and block the access to pore mouths, while internal deposits cause unit cell expansion. Oxidative regeneration successfully restores activity across multiple cycles without zeolite framework degradation, and strategic incomplete regeneration retaining around 1 wt % residual coke accelerates catalyst startup. These findings establish that effective skeletal butene isomerization requires a synergy between three elements: Brønsted acidity from the zeolite framework, structural confinement at the pore mouths, and carbonaceous deposits that mediate acid-catalyzed reactions from the inside of the zeolite outward. This understanding provides a framework for rational catalyst design and regeneration strategies, with implications extending to other zeolite-catalyzed hydrocarbon transformations where “beneficial coke” plays an activating role.

We further reveal that catalyst deactivation stems from external carbonaceous deposits that compress the zeolite structure and block the access to pore mouths, while internal deposits cause unit cell expansion.

papers.title: MAGR-TCM: a knowledge graph-powered multi-agent model for intelligent home health consultation and triage in TCM gynecology
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) demonstrates distinct efficacy in managing gynecological disorders. However, accessing this specialized care in a home setting remains challenging due to the high cost of frequent hospital visits, privacy concerns, and a lack of immediate professional guidance. While general-purpose artificial intelligence offers a convenient alternative, the semantic gap between a patient's colloquial symptom descriptions and formal TCM diagnostic logic-compounded by the inherent 'hallucination' risks of large language models-prevents these tools from providing safe, actionable advice. To bridge this gap, this study proposes MAGR-TCM, an intelligent home health consultation and triage model. METHODS: Under expert supervision, a domain-specific knowledge graph was constructed, encompassing 10,231 entities and 32,051 relationships extracted from 741 high-quality clinical case records. Based on this foundation, we developed a Multi-Agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework comprising four specialized agents designed to reconstruct the complete TCM 'Disease-Pattern-Therapeutic Principle-Formula-Medicinal' reasoning chain from informal user inquiries. This collaborative architecture simulates the expert diagnostic process to generate logical, evidence-based health guidance. RESULTS: Experimental results demonstrate that MAGR-TCM significantly outperforms all baseline models on both RAGAS automatic evaluation and expert human evaluation. The model achieved 100% sensitivity and specificity on the safety test set, further validating its practical utility in home health settings and its ability to distinguish self-treatable conditions from those requiring urgent hospital care. CONCLUSIONS: By transitioning from black-box predictions to transparent, safe, and explainable reasoning logic, MAGR-TCM offers a technological paradigm for patient-centered home health management. It effectively mitigates generative hallucinations, making professional TCM expertise safely accessible for women's daily self-care and preliminary triage.

papers.title: Severe tsutsugamushi disease complicated by disseminated intravascular coagulation, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and multiple organ dysfunction: a case report
papers.abstract: Background Tsutsugamushi disease (scrub typhus), caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi and transmitted by chigger mites, classically presents with fever, eschar, and lymphadenopathy. However, cases lacking an eschar often face delayed diagnosis and can rapidly progress to severe hyperinflammatory conditions like sepsis, disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS), carrying high mortality. Case presentation A previously healthy adult male chef residing in Shenzhen, China, presented with a 10-day history of recurrent fever (peak 40.3 °C) and myalgia of the limbs and lower back. He reported unknown arthropod bites but had no typical eschar. On admission, he had thrombocytopenia (70 × 10^9/L) and elevated C-reactive protein (102.61 mg/L). He rapidly deteriorated to a platelet nadir of 33 × 10^9/L, complicated by DIC, ARDS, liver injury, and myocardial damage. Physical examination revealed a crater-like round ulcer on the left scrotum. The diagnosis was confirmed by positive O. tsutsugamushi antibodies at the Shenzhen Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and peripheral blood metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS). Treatment included doxycycline, empirical meropenem and vancomycin, low-dose dexamethasone, intravenous immunoglobulin, plasma transfusion, and comprehensive organ support. He stabilized and was discharged after 9 days. Conclusion Severe tsutsugamushi disease can trigger a hyperinflammatory response leading to DIC, ARDS, and MODS, with a rapid and fulminant course. The absence of a typical eschar is a major cause of delayed diagnosis. In patients with unexplained fever, thrombocytopenia, and multi-organ injury even without an eschar careful inspection for atypical ulcers or eschars in concealed areas such as the perineum and axillae is warranted, especially in those with a history of exposure to endemic areas or bites of unknown arthropods. Diagnosis should rely primarily on clinical features and conventional serology. For critically ill patients with negative routine tests, metagenomic NGS may be considered as a supplementary diagnostic approach. Prompt recognition and timely administration of targeted antibiotic therapy are critical for improving prognosis.

Physical examination revealed a crater-like round ulcer on the left scrotum. Prompt recognition and timely administration of targeted antibiotic therapy are critical for improving prognosis.

papers.title: Conversion of Microfibers to Cellulose Nanofibers (CNF) for High-performance 3D Printing Composites: A Review
papers.abstract: The global transition toward a circular bio-economy has positioned Cellulose Nanofibers (CNF) as a premier sustainable alternative to petroleum-based reinforcements in additive manufacturing. This review provides a comprehensive meta-analysis of the "top-down" conversion of hierarchical microfibers into individualized nanofibers and their subsequent integration into high-performance 3D printing composites. We evaluate the synergistic effects of chemical pretreatments, specifically TEMPO mediated oxidation and acetylation on fiber morphology and interfacial compatibility. Multi-instrumental screening data revealed that while mechanical disintegration alone is energy-prohibitive >20,000 kWh/t, TEMPO-oxidation facilitates the liberation of nanofibers with ultra-high aspect ratios and uniform diameters of 3-5 nm at significantly reduced energy inputs. FTIR and XRD analyses confirm the successful substitution of hydrophilic hydroxyl groups without compromising the Cellulose I crystalline core, a critical factor for dispersion in hydrophobic polymers like PLA, ABS, and PP. Furthermore, we analyze the rheological and thermal bottlenecks of 3D printing; TGA and DTA results indicate a narrowed processing window 220°C for modified CNFs, while DMA profiling demonstrates a 25–40% increase in storage modulus above the glass transition temperature (Tg), effectively extending the structural utility of bio-polymers. The review concludes by identifying the "Future Scope" of the field, highlighting the need for solvent-free grafting techniques and thermal robustification to enable the next generation of industrial-scale, bio-reinforced additive manufacturing.

papers.title: Effect of Acute Coffeeberry Extract on Self-Reported Mental Energy and Physical Performance Following a Fatiguing Cognitive Task: a Randomized, Double-Blind Controlled Trial
papers.abstract: Abstract Objectives To assess the acute effects of two doses of coffeeberry (CB®) extract use on (i) mental energy and fatigue-related feelings (primary outcomes) and (ii) cycling performance (exploratory outcome). Methods Twenty-eight adults completed a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, cross-over experiment. Treatments were a base beverage supplemented with a CB® extract at doses of 100 mg (CB®100) and 300 mg (CB®300). The base beverage alone was the placebo (PL) and the base beverage with 75 mg caffeine (CAFF) was the positive control. Participants consumed one of the four beverages during four separate visits. Before (BL) and one-hour post-treatment (Post 1), cognitive tests and scales assessing the mood states of alertness, energy and fatigue were completed, taking 55-min. Two-hours post-treatment, a 20-min-high intensity interval cycling protocol was performed followed by a 3-min all-out time trial. Treatment effects on primary outcomes were tested using repeated measures ANOVAs. Cycling performance outcomes were tested using dependent t-tests. Results There was a significant Beverage x Time interaction for alertness ( p = 0.008), mental energy ( p = 0.009), and mental fatigue ( p = 0.008). Post-hoc analysis showed significant improvements from BL to Post 1 in the CAFF condition for alertness ( p = 0.002); and mental energy ( p = 0.006). Conclusions Beverages containing 100 mg or 300 mg CB® extract consumed one-hour before a cognitive test and two-hours before a high intensity exercise bout does not influence feelings of alertness, mental energy and fatigue or cycling performance. A 75 mg dose of caffeine transiently improves feelings of alertness and mental energy. Trial Registration The trial is registered at the US National Institutes of Health (ClinicalTrials.gov) #NCT03870126. Presented at the American Society of Nutrition, 2021.

papers.title: Magnetic GO@AlFe2O4@SO3H nanocatalyst: a sustainable approach for the synthesis of 5-phenyl-1,3,4-thiadiazol-2-amines
papers.abstract: A novel magnetic nanocatalyst, denoted as GO@AlFe 2 O 4 @SO 3 H, has been successfully designed and applied as an efficient and sustainable heterogeneous catalyst for the synthesis of 5-phenyl-1,3,4-thiadiazol-2-amines. This one-pot methodology involves the direct cyclocondensation reaction of readily available benzoic acid derivatives with thiosemicarbazide, employing phosphorus oxychloride (POCl 3 ) as a cyclodehydrating agent. Remarkably, the reaction proceeds smoothly in water as a green solvent at a mild temperature of 50 °C, completing within 30 min. The protocol demonstrates excellent substrate generality, affording a diverse library of 19 target heterocyclic compounds in consistently high yields ranging from 87% to 96%. The robust GO@AlFe 2 O 4 @SO 3 H nanocomposite, which integrates the high surface area of functionalized graphene oxide (GO) with the superparamagnetic properties of aluminium-doped iron oxide (AlFe 2 O 4 ) and Brønsted-acidic sulfonic sites (-SO 3 H), facilitates straightforward magnetic separation from the reaction mixture. This feature underpins the catalyst’s exceptional reusability, as it could be recovered and successively reused for up to seven consecutive cycles without a significant loss in its catalytic performance. The presented work underscores a sustainable, rapid, and practical approach for accessing biologically relevant 1,3,4-thiadiazole frameworks, highlighting the advantages of magnetically recoverable nanocatalyst in promoting sustainable synthetic methodologies.

papers.title: The Substrate Effect: Rice Husk Versus Cotton Gin Trash in Mycelium-Based Composite Production
papers.abstract: Mycelium-based composites (MBCs) are emerging as low-carbon materials for converting agricultural residues into construction-oriented panels. However, the specific role of substrate selection remains difficult to define because fungal species, nutrient systems, and processing conditions often vary between studies. Here, rice husk and cotton gin trash were directly compared as locally available Australian feedstocks for heat-pressed MBC panels under the same cultivation and fabrication framework. Four white-rot fungal isolates, Amauroderma sp., Ganoderma sp., Pycnoporus coccineus, and Trametes hirsuta, were cultivated with wheat grains as a nutrient supplement, enabling the substrate effect to be isolated more clearly. The panels were assessed through density measurements, microstructural imaging, tensile, compressive and flexural testing, and thermal characterisation by TGA and DSC. Rice-husk panels formed denser, more compact board-like structures, with densities of approximately 250–259 kg m−3, supporting their potential for compact, non-load-bearing interior panel applications. Cotton gin trash panels were lighter, with densities of approximately 138–149 kg m−3 but showed improved deformation tolerance and strong flexural performance in selected panels. Mechanically, CGT-based panels reached peak tensile, compressive, and flexural stresses of approximately 0.70, 0.90, and 3.04 MPa, respectively, compared with maxima of approximately 0.35, 0.80, and 1.31 MPa for the corresponding RH-based panels. Thermal analysis further confirmed substrate-dependent behaviour. This study demonstrates that substrate choice can be used as a practical design tool to tailor MBC panels for either compact board-like products or lightweight functional panel systems.

papers.title: Could dexmedetomidine-induced immunogenic cell death sensitize EBV-driven nasopharyngeal carcinoma to PD-1 blockade? A preclinical hypothesis and falsification framework
papers.abstract: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is an Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-driven epithelial malignancy characterized by persistent viral antigens but inefficient antigen presentation, dysfunctional dendritic cells, and exhausted T cells. Although programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) blockade has improved clinical outcomes, many patients do not achieve durable benefit. Dexmedetomidine (DEX) is an alpha2-adrenoceptor agonist used for sedation that was recently reported in a single preclinical study to induce immunogenic cell death (ICD) through partial endoplasmic reticulum stress, eIF2α phosphorylation, autophagy, surface calreticulin exposure, and HMGB1 and ATP release, effects that enhanced dendritic-cell uptake and cooperated with PD-1 blockade in non-NPC tumor models. This phenotype requires approximately 600 μM DEX, several orders of magnitude above the concentration range in which DEX engages the alpha2-adrenoceptor selectively, so the effect more likely reflects an off-target interaction than canonical receptor pharmacology. We propose that, if independently reproduced in EBV-positive NPC and traced to a defined molecular target, this phenomenon could enhance cross-presentation of EBV antigens and prime EBV-specific CD8+ T cells, providing an immunological rationale for combination with PD-1 blockade. This hypothesis is constrained by the exposure gap, the absence of independent or NPC-specific validation, context-dependent tumor-promoting and immunosuppressive effects, a DEX-associated T-cell exhaustion signature, and the unresolved identity of the responsible target. We therefore do not advocate systemic dose escalation or immediate interventional testing. Instead, we present a staged falsification framework requiring independent confirmation of canonical ICD, spatially resolved demonstration of antigen-specific cross-presentation and stromal T-cell infiltration, deconvolution of the molecular target through thermal proteomics and CRISPR-based screening, and exclusion of hemodynamic, metastatic, and immunosuppressive liabilities before efficacy testing in EBV-relevant models. Only if these criteria are satisfied should localized delivery, target-directed inducer design, or prospective clinical evaluation be considered. This Perspective repositions DEX as a phenotypic probe for target discovery rather than a repurposed receptor agonist or an established anticancer therapy.
