papers.title: Jute yarn with surfaces modified by eco-friendly deposition of carbon nanotubes: mechanical, physical, thermal, and flame-retardant properties
papers.abstract: Abstract The use of natural fibres has expanded in applications such as polymer composites, automotive components, and the aerospace industry. Among them, jute fibre (JF) stands out because of its commercial availability, low cost, and low density, despite limitations such as its insulating behaviour and flammability. To address these drawbacks, nanoparticles can be deposited via electrophoresis. In this work, carbon nanotubes (CNTs) were deposited onto JF using a modified electrophoretic deposition technique, recently termed High-Impulse Electrophoretic Deposition (HIEPD), which is suitable for aqueous suspensions and insulating materials. This method does not require solvents, enabling a one-pot, eco-friendly approach. The characterisation of JF included the evaluation of mechanical, electrical, thermal, and flammability properties. Optical microscopy confirmed CNT deposition, although aggregates were observed on the fibre surface. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) showed an increase in final residue from 4 % (commercial fibre) to 12 % (10 min) and 22 % (20 min), indicating that treatment time affected CNT loading. A reduction in degradation onset temperature suggested catalytic effects associated with CNTs. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy indicated that conductivity was up to five orders of magnitude higher in fibres treated for 20 min than in untreated fibres. Mechanical tests did not show statistically significant differences, with tensile strengths remaining above 50 MPa. Flame tests indicated improved flame-retardant behaviour, reducing after-flame time from 27 s to 7 s and afterglow time from 8 min to 2 min. The obtained results suggest that CNT deposition onto the JF surface, forming a conductive and protective coating, enhances both the electrical conductivity and flame-retardant performance of the fibres.

papers.title: Consistency-regularized graph-tabular evidence fusion for cold-start drug-drug interaction prioritization
papers.abstract: Background Drug-drug interactions (DDIs) remain difficult to prioritize for new, rarely prescribed, or poorly characterized drugs because interaction evidence is sparse and conventional random pair splits can overestimate generalization. Objective This study evaluated whether a consistency-regularized heterogeneous graph-tabular model can improve cold-start DDI prioritiza-tion under a strict drug-disjoint protocol. Methods We constructed RxPairEvid, a multi-source evidence resource that links curated drug knowledge, drug-protein-pathway relations, protein interaction context, side-effect resources, transcriptomic perturbation evidence, and spontaneous-report safety signals. RxDDI-ConsisGAT encodes mechanistic context with relation-aware GATv2 layers, encodes pairwise evidence through a tabular pathway, and fuses both views for binary interaction scoring. Training uses two stochastic forward passes with independent dropout masks and penalizes probability disagreement alongside label-smoothed binary classification loss. Results On held-out cold-start testing, RxDDI-ConsisGAT achieved AUROC = 0.8352 and AUPRC = 0.6910. Same-protocol baselines and ablations showed lower test AUROC for the no-consistency model (0.8255), tabular-only model (0.7734), graph-only model (0.7163), HeteroSAGE-fusion model (0.7318), logistic regression (0.7597), and HistGradientBoosting (0.7803). Diagnostic analyses showed useful score separation, broadly reasonable calibration, and interpretable evidence patterns. Conclusion The findings support graph-tabular evidence fusion as a practical strategy for expert-facing cold-start DDI triage, while prospective validation and threshold calibration remain necessary before clinical deployment.

papers.title: Multifunctional PMMA144- b -PDMAEMA51/TiO2 Nanocomposites for Efficient Dye Removal and Antibacterial Applications: Experimental and DFT Insights
papers.abstract: Abstract In this study, poly(methyl methacrylate)-b-poly(2-(dimethylamino)ethyl methacrylate) (PMMA-b-PDMAEMA), an amphiphilic block copolymer containing various chain lengths of a pH- and temperature-responsive PDMAEMA segment, was synthesized via atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP). A PMMA-Br macroinitiator was first prepared by polymerization of methyl methacrylate using butyl 2-bromoisobutyrate (BuBriB) and a CuBr/2,2′-bipyridine catalytic system, and then the chain was extended with further batch polymerization of DMAEMA using the PMMA-Br macroinitiator. TiO2 nanoparticles were synthesized by the sol–gel method, and they were incorporated into the block copolymer through solvent casting to obtain PMMA-b-PDMAEMA/TiO2 nanocomposites. The synthesized copolymers and nanocomposites were comprehensively characterized by GPC, FTIR, 1H NMR, TGA, DSC, SEM, and XRD. The polymer nanocomposite containing 10% TiO2 achieved over 96% removal of methylene blue (MB) within 70 min at pH 7 under visible LED irradiation in the presence of NaBH4. In addition, it exhibited significant antibacterial activity, producing inhibition zones of 24.75 mm against Shigella sonnei (S. sonnei) and 23.25 mm against Staphylococcus hemolyticus(S. hemolyticus) at a dose of 45 μg. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further elucidated the interactions between TiO2 nanoparticles and PMMA-b-PDMAEMA, the adsorption mechanism of methylene blue, and the interactions of the nanocomposites with bacterial cell proteins. These findings demonstrated that PMMA-b-PDMAEMA/TiO2 nanocomposites are promising multifunctional materials for environmental remediation by combining efficient dye adsorption with antibacterial activity. The novelty of this work lies in the development of a multifunctional PMMA-b-PDMAEMA/TiO2 nanocomposite that combines the mechanical stability, pH-responsive behavior, dye adsorption, and antibacterial properties of the prepared nanocomposites on a single platform for environmental remediation.

papers.title: Influence of rising groundwater levels on the mechanical and deformation characteristics of bridge pile foundations in land subsidence areas
papers.abstract: Long-term groundwater overexploitation has induced severe land subsidence in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region, while groundwater level rise associated with the South-to-North Water Diversion Project and increased precipitation under climate warming have promoted groundwater level recovery. Rising groundwater levels may alter the hydro-mechanical behavior of thick soft soil and affect the safety of bridge pile foundations in subsidence areas. Taking the bridge pile foundation of the Xiong’an–Daxing rail transit project as an example, this study uses the finite difference method to investigate pile–soil stress and deformation responses under groundwater level rise. A moisture-content-dependent Burgers creep model is established to characterize soil creep and pile–soil interaction. The effects of groundwater level rise induced by groundwater recharge and rainfall on pile foundation deformation, bearing capacity, pore water pressure, and soil settlement are analyzed. The results show that the proposed model captures the staged evolution of soil settlement and that pile bearing capacity responds nonlinearly to groundwater level rise. The findings provide a reference for evaluating the safety of bridge pile foundations and related infrastructure under groundwater level recovery in land subsidence areas.

papers.title: A magnetically recoverable, fluorescence-tracked, molecularly imprinted nanocarrier for controlled bortezomib release
papers.abstract: Abstract Background A dual fluorescent-magnetic molecularly imprinted nanocomposite (FMMIP-BTZ) was synthesized by coating Fe₃O₄ nanoparticles with silica and fluorescein-5-isothiocyanate, followed by in-situ polydopamine polymerization using bortezomib (BTZ) as template. Methods The prepared nanocomposite was characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), vibrating sample magnetometry (VSM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), fourier transform infrared (FTIR), UV-visible and fluorescence analysis. Results Template-selective recognition was confirmed by an imprinting factor of 3.20 (85.34 mg g⁻¹ for FMMIP versus 26.67 mg g⁻¹ for the non-imprinted control), with a BTZ loading efficiency of 69.3%. Release followed zero-order kinetics (k₀ = 3.276% h⁻¹, R² = 0.9937), reaching 80.5 ± 1% cumulative release, and was pH-responsive, rising from 41.1% at pH 7.4 to 84.5% at pH 4 over 6 h. Saturation magnetization fell from 0.48 to 0.04 emu g⁻¹ as the non-magnetic shell was added; despite this, particles remained separable under an external magnetic field at every synthesis, washing, and release step. Dual fluorescence from released BTZ and the FITC-labelled core enabled spectroscopic tracking of release. In an acute dermal irritation assessment, FMMIP-BTZ produced a mean erythema score of 1.00 at 24 h compared with 3.00 for the control. Molecular docking against COX-2, PRDX5, EGFR, and AKT1, together with a 100-ns MD simulation of the AKT1–bortezomib complex, provided exploratory mechanistic context for the experimentally observed response. Conclusion FMMIP-BTZ is thus a molecularly selective, magnetically separable, fluorescence-trackable platform with controlled, pH-responsive release; cellular uptake, cytotoxicity, and in vivo antitumour efficacy remain to be established.

papers.title: Combustion Characteristics and Kinetics of Coke in O2/CO2 Atmosphere under Varying Oxygen Concentration
papers.abstract: To clarify the effect of oxygen concentration on coke combustion in an O2/CO2 atmosphere, non-isothermal thermogravimetric experiments were conducted at 20%, 40%, and 60% O2 with heating rates of 5, 10, and 20°C·min−1. Combustion characteristic parameters and the flammability, burnout, and comprehensive combustion indices were determined, and the reaction mechanism and kinetic parameters were evaluated by the Z(α) master plot method combined with FWO and KAS model-free methods. Raising the oxygen concentration shifted the TG-DTG and DSC curves toward lower temperatures and increased combustion intensity. At 20 °C·min−1, increasing O2 from 20% to 60% decreased the burnout temperature by 130.02°C and increased the maximum mass loss rate by 76.7%. The optimal combustion performance was obtained at 60% O2 and 5°C·min−1. The Z(α) master plot method revealed a three-stage kinetic mechanism: R3 phase-boundary control, F2/F3 reaction, and D3 three-dimensional diffusion. The FWO method yielded average activation energies of 75.56, 93.29, and 98.62 kJ·mol−1, while the KAS method gave 63.48, 86.00, and 89.27 kJ·mol−1. These values generally decreased with increasing conversion, with the exception of a local increase at α = 0.6 for the 40% O2 atmosphere. papers.title: Optimized garlic essential oil-based nanostructured lipid carriers as anti - Gammacoronavirus galli agent
papers.journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology
papers.abstract: Introduction Gammacoronavirus galli is a pathogenic avian coronavirus that causes huge economic losses in the poultry industry worldwide. The continuous emergence of viral variants challenges existing control strategies and highlights the need for novel and complementary antiviral approaches. This work reported the development of nanostructured lipid carriers (NLC) loaded with garlic essential oil (EO) as a potential antiviral strategy. Methods The chemical composition of the garlic EO was elucidated, revealing a predominance of organosulfur compounds. Different NLC systems composed of ucuuba butter, copaiba oil, garlic EO and stabilized by a surfactant were optimized using a 2 4 factorial design. The optimized formulations were monitored in the physicochemical stability study, in terms of particle size, polydispersity index and Zeta potential, for 6 months (25 °C), as well as the thermal cycling stability. The most promising system and its excipients were structurally characterized through experimental methodologies (FTIR-ATR, DSC and FESEM). Cytotoxicity was assessed in VERO cells, nanotoxicity in a chicken embryo (CE) model and antiviral efficacy in cell lineages infected with Gammacoronavirus galli . Results and Discussion Such systems proved to be stable up to 180 days at room temperature, with excellent structural properties and biocompatibility. The results indicated that the NLC formulation preserved the biological activity of garlic EO and demonstrated antiviral activity against G. galli . The nanotechnological strategy proposed here described the development of biocompatible and efficient formulations against G. galli , providing promising candidates to be subjected to further preclinical assays against enveloped viruses.

papers.title: Multiprotocol Rheological Characterization of the Order–Disorder Thermal Transition in a Xanthan Gum Solution
papers.abstract: Abstract Xanthan gum (XG) forms weak-gel aqueous dispersions whose solid-like elasticity is progressively lost on heating through a helix-to-coil (order–disorder) transition. How far that transition reaches into the nonlinear and time-dependent mechanical response remains not fully characterized. A 0.5% (w/v) XG solution was characterized from 10 to 60 °C by steady shear, strain-amplitude and frequency sweeps, step-strain relaxation, creep–recovery, and large-amplitude oscillatory shear (LAOS), and by 1H NMR spectroscopy. A common broken-line criterion applied to 33 descriptors across seven data sets, 28 of which were resolvable, gave an average breakpoint temperature of 32.4 ± 1.7 °C. LAOS revealed strain-dependent weakening of the intracycle nonlinearities (strain stiffening/softening, shear thickening/thinning) upon heating. The dissipation ratio ϕ increased with temperature within the linear regime, but the dependence reversed and was much weaker at large strain amplitudes. The weak Type III G″ overshoot attenuated roughly 8-fold on heating, so the amplitude-sweep response approached Type I strain thinning.

papers.title: EVALUATING THERMAL STABILITY AND FIRE RESISTANCE OF NANOFILLER REINFORCED POLYMER COMPOSITES FOR ADVANCED ENGINEERING APPLICATIONS
papers.journal: International Journal of Engineering Technology Research & Management
papers.abstract: Polymer composites support lightweight engineering across transport, construction, electronics and energysystems, but thermal degradation and flammability constrain their use in demanding environments. Nanofillerreinforcement offers opportunities to modify heat transfer, decomposition behaviour and protective charformation, although performance depends on filler chemistry, dispersion, loading and interactions with thepolymer matrix. This study proposes a comparative evaluation of thermal stability and fire resistance in nanofillerreinforced polymer composites for advanced engineering applications. Unfilled polymers and reinforcedformulations are compared using thermogravimetric analysis, differential scanning calorimetry, flammabilitytesting and cone calorimetry. Key indicators include decomposition temperatures, residual char, ignition time, heatrelease, smoke production and mechanical property retention. Microscopy and chemical characterisation examinedispersion, interfacial behaviour and degradation mechanisms. The analysis considers processing conditions,specimen geometry and testing variability to distinguish reproducible improvements from formulation dependenteffects. Particular attention addresses trade-offs involving processability, strength, smoke generation and materialcost. The proposed evaluation provides a basis for selecting promising formulations while recognising thatlaboratory performance requires application specific validation before claims concerning component safety,durability or regulatory compliance are justified under service conditions.

papers.title: Digital mental health interventions for university students during the COVID-19 pandemic and post-pandemic periods: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
papers.abstract: Background University students experience elevated levels of anxiety, depression, and stress, prompting growing interest in accessible digital psychological interventions. This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the effectiveness of digital psychological interventions for university students during the later stages of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic and the post-pandemic periods. Methods PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science (WoS), and Cochrane were searched for randomized controlled trials involving university students published between 2020 and June 2026. Random-effects models (Hedges’ g, modified Knapp-Hartung [mKH]) were applied, and Risk of Bias was assessed with Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2). Results A total of 34 trials (6,544 students, 15 countries) were included. Benefits were significant for depression at 8 weeks (g = 0.48), anxiety at 2 and 8 weeks (g = 0.24 and g = 0.57), stress at 4 weeks (g = 0.23), and post-intervention anxiety (g = 0.75; I 2 = 88.6%), but not for pooled anxiety. Overall, 52.9% of studies were at high Risk of Bias, and only one of six active-comparator trials compared digital with face-to-face delivery. Conclusion Digital interventions yield modest short-term benefits, but heterogeneity, high Risk of Bias, and a scarcity of face-to-face comparisons limit confidence. Systematic review registration http://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/E2C78 , identifier (E2C78).

papers.title: Permanent prophylactic mesh reinforcement in elective and emergency midline laparotomy: a registry-based comparative analysis
papers.abstract: Background Prophylactic mesh reinforcement reduces the incidence of incisional hernia (IH) after midline laparotomy and is recommended for high-risk patients. However, concerns regarding contamination, mesh infection, and prosthetic-related morbidity have limited its implementation in emergency surgery. Whether emergency indication is associated with worse outcomes among mesh-treated patients remains uncertain. Methods A retrospective registry-based cohort study used data from the Spanish National Incisional Hernia Registry (EVEREG) from 2020 to 2025 (17 hospitals). Adults undergoing midline laparotomy with permanent prophylactic mesh reinforcement were stratified by elective or emergency indication. In-hospital outcomes included overall and general complications (cardiac, respiratory or renal failure), surgical-site occurrence (SSO), mesh infection, mesh removal, abdominal complications during the index stay and mortality at 30 days. Analyses used 204 patients with completed in-hospital data and clinically specified multivariable logistic regression models. Results The registered cohort included 234 patients: 104 elective and 130 emergency procedures. Among 204 patients with completed in-hospital modules (85 elective, 119 emergency), overall complications occurred in 38.8% versus 62.2% and general complications in 21.2% versus 48.7%, respectively; both remained significant after multiplicity correction. No statistically detectable differences were observed in SSO, mesh infection, mesh removal, abdominal complications or mortality (10.6% versus 11.8%). Recorded Clavien–Dindo categories were higher after emergency surgery (P = 0.006). After adjustment, emergency indication was associated with general complications (OR 2.13, 95% CI 1.01–4.47), but not mortality (OR 1.00, 95% CI 0.39–2.57). Renal disease and contamination were associated with overall complications, and contamination with abdominal complications. Older age and higher body mass index (BMI) were associated with mortality (BMI: OR 1.64 per 5 kg/m 2 , 95% CI 1.06–2.53). Conclusion In this selected registry cohort, emergency indication was associated with greater early general morbidity, whereas no statistically detectable increase in short-term wound- or mesh-related events was observed, with considerable uncertainty. As a cautious implication requiring confirmation, emergency indication per se might not be an absolute contraindication to prophylactic mesh in selected patients. The small number of mesh-related events, the absence of a non-mesh control group and the loss to follow-up preclude conclusions on equivalent safety or effectiveness in preventing incisional hernia.

papers.title: CaCO3-Filled Polypropylene Block Copolymer Composites: Strain-Rate-Dependent Tensile Behavior, Bergström–Boyce Calibration, Parameter Identifiability, and Creep and Stress-Relaxation Prediction
papers.abstract: Finite element analysis predicts the response of filled polymers only when the constitutive model suits the material and its parameters are reliably identified. This study evaluates the applicability and limits of the Bergström–Boyce (BB) model for calcium carbonate (CaCO3)-filled polypropylene block copolymer (PPB). Neat PPB and composites with 10, 20, and 30 vol% CaCO3 are tested in uniaxial tension at five strain rates and characterized by dynamic mechanical analysis and differential scanning calorimetry. The BB parameters are identified by a multi-start evolution strategy with trust-region refinement, and their identifiability is assessed by sensitivity, Fisher-information, profile, and multi-start analyses. The filler raises Young’s modulus from 1523 to 3716 MPa while reducing ductility and rate sensitivity. The model reproduces the tensile response with R2 = 0.94–0.99 in calibration and 0.96–0.99 at the two withheld strain rates, whereas the viscous-network locking stretch is unidentifiable. Without refitting, the parameters predict the stress relaxed in 1 h within a median factor of 1.3. Predicted creep, however, inherits the stress exponent of the flow rule and approaches the measurements only near 11–17 MPa. Identifiability established in tension is thus local to the calibration conditions; sustained loading requires creep or relaxation data at the service stress.

Identifiability established in tension is thus local to the calibration conditions; sustained loading requires creep or relaxation data at the service stress.

papers.title: Status and perspective on mechanical and protective properties of PVD MeSiN nitride nanocomposite coatings
papers.abstract: MeSiN nanocomposite coatings have attracted growing interest due to their exceptional combination of high hardness, wear, and corrosion resistance. However, existing studies still lack a comprehensive analysis of their microstructural characteristics, performance metrics, and optimization strategies. This review critically examines recent advances in the fabrication techniques, structure–property relationships, and potential optimization strategies of MeSiN coatings. Depending on the silicon content, MeSiN systems exhibit three structural regimes: solid solution, nanocomposite, and amorphous structure. Among them, the nanocomposite configuration, comprising nanocrystalline MeN grains embedded within an amorphous SiN x matrix, offers the most balanced improvement in mechanical strength and environmental resistance (hardness 20 ~ 40 GPa, oxidation temperature 900 ~ 1000 °C). The effects of Si and the Si-based coating structure in mechanical strengthening as well as corrosion and oxidation protection are discussed in detail. Furthermore, optimization perspectives are proposed. Multicomponent coating and multilayer architecture collectively enhance thermal stability, mechanical strengthening, and corrosion performance. Remaining challenges include limited understanding of degradation mechanisms under complex service conditions, the need for improved interface engineering, and the implementation of data-driven design strategies. This study offers insights into the development of next-generation MeSiN coatings for extreme environments in aerospace, marine, and manufacturing applications.

papers.title: Manipulating Plasticity and Conductivity of Composite Polymer Electrolytes with a ZrO2 Ceramic Filler for Improving the Performance of Sodium Batteries
papers.abstract: Abstract Although sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are touted as cheaper than lithium-ion batteries, their commercial adoption is hindered by interfacial instability, dendrite formation, and safety concerns arising from flammable liquid electrolytes. To counter these issues, in this study, a composite polymer electrolyte (CPE) was developed comprising poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (P(VDF-HFP)), poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO), sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF6) salt, succinonitrile, and zirconium dioxide (ZrO2) via a simple solution casting method. The optimized CPE with 2.5 wt % ZrO2 (CPE-2.5) enhanced the amorphous nature of the matrix, porosity, voltage stability of the electrolyte, ionic conductivity (manipulating the Na+ ion transference number), and elasticity–plasticity balance. ZrO2 acted like a bridge between NaPF6 salt and the PEO matrix, establishing a Na+-conducting porous path when filled with a liquid electrolyte. The CPE-2.5 exhibited a high ionic conductivity of 1.26 ± 0.04 × 10–3 S cm–1, excellent electrochemical stability up to 4.96 V vs Na/Na+, and strong mechanical stability (tensile strength of ∼10.55 MPa). Direct evidence for the interaction of Lewis acid Zr4+ centers with PF6– was provided by differential scanning calorimetry. This interaction enhanced the matrix conductivity, preventing ion-pairing. The CPE-2.5 exhibited optimal porosity (22%) to retain the electrolyte and balanced plasticity and elasticity to accommodate volume change during 2000 h plating/stripping of Na and low polarization (∼100 mV). The Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 half-cell delivers a capacity of 107.5 mAh g–1 with 95% retention over 200 cycles. This work highlights ZrO2-induced manipulation of porosity, conductivity, and plasticity as a strategy for durable solid-state SIBs.

papers.title: A human-specific TAF8 isoform diversifies the composition of the TFIID general transcription factor
papers.abstract: Despite its central role in RNA polymerase II transcription, the composition and function of the TFIID general transcription factor can vary across tissues and developmental stages. Such variability may provide a substrate for evolutionary innovation and contribute to human-specific regulatory functions. Here, we identify a human-specific short isoform of TAF8 (TAF8s), a scaffold subunit of TFIID, generated through the use of an intronic polyadenylation site (iPAS). Comparative genomic analyses reveal that the genomic substrate for this isoform originated with the insertion of a FLAM-C Alu element into intron 5 in the common ancestor of anthropoid primates (Simiiformes), whereas subsequent small sequence changes at the Alu-associated iPAS coincide with the emergence of TAF8s expression in the human lineage. TAF8s lacks nearly half of the canonical TAF8 coding sequence, is widely expressed across human tissues, and accounts for a substantial fraction of TAF8 transcripts. It encodes a truncated protein lacking the canonical nuclear-localization signal and localizes predominantly to the cytoplasm. Despite retaining interactions with its histone-fold partner TAF10 and other core TFIID subunits, TAF8s loses interaction with TAF2, providing a molecular basis for alternative TFIID sub-complex formation. Together, our findings identify a recently evolved human-specific regulatory innovation at the TAF8 locus that diversifies the composition of a conserved general transcription factor. This example illustrates how evolution of transcript isoforms can generate new protein interactions and molecular complexity in essential cellular machineries, with potential implications for the functional diversification of TAF-containing complexes and the genetic basis of TAF-related developmental disorders.

papers.title: Crystal-field modulation activates dormant tetrahedral Co sites for efficient alkaline hydrogen evolution
papers.abstract: Water activation in the Volmer step is a major kinetic bottleneck in alkaline hydrogen evolution, yet the catalytic potential of many lattice sites remains underutilized. Here, we develop an oxalic-acid-assisted treatment to modulate the surface coordination environment of spinel Co 3 O 4 while preserving its crystalline framework. The optimized U-Co 3 O 4 -2 electrode requires an overpotential of 38 mV to reach 10 mA cm −2 in 1.0 M KOH and sustains operation for at least 1000 h. Density functional theory indicates that coordination unsaturation reconstructs the local crystal field and selectively lowers dz 2 occupation at tetrahedral Co sites. The resulting orbital redistribution reduces the population of Co-H 2 O antibonding states, strengthens Co-H 2 O coupling, and makes dissociative water activation thermodynamically more favorable. Thus, tetrahedral Co sites that are weakly active in pristine Co 3 O 4 can be converted into catalytically competent water-activation centers. These results identify coordination-induced crystal-field modulation as a strategy for increasing lattice-site utilization in non-noble-metal alkaline HER catalysts.

These results identify coordination-induced crystal-field modulation as a strategy for increasing lattice-site utilization in non-noble-metal alkaline HER catalysts.

papers.title: ESCRT-III homolog PspA shapes membrane architecture and multicellularity in magnetoglobule bacteria
papers.abstract: Abstract Endosomal Sorting Complex Required for Transport (ESCRT)-III proteins are crucial for membrane remodeling and repair across all domains of life. Eukaryotic ESCRT-III and cyanobacterial homologs such as Phage shock protein A (PspA) and Vipp1/Imm30 remodel membranes into diverse structures, including vesicles, rings, filaments, tubular rods, and multivesicular bodies (MVBs). Here, our microscopy analysis reveals that multicellular magnetoglobules possess elaborate compartments, including magnetosome organelles, polyphosphate granules, and various membrane structures, such as vesicles, rings, tubular rods, filaments, and MVB-like formations. This complexity suggested that membrane-remodeling PspA might be essential for their compartmentalization, morphogenesis, and the evolution of multicellularity. We generated nine magnetoglobule genomes, uncovering significant expansion relative to unicellular magnetotactic bacteria. Phylogenetic analysis implied that multicellular magnetoglobules might share a common ancestor with unicellular magnetotactic bacteria and undergone differentiation, forming two morphologies. Furthermore, PspA was ubiquitous in magnetoglobules, forming a distinct clade within bacterial and archaeal ESCRT-III phylogeny. All phylogenetic evidence suggested their evolution from a unicellular ancestor within the phylum Desulfobacterota. Heterologous expression of magnetoglobule pspA2 in Escherichia coli resulted in PspA2 localized at the poles in rod-shaped unicells and with a dispersed distribution in filamentous cells. Cryo-electron tomography of PspA2-expressing cells revealed filament bundles, membrane sacculi, vesicles, and MVB-like structures. Furthermore, electron-dense foci, mirroring the PspA2 distribution in filamentous cells, altered the inward orientation of the septum, potentially interfering with cell division. Collectively, these results demonstrate the membrane-remodeling function of magnetoglobule PspA proteins and suggest that they may contribute to the morphogenesis and evolution of multicellularity in magnetotactic bacteria.

papers.title: The more the merrier? systematic review and meta-analysis of working memory and category learning
papers.abstract: The role of working memory capacity (WMC) in category learning (CL) remains theoretically contested. While the COVIS model posits that information-integration (II) learning is WMC-independent, empirical findings are mixed. Through a systematic review and subsequent three-level meta-analysis of 21 articles (164 effect sizes), we synthesized the WMC–CL relationship. Results revealed a significant overall positive correlation (r = 0.258; trim-and-fill adjusted r = 0.118). Notably, category structure (rule-based vs. information-integration) did not significantly moderate this relationship, challenging the COVIS prediction that implicit learning is independent of WMC. However, WMC task-specific moderation revealed significantly weaker correlations for reading span compared to operation span, memory updating, and spatial storage. No moderating effects were found for age, gender, or stimulus modality. These findings suggest that performance across diverse category structures shares a common reliance on WMC.

Results revealed a significant overall positive correlation (r = 0.258; trim-and-fill adjusted r = 0.118). These findings suggest that performance across diverse category structures shares a common reliance on WMC.

papers.title: Generating the dark matter mass from the QCD vacuum: a new approach to the mass aspect of the dark matter–baryon coincidence problem
papers.abstract: Abstract The comparable abundances of dark matter and baryons imply a deep connection between the dark sector and the QCD sector. In asymmetric dark matter models, the number densities of both sectors are ensured to be similar. However, a complete solution should also include a mechanism relating their masses. In this study, we explore a new mechanism where an $$\mathcal {O}(\Lambda _\textrm{QCD})$$ O ( Λ QCD ) dark matter mass arises from the QCD vacuum. The idea is realized by a strongly coupled chiral dark sector, featuring a light composite fermion as the dark matter. Its mass is generated through the vacuum misalignment induced by QCD, ensuring the mass to be comparable with baryons. The model also features additional light bosons, including GeV-scale dark pions and a composite QCD axion.

papers.title: Scientific exploration outlasts industrial momentum and sustains innovation in genetic research: survey of 20 million papers and patents
papers.abstract: Long-term innovation depends not only on discovering new elements but also on facilitating new recombination at the time of their co-availability. This notion of combinatorial innovation raises the question about whether scientific exploration and industry research persist over similar time horizons to meet innovative opportunities. Here, we analyze about 20 million papers and US, Chinese, and European patents to compare the courses of scientific and industrial activities in genetic research, a domain of far-reaching societal importance. We observe that research on new genes has declined since the early 2000s, but the exploration of novel gene combinations remains active for biotechnology innovation. Yet, fields of highly practical or commercial focus are less likely to test novel gene combinations. Furthermore, industry R&D on each gene tends to decline earlier than scientific interest in that gene. After this decline of the industrial momentum, continuous scientific research still sustains exploratory and innovative opportunities, involving novel gene combinations, clinical trials, and technologically-impactful work. Based on a hypothetical scenario of over-aligned science and industry, we estimate that up to 42.2–74.4% of the combinational opportunities would be unexplored if scientific research becomes hindered due to industry’s retreat. This study suggests the potential complementary roles of scientific and industrial research with different temporal modes in innovation cycles, calling for balanced policies to foster innovation ecosystems.

papers.title: Bio-inspired mineralization of CO2 to nanoscaled hydrozincite mediated via Zea mays saccharata
papers.abstract: Abstract The bio-inspired mineralization of CO 2 to single-phase Hydrozincite Zn 5 (CO 3 ) 2 (OH) 6 was demonstrated for the first time in this contribution utilising aqueous extracts of Zea mays saccharata (ZMS). The latter has been a successful chelating and capping agent. Under ambient circumstances (room temperature & atmospheric pressure), this novel method produced single-phase crystalline hydrozincite Zn 5 (CO 3 ) 2 (OH) 6 with an average crystallite size of 38.5 nm. The UV–VIS–DRS, PL, FT-IR, XRD, and SEM–EDS studies sustained the potential of the bio-engineered nanoscaled Hydrozincite Zn 5 (CO 3 ) 2 (OH) 6 as a highly reflective material (Diffuse reflectance > 95%) and an effective blue luminescence (λ MaxEmission ≈ 457.3 nm). Electrochemical properties were investigated in 1 M NaOH electrolyte using cyclic voltammetry (CV) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). CV studies demonstrated a significant increase in current response with distinct Faradaic peaks at + 0.07 V, + 0.18 V, and − 0.16 V (vs. Ag|AgCl), confirming the inherent electrochemical activity and surface redox behaviour of the nanoparticles. This was further corroborated by EIS, which showed a substantial reduction in charge transfer resistance (R ct ) from 845.84 kΩ for the bare glassy carbon electrode (GCE) to 94.30 kΩ for the Zn 5 (CO 3 ) 2 (OH) 6 modified GCE, indicating enhanced charge-transfer kinetics. These results demonstrate a bio-engineering route for synthesizing single-phase crystalline hydrozincite Zn 5 (CO 3 ) 2 (OH) 6 nanoparticles with favorable opto-electrochemical properties, including enhanced electrochemical behaviour and charge transfer characteristics. Furthermore, the study demonstrates the feasibility of CO 2 mineralization to hydrozincite under ambient conditions.

papers.title: Blockchain-enabled depth-wise separable dual convolutional neural network for reliable scheduling to maximize network lifetime in wireless sensor network
papers.abstract: Abstract Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are a well-known and common deployed network in the field of monitoring and data collection in distributed systems, but the network has many difficulties including limited energy resources, reduced lifetime of the deployed network, inefficient scheduling, and unreliable communication. In this paper, the authors proposed a Blockchain based Dual Convolutional Neural Network (DS2CNN) approach to address the above issues, which is designed to effectively schedule tasks in WSNs and optimize the network lifetime. The proposed approach begins by a corona based zone partitioning model which organizes the network to enable its efficient management of data and reduces communication overhead. A Self-Guided Deep Clustering Network (SeGDCN) is proposed to learn discriminative representations and generate compact and balanced clusters out of the collected data. To perform energy-efficient and load-balanced operation of the network, cluster head (CH) selection using Improved Exponential Distribution Optimizer (I-EDO) is then carried out. The node activity scheduling is completed after clustering, using the DS2CNN model combined with a Dual Attention Transformer Network (DATN) to make intelligent judgments on the activity and sleep states under the condition of the network. To ensure security and trustworthiness, a Weighted Byzantine Fault Tolerance Consensus Algorithm (WByFTCA) is validated of the scheduling and control decisions by a mechanism based on blockchain, so that the integrity and bad behavior resistance is guaranteed. Finally, the optimal routing is done by implementing a Delay-sensitive Energy-Efficient Routing Scheme (DEERS), which uses residual energy, link quality and delay to select optimum routing. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework over the conventional approaches which are potentially suitable for energy efficient and secure WSN application in terms of achieving an increase in network lifetime and decrease in energy consumption and latency.
papers.summary: Abstract Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are a well-known and common deployed network in the field of monitoring and data collection in distributed systems, but the network has many difficulties including limited energy resources, reduced lifetime of the deployed network, inefficient scheduling, and unreliable communication. The node activity scheduling is completed after clustering, using the DS2CNN model combined with a Dual Attention Transformer Network (DATN) to make intelligent judgments on the activity and sleep states under the condition of the network. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework over the conventional approaches which are potentially suitable for energy efficient and secure WSN application in terms of achieving an increase in network lifetime and decrease in energy consumption and latency.

papers.title: Organic matter composition and origin differ between restored and natural UK saltmarshes up to 100 years after the breach
papers.abstract: Restoring saltmarshes to enhance atmospheric carbon dioxide uptake is thought to represent a means of climate change mitigation. While carbon stocks in restored marshes were found to reach equivalence with natural sites, the shares of autochthonous and allochthonous carbon sources entering these marshes are less well known. This issue is important because allochthonous carbon is usually excluded from stock calculations. To determine if differences do exist, the conventional tools for determining organic matter source – elemental, stable isotope and thermogravimetric analyses – were applied to sediments from four restored saltmarshes of different ages. Comparisons were then made with existing data from nearby natural marshes. Breach depth horizons in individual cores were successfully identified using foraminifera, unicellular marine protists. The OC/N-ratio was persistently lower in restored saltmarshes compared with natural counterparts even 100 years after the creation of a breach. Additionally, δ 13 C signals indicated a mixture of organic matter sources to the restored sites and there was often a higher proportion, based upon thermal sensitivity, of recalcitrant material in the organic matter of the restored marshes. Together, these results indicated that a higher proportion of allochthonous organic matter was entering these restored marshes. Understanding the composition of the organic matter in restored marsh sediment will allow the development of robust and constructive climate change mitigation methods.
papers.summary: Restoring saltmarshes to enhance atmospheric carbon dioxide uptake is thought to represent a means of climate change mitigation. Together, these results indicated that a higher proportion of allochthonous organic matter was entering these restored marshes. Understanding the composition of the organic matter in restored marsh sediment will allow the development of robust and constructive climate change mitigation methods.

papers.title: Ontogeny, histochemistry, and the influence of rocky outcrops on secretory ducts in leaves of Kielmeyera rubriflora Cambess (Calophyllaceae)
papers.abstract: Abstract Calophyllaceae in Brazil is represented by seven genera and 96 species, including trees, subshrubs, shrubs, and some lianas, characterized by the presence of canals and cavities responsible to produce bioactive compounds. Although investigations on these structures have been conducted in adult leaves of Kielmeyera rubriflora Cambess, gaps in knowledge remain. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the ontogeny of the ducts, their distribution pattern, the main metabolites present in the secretion, and the influence of rocky outcrops in the Amazonian Savanna on duct density and lumen area. Samples of shoot apices with leaf primordia and leaves at different developmental stages were collected from three distinct substrates in the Amazonian Savanna in Nova Canaã do Norte. The samples were processed using standard plant anatomy methodologies. The ducts of K. rubriflora Cambess develop from the ground meristem through schizogenous formation and are located beneath the epidermis, in the cortical parenchyma, near the phloem, and in the central parenchyma. The anatomical characteristics described for K. rubriflora Cambess are consistent with previous studies. Based on histochemical analyses, we observed that the secretion is of a lipophilic and hydrophilic nature. Regarding the influence of rocky outcrops, variations in duct density and lumen size were observed. We conclude that anatomical studies of K. rubriflora Cambess eaves are essential for understanding its adaptive strategies and for the taxonomic delimitation of Kielmeyera . The metabolites identified play crucial roles in plant protection and resistance, and the differences observed in duct density and lumen area among substrates suggest a possible environmental influence, which should be tested using broader sampling.

papers.title: Domain-alteration chimeras rewire oncogenic complexes in prostate cancer
papers.abstract: Abstract Transcriptional addiction to the androgen receptor (AR) underlies metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer 1 , in which AR maintains oncogenic programs through domain-specific interactions with the acetyltransferases p300 and CBP (collectively p300/CBP) 2 . Here we describe a novel therapeutic modality, domain-alteration chimeras (DALTACs), that rewire endogenous protein complexes by enforcing non-native domain–domain interactions. Our first-in-class AR–p300/CBP DALTAC-1 induces synthetic proximity between the ligand-binding domain of AR and the bromodomain of p300/CBP, misconfiguring their native interface and locking the complex in a non-productive state. DALTAC-1 triggers a ‘super-inhibitory’ effect, suppressing AR-driven transcription and proliferation more potently than combined AR and p300/CBP inhibition. Mechanistically, DALTAC-1 reprograms p300/CBP substrate engagement, abolishing the histone mark H2B N-terminal acetylation and inducing neomorphic acetylation of AR and coactivators, ultimately collapsing the AR neo-enhanceosome. Chromatin profiling revealed redistribution of AR and p300/CBP towards palindromic androgen response elements, accompanied by disruption of cofactor and transcriptional machinery recruitment at oncogenic AR and ERG neo-enhancers. DALTAC-1 exhibits exquisite lineage selectivity, displaying potent activity in AR–p300/CBP dual-dependent cells and sparing AR-negative cells. In multiple in vivo models, DALTAC-1 induces deep and durable tumour regressions. Together, these findings establish DALTACs as a broadly applicable strategy to rewire disease-defining complexes through domain-topology alteration, expanding induced-proximity therapies, and the precise lineage selectivity of DALTAC-1 supports its translational potential in AR-driven prostate cancer.

papers.title: Quantifying charger-related uncertainty in electrical mobility analysis of aerosols with MPSS-UQ 1.0
papers.abstract: Charging probability is the greatest source of uncertainty in electrical mobility-based measurements of aerosol size distributions, but its influence on the results is rarely quantified and reported. In bipolar charging, the charge distribution is almost universally modeled using the Wiedensohler approximation, although it has been shown to deviate significantly from the true charge distribution under many measurement conditions. The charge distribution depends, among other factors, on the mobilities of the charger ions, which are typically not precisely known. Ignoring this uncertainty can lead to biased size distribution estimates and severe underestimation of their uncertainty. In this work, we quantify the uncertainty that imprecisely known charger ion mobilities introduce into the charged particle fractions, and then propagate this uncertainty into the estimates of the particle size distributions using a modular Bayesian approach, in which the ion mobilities are treated as nuisance parameters and marginalized over their plausible range. The inversion method, which is available as the open-source Python package MPSS-UQ, is implemented with particular emphasis on computational efficiency and tested with both synthetic and real mobility particle size spectrometer data. For a month-long field dataset, marginalizing over the uncertain ion mobilities widened the posterior credible intervals of the estimated size distributions on average by a factor of 2.4, with factors up to 10 in some size classes, compared to conditioning on fixed mobility values. The wider intervals provide a more realistic assessment of uncertainties in the inferred size distributions, and quantifying the structure of this uncertainty helps identify where improvements in the characterization of charger ion properties or in the measurement setup would be most effective.

papers.title: Development of a hollow microcapsule preparation method under neutral pH and low temperature using melamine–formaldehyde prepolymer
papers.abstract: The preparation of hollow microcapsules using melamine–formaldehyde (MF) prepolymer was investigated. Chlorobenzene was used as the core material, and large emulsion droplets were prepared by the Shirasu-porous-glass (SPG) membrane emulsification method. The effects of polymerization conditions were evaluated using MF prepolymer as the capsule wall material. Good capsule formation was possible even under mild conditions near neutral pH and at room temperature. Measurements of the bulk density and core retention rate of the capsules confirmed that a certain amount of core material could be removed. This technology is considered to be highly cost-effective and industrially useful.

papers.title: Physiology-adapted cardiac CT angiography during veno-arterial ECMO in neonatal and pediatric postoperative congenital heart disease: feasibility and clinical impact
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Cardiac computed tomographic angiography (CCTA) provides high-resolution anatomical assessment in cases of congenital heart disease (CHD). This is crucial in patients supported by veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO), since the fundamental alteration of systemic hemodynamics and contrast transit kinetics makes conventional CT acquisition strategies unreliable. We evaluated the feasibility, diagnostic yield, and clinical impact of a structured CCTA protocol adapted to ECMO-dependent physiology in postoperative neonatal and pediatric CHD patients. Methods This retrospective, single-center cohort study (2013–2022) included all consecutive postoperative neonatal and pediatric patients with CHD who underwent clinically indicated CCTA while supported by VA-ECMO subsequent to cardiac surgery. Contrast administration route and scan timing were individualized according to ECMO circuit flow characteristics and clinical indication. Results Twenty-six CCTA examinations were performed in 25 patients ranging in age from 3 days to 14.8 years (median age 133 days; median weight 5.1 kg). Contrast was administered via the arterial ECMO limb in 15 cases and intravenously with controlled ECMO flow modulation in 11. In 18 of the 26 examinations (69%) the examination revealed a pathology. CCTA provided anatomical information beyond echocardiography in 22 of 26 cases (85%) and directly informed a surgical or catheter-based intervention in 14 cases (54%), with procedural confirmation in all. No transport-related or CT-related adverse events occurred. Conclusion When acquisition protocols are adapted to ECMO-dependent hemodynamics, CCTA is feasible and diagnostically consequential in neonatal and pediatric patients supported by VA-ECMO after congenital cardiac surgery. A physiology-guided strategy enables consistent vascular enhancement and frequently identifies clinically actionable findings not detected by echocardiography which can directly inform therapeutic decision-making in this critically ill population.

papers.title: Comparison of Bresenham and Siddon ray tracing algorithms for sparse view 3D reconstruction of simulated coronary vessel models
papers.abstract: Interventional C-arm imaging enables minimally invasive cardiac procedures while reducing radiation exposure through sparse-view acquisition. However, reconstruction of three-dimensional vascular morphology from a limited number of projections remains a severely ill-posed inverse problem, particularly in the presence of Poisson quantum noise. This study evaluates two ray-tracing models, Siddon’s (weighted) and Bresenham’s (binary), combined with the Simultaneous Iterative Reconstruction Technique (SIRT) and Total Variation regularization (SIRT+TV). Synthetic phantoms derived from patient-specific coronary geometries were reconstructed from nine simulated noisy cone-beam projections acquired at different angles. Reconstructed volumes were binarized using Otsu and IoU-maximized thresholds. Automatic Otsu thresholding was ineffective for Bresenham-based reconstructions due to severe reconstruction artifacts. Nevertheless, IoU-maximized thresholding yielded a mean Dice-Sørensen coefficient of 0.795, indicating preservation of relevant vascular information. Siddon-based reconstruction produced fewer artifacts and achieved superior performance, reaching a Dice-Sørensen coefficient of 0.860 with SIRT. No clear advantage of TV regularization over SIRT alone was observed. The results demonstrate that key aspects of vascular morphology can be recovered from sparse-view projections. However, the observed reconstruction errors indicate that substantial methodological improvements are required before practical application can be considered.
papers.summary: Interventional C-arm imaging enables minimally invasive cardiac procedures while reducing radiation exposure through sparse-view acquisition. The results demonstrate that key aspects of vascular morphology can be recovered from sparse-view projections. However, the observed reconstruction errors indicate that substantial methodological improvements are required before practical application can be considered.

papers.title: Structural compatibility enables functional co-assembly of Kir2.1 channels and the voltage-sensing domain of voltage-sensitive phosphatases
papers.journal: Pflügers Archiv - European Journal of Physiology
papers.abstract: Abstract Voltage-sensing domains (VSDs), which are integral parts of voltage-gated K + channel (K V ) proteins, are highly modular protein components that function largely independently of ion-conducting pores – a property exploited in genetically encoded voltage indicators (GEVIs). Conversely, inward-rectifier K + channels such as Kir2.1 possess a pore-only architecture and lack a VSD. Here, we demonstrate an unexpected and functionally relevant structural compatibility between the independently evolved pore-only and VSD-only membrane protein families. When co-expressed, Kir2.1 and ASAP-type GEVIs form complexes that constrain VSD movement and markedly interfere with voltage-dependent fluorescence responses. Molecular modeling combined with targeted mutagenesis identified a conserved hydrophobic interface that mediates this interaction. A single bulky substitution in the VSD of the GEVI rEstus-NI (A79W) disrupted the impact of Kir2.1 while preserving the GEVI’s voltage-sensing performance. These findings suggest that pore-only and VSD-only proteins can assemble into functional K V -like architectures, and highlight that membrane proteins may engage in unexpected interactions capable of altering experimental readouts in physiological voltage imaging studies. The study also raises the possibility that independently evolved functional membrane proteins may assemble into previously unrecognized higher-order complexes with distinct functional properties under physiological conditions.

papers.title: Sulfated prism[6]arene binds one guest internally and one guest externally
papers.abstract: We report the synthesis of sulfated prism[6]arene (Pr[6]AS) by reaction of (HO) 12 Pr[6] with SO 3 ·pyridine in 35% yield. Pr[6]AS has very good solubility in water (>30 mM) and does not undergo self-association according to 1 H NMR dilution experiments. Qualitative 1 H NMR investigations show that guest resonances shift dramatically upfield and become significantly broadened upon complexation with Pr[6]AS. Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments show that Pr[6]AS forms ternary complexes (Pr[6]AS·guest 2 ) with hydrophobic ammonium ions in phosphate buffered saline with β-values ( K a1 × K a2 ) values up to 6.84 × 10 13 M −2 . Molecular dynamics simulations show that Pr[6]AS firmly binds one guest ( 6q , Me 4 Bipip) within its cavity and a second guest ( 6q , Me 4 Bipip) on the convex region of Pr[6]AS in close proximity to the externally directed sulfate substituents. Uncomplexed Pr[6]AS holds 7.6 ± 1.9 H 2 O and one Na + ion within its cavity. Formation of the 1:1 and 1:2 Pr[6]AS– 6q complexes results in expulsion of the Na + ion and approximately five of the solvating H 2 O molecules. Intriguingly, the combination of larger naphthalene walls and sulfate ionic groups that are conformationally restricted creates a secondary guest binding site on the exterior of Pr[6]AS which suggests a route toward the design of high molecularity complexes.

papers.title: Study on two-step and low-temperature wet activation of residual carbon derived from coal gasification fine slag and its electrochemical performance for supercapacitor
papers.abstract: Abstract Supercapacitors are promising electrochemical energy storage devices because of their high power density, fast charge–discharge rate, and long cycle life. The development of low-cost and high-performance carbon electrode materials is crucial for improving their practical application. Herein, residual carbon (RC) from coal gasification fine slags (CGFSs) was used as a carbon precursor to prepare low-cost carbon electrode materials (RCHK-X) through HNO₃ pre-activation followed by KOH activation. HNO₃ treatment introduced abundant oxygen-containing functional groups, while subsequent KOH activation further enhanced the surface functionality and specific surface area, removed part of the nitrogen-containing species introduced during acid treatment, and generated more defects and electrochemically active sites. The optimized RCHK-3 sample exhibited a specific surface area of 775 m² g⁻¹ and a low contact angle of 35.0°, suggesting favorable ion accessibility and surface wettability. When used as a supercapacitor electrode, RCHK-3 delivered a specific capacitance of 155 F g⁻¹ at 0.5 A g⁻¹ and maintained 99.03% of its capacitance after 10,000 cycles. This work demonstrates an effective strategy for converting CGFS-derived residual carbon into value-added electrode materials and provides guidance for designing porous carbon materials for high-performance supercapacitors.

papers.title: LLM-guided adaptive segmentation of tunnel linings from point clouds
papers.abstract: Automated inspection of segmental tunnel linings requires adaptive segmentation from 3D point clouds, yet expert-tuned pipelines often degrade when tunnel conditions vary. This paper presents R4Tun, a large language model (LLM)-driven adaptation framework that extends an expert-designed pipeline (SAM4Tun) with bounded parameter tuning informed by structured context: memory ($m$), state ($s$), and knowledge ($k$). Evaluated on 30 selected Seg2Tunnel subsets (13 regular, 17 complex) across three LLMs, the full $m+s+k$ design raised mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU) from 0.18 to 0.43--0.48 and overall accuracy (OA) from 0.42 to 0.59--0.65 relative to the static SAM4Tun baseline, with the near-reference regular (staggered) subsets reaching mIoU 0.784--0.796 across LLMs. Across 270 (30 tunnels $\times$ 3 different LLMs $\times$ 3 context settings) runs, the LLMs showed similar parameter-adjustment trends (with overlapping 95\% CIs on mean gains) and consistently adjusted a shared set of critical parameters. These results support R4Tun as a controlled, label-free, cross-LLM adaptation mechanism in the tested SAM4Tun--Seg2Tunnel setting, demonstrating consistent accuracy gains; we position R4Tun as a mechanism contribution rather than a deployable final-inspection system, in which each bounded parameter change is auditable via logged rationales.

papers.title: Airborne Microplastic Generation and Transport from 3D Printing Activities in a University Setting
papers.abstract: Plastics are everywhere in modern environments, and smaller plastic particles, known as microplastics (MPs, 1 µm-5 mm), have raised increasing concerns regarding indoor air quality and potential human exposure. Given that people spend more than 80% of their time indoors, understanding potential indoor sources and the distribution of MPs is important. Three-dimensional (3D) printing activities have become increasingly common in educational settings and may contribute to indoor MP pollution. However, limited information is available regarding the occurrence, spatial distribution, and physicochemical properties of deposited MPs in and around a university makerspace where filament-extrusion 3D printers and fabric-based activities are routinely used. Deposited particles were collected from multiple locations and characterized using stereomicroscopy and pyrolysis gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (Py-GC/MS). Microscopic analysis quantified particles larger than 10 µm, whereas Py-GC/MS determined mass-based deposition rates for particles larger than 1 µm. MPs were detected throughout the makerspace and in surrounding areas, suggesting potential particle transport beyond the immediate printing area. Methyl methacrylate (MMA) was identified as the predominant pyrolysis product of the black MPs possibly generated by 3D printing activities. These findings provide evidence of MP deposition in a university makerspace and highlight the need for further investigation into indoor MP sources, particle transport, and potential inhalation exposure among individuals engaged in 3D printing and related activities.

papers.title: Noise-assisted quantum entanglement: memory-enhanced coherence in stochastic Jaynes–Cummings dynamics
papers.abstract: Abstract We investigate qubit entanglement dynamics in a two-qubit-cavity system with stochastically fluctuating coupling strength, comparing white noise (Markovian) and Ornstein–Uhlenbeck noise (non-Markovian) processes. We analytically solve the system dynamics for both Fock and coherent cavity states and systematically characterize how initial qubit configurations affect entanglement generation and preservation. Our results reveal distinct dynamical regimes: In the Fock state cavity, initial states in the single-excitation subspace generate robust qubit entanglement in decoherence-free subspaces, while initially entangled states in the double-excitation subspace exhibit inevitable decay without protective symmetries. For coherent cavities, we identify a critical photon-number threshold in the intermediate coherent state amplitude regime where dynamics transition from low-frequency to high-frequency entanglement oscillations, while universal entanglement loss occurs at large amplitudes. Remarkable resilience against entanglement sudden death emerges under strong non-Markovian noise with long correlation times, where repeated revivals occur. These findings establish cavity photon statistics and environmental memory time as key control parameters for engineering qubit entanglement dynamics in qubit-cavity systems, revealing how system-environment correlations govern quantum information preservation.

papers.title: Enhanced Propane Dehydroaromatization over CeZn/ZSM-5 Nanosheets
papers.abstract: Abstract Propane dehydroaromatization (PDA) provides an efficient nonpetroleum route for upgrading light alkanes into high-value aromatics, yet conventional Zn-modified ZSM-5 (Zn/n-HZSM-5) catalysts suffer from rapid deactivation owing to diffusion limitations and subsequent carbon deposition. Herein, we developed a catalyst with a shortened b-axis (Zn/s-HZSM-5) via a urea-assisted hydrothermal method to optimize mass transfer within the zeolite channels. Compared with the Zn/n-HZSM-5 possessing a prolonged b-axis thickness of 250–270 nm, the Zn/s-HZSM-5 catalyst exhibited a significantly thinner b-axis of 100–130 nm, leading to a dramatic enhancement in propane conversion from 39.5% to 89.1%. Zero-length column (ZLC) desorption, fixed-bed breakthrough, and transient propane/N2 switching experiments demonstrated that the shortened b-axis pathways accelerated the diffusion of heavy aromatics, thereby reducing their residence time within the micropores. Ultraviolet Raman (UV-Raman) and thermogravimetric (TG) analyses revealed that Zn/s-HZSM-5 suppresses graphitic coke formation, which was responsible for irreversible pore-mouth blocking. To improve the regeneration durability of the catalyst, a trace amount of Ce was incorporated (0.10CeZn/s-HZSM-5), giving an aromatics yield exceeding 50% after three consecutive reaction–regeneration cycles (560 °C, WHSV at 0.8 h–1 and N2/C3H8 at 1.5 vol/vol). This work indicates that managing diffusion kinetics via b-axis manipulation is a key strategy for achieving sustained longevity in alkane upgrading.

papers.title: Efficient inverse cobalt-based catalysts for low-temperature methanation of low-concentration CO2 streams
papers.abstract: The catalytic hydrogenation of residual carbon dioxide in hydrogen-rich gas streams is highly relevant to hydrogen purification and low-carbon energy technologies. Herein, we report a series of cobalt-based inverse Ba–REE/Co (REE = Ce, Nd, Sm) catalysts designed for efficient methanation of low-concentration CO 2 streams. The application of an inverse oxide/metal configuration resulted in promoter oxides being dispersed on metallic cobalt, thereby maximizing metal–oxide interfacial interactions and enabling synergistic reactant activation. All catalysts exhibited high activity, achieving 78–84% CO 2 conversion at 220 °C and nearly complete conversion at 270 °C. Among the catalysts, Ba–Ce/Co showed the best performance. Comprehensive characterization studies revealed that catalytic performance is not directly dependent on CO 2 adsorption capacity but rather on the nature and accessibility of adsorption sites under reaction conditions. In particular, weak, accessible basic sites promote efficient CO 2 activation and intermediate turnover, whereas stronger binding leads to partial surface blocking. The findings also highlight inverse oxide/metal architectures as a rational design strategy for highly efficient catalysts for processes of industrial and economic significance.

papers.title: A systematic review of soil in forensic investigations: from physicochemical characterization to microbial fingerprinting
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Soil is a versatile, and one of the most widely encountered trace materials during forensic investigations. Soil pertains unique physicochemical characteristics, having varied biological composition that it’s specified to geological locations. These specific characteristics confer linkage to suspects, victims, and related articles at the scene of incident. Despite its long history of forensic application, the full analytical potential of soil, particularly through the lens of modern molecular microbiology, has yet to be fully consolidated in a single comprehensive review. Main Body This review examines soil as forensic trace evidence across its physical, chemical, biological, and microbiological dimensions, with particular emphasis on the emerging role of the soil microbiome as a forensic discriminator. A systematic search for peer-reviewed literature published between 2002 and 2025 have been conducted using the databases sources: Search Terminologies used in this search included following combination of words: “forensic soil”, “soil trace evidence”, “soil microbiome forensics”, “soil microbial fingerprint”, “next-generation sequencing forensics”, “post-mortem interval soil”, and “geolocation microbial”. A total of 75 studies were included after screening for relevance, methodological quality, and date of publication. Key applications include geographic origin determination, suspect–scene linkage, post-mortem interval estimation, and corroboration of conventional forensic evidence. Critical challenges include the absence of standardized protocols, limited geo-referenced, reference databases, environmental variability of microbial communities, and unresolved questions of legal admissibility. Conclusion An integrated, multidisciplinary framework combining physical, chemical, and microbiological analyses, supported by validated bioinformatics pipelines and comprehensive reference databases, is necessary to realize the full forensic potential of soil. Addressing current methodological and legal gaps will be essential for the routine admission of soil microbiome evidence in judicial proceedings.

papers.title: Proton conducting Cicer arietinum L starch electrolyte doped with NH4SCN for electrochemical double layer capacitors
papers.abstract: Abstract A chickpea starch–agar biopolymer electrolyte plasticized with glycerol and doped with NH 4 SCN was successfully developed for symmetric electrochemical double-layer capacitor (EDLC) applications. FTIR confirmed the interaction between NH 4 SCN and the biopolymer matrix, while XRD revealed increasing amorphous character with salt addition. The optimized CSA5 electrolyte exhibited a maximum ionic conductivity of 1.1 × 10 − 3 S cm −1 , a low bulk resistance of 43.60 Ω, an ionic transference number of 0.89, an electrochemical stability window of 1.8 V, and good thermal stability. The EDLC exhibited a specific capacitance of 40.0 F g −1 at 5 mV s −1 from CV, decreasing to 3.9 F g −1 at 70 mV s −1 . From GCD measurements, the specific capacitance decreased from 42.14 F g −1 at 0.15 mA to 21.28 F g −1 at 0.25 mA. The corresponding energy density decreased from 5.85 to 2.95 Wh kg −1 , while the power density increased from approximately 375–625 W kg −1 . The rate-dependent capacitance indicates limitations in ion transport and electrode/electrolyte interfacial accessibility at higher scan and current rates. Overall, the CSA5 electrolyte demonstrates the basic electrochemical functionality required for solid-state EDLC applications and provides a preliminary assessment of its energy-storage potential.

papers.title: Tunable Gaussian Random Number Generator from a Nanoscopic Domain-Wall-Based Spintronic Device
papers.abstract: Abstract Existing hardware implementations of Gaussian random number generators (RNGs) rely on large arrays of binary devices, resulting in substantial hardware footprints or sampling-time overheads. Here, we present a racetrack memory-based random number generator (RTM-RNG) that directly generates analog Gaussian random number streams from a single domain-wall-based nanoscale racetrack. A geometrically engineered racetrack tip creates a localized current-density gradient, enabling field-free stochastic domain-wall nucleation driven by nanosecond current pulses. The domain-wall nucleation probability is continuously tunable via an electrically generated Oersted field or an external magnetic field, providing direct control over the mean of the output distribution. We demonstrate more than 256 distinguishable states from a single nanoscopic RTM-RNG device, thus making a Gaussian RNG with more than 8-bit resolution possible. Compared with conventional binary random bitstreams, the RTM-RNG achieves high-quality Gaussian distributions up to 83 times faster.

papers.title: Mechanistic Insights and Characteristics of Levofloxacin HCl-Loaded Solvent Exchange-Triggered Myristic-Based In Situ Forming Matrix
papers.abstract: Abstract A solvent exchange–triggered myristic acid (MYR)-based in situ forming matrix (ISM) incorporating levofloxacin hydrochloride (Lf) was developed as a controlled drug release system for localized periodontal therapy. The formulation, composed of MYR dissolved in N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) with optional triacetin (TRI), undergoes aqueous-induced phase inversion to form a crystalline laminar matrix. Physicochemical evaluation demonstrated low injection force (<1.2 N), tunable viscosity, and density-driven buoyancy behavior, while water tolerance and interfacial studies confirmed that TRI retarded solvent exchange and delayed matrix crystallization. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) supported the retention of MYR crystallinity after matrix formation. Cross-sectional and SEM analyses revealed progressive matrix densification and increasing structural tortuosity over time, explaining the transition from initial burst release to sustained diffusion-controlled drug release. In vitro drug release exhibited dose-dependent and matrix-modulated behavior (0.25–1.5% w/w), with higher MYR content restricting diffusion and higher Lf loading enhancing concentration gradients. The controlled release characteristics directly translated into antimicrobial performance. Antimicrobial studies against Staphylococcus aureus, MRSA, Porphyromonas gingivalis, and Aggregatibacter actinomycetemcomitans demonstrated intrinsic solvent contribution, clear dose-dependent inhibition, and sustained activity for up to 7 days. Cytotoxicity evaluation in human dermal fibroblasts showed >80% cell viability in the MTT assay and >90% viable cells in the Annexin V/PI assay, with no significant increase in apoptosis under the tested conditions. Under a clinically realistic loading constraint of 1.0 mg formulation per periodontal pocket, theoretical drug concentrations (5–30 μg/mL) exceeded MIC values for key pathogens. Computational analyses further supported diffusion retardation and MYR–Lf interaction as molecular mechanisms underlying sustained release. Collectively, the MYR-based ISM platform enables tunable and sustained antimicrobial delivery through crystallization-driven matrix formation and controlled solvent exchange.

papers.title: P53-mediated apoptosis and topoisomerase IIα inhibition by an acridine derivative in hepatocellular carcinoma
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Primary liver malignancy represents a significant worldwide health burden characterized by restricted therapeutic alternatives and elevated relapse frequencies. While acridine-based compounds have demonstrated promising bioactive properties including anticancer capabilities, challenges persist in enhancing their therapeutic efficacy and target specificity. Purpose This investigation evaluated the antineoplastic properties and underlying molecular mechanisms of a newly synthesized acridine hydrochloride compound, N-(3-(4-(3-aminopropyl)piperazin-1-yl)propyl)acridin-9-amine hydrochloride (9-BAPPA), targeting HepG2 hepatocellular carcinoma cells. Methods Cell viability in NHPL and HepG2 cells was determined using the MTT assay. Cell death was showed both morphologically with fluorescent double staining (AO/EB) and biochemically with flow cytometry analysis. The levels of p53, BCL-2, BAX, caspase-3, and PCNA proteins was assessed by immunocytochemistry, while mRNA expression of p53, caspase-3, and the BAX/BCL-2 ratio were measured using qRT PCR. In addition, molecular docking with topoisomerase IIα was performed to explore the compound’s predicted binding mode. Results In vitro assays showed that 9-BAPPA selectively inhibited HepG2 cells (IC₅₀ = 15.2 µg/mL) with much lower toxicity toward normal NHPL cells (IC₅₀ = 34.3 µg/mL). Treated cells exhibited apoptotic morphology and cell cycle arrest at sub-G₀/G₁ and G₂/M phases ( p < 0.0001). Upregulation of p53, caspase-3, and the BAX/BCL-2 ratio at both mRNA and protein levels ( p ≤ 0.01) confirmed the activation of the intrinsic p53-dependent mitochondrial apoptosis pathway. Computational docking analyses revealed robust binding interactions between 9-BAPPA and essential residues (MET 762, MET 766, Q778) within topoisomerase IIα, confirming its mechanism as a topoisomerase-interfering compound. In silico Pharmacokinetics showed good oral bioavailability and promising permeability of Blood Brain Barrier. Conclusion 9-BAPPA exhibits significant selective antineoplastic properties through P53-mediated apoptotic pathway activation and cell cycle disruption in HepG2 cells, warranting additional investigation as a potential therapeutic compound for hepatic malignancies.

Methods Cell viability in NHPL and HepG2 cells was determined using the MTT assay. Results In vitro assays showed that 9-BAPPA selectively inhibited HepG2 cells (IC₅₀ = 15.2 µg/mL) with much lower toxicity toward normal NHPL cells (IC₅₀ = 34.3 µg/mL).

papers.title: Guided-wave transmission of ultrasonic signals using compressive sensing and time-domain encoding
papers.abstract: The increasing deployment of intelligent structures and embedded sensor networks creates a growing demand for reliable transmission of measurement data in environments where conventional wired and wireless communication methods are ineffective. In metallic and enclosed structures, electromagnetic waves are strongly attenuated, while wired solutions increase system complexity and weight. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel guided-wave-based framework for the transmission of full ultrasonic measurement signals within structural elements. The proposed approach combines compressive sensing with a dual-stage encoding strategy. First, ultrasonic signals acquired by piezoelectric sensors are compressed using the Compressive Sampling Matching Pursuit (CoSaMP) algorithm, enabling efficient representation with a reduced number of samples while preserving essential measurement information. Next, selected amplitude–time pairs are encoded into single integer values and mapped onto a binary representation. This binary data is transmitted through the structure using a pulse position modulation (16-PPM) scheme, where information is encoded in the temporal location of ultrasonic wave packets. The method was validated both numerically, using finite element simulations, and experimentally on an aluminium plate instrumented with piezoelectric transducers. The transmission process was performed in a multi-hop configuration, and the original measurement signals were reconstructed at the final node. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables accurate reconstruction of ultrasonic signals from significantly reduced datasets, with only approximately 6% of samples required. Despite the presence of noise and wave dispersion, the reconstructed signals preserved the features necessary for reliable damage detection and localization. The study confirms that guided waves can be used not only for structural diagnostics but also as a medium for robust transmission of measurement data, enabling integrated sensing–communication systems for structural health monitoring applications.
