papers.title: Spatial Glycomics of a Mouse Model of High-Grade Serous Ovarian Cancer
papers.abstract: Abstract Ovarian cancer (OC) is one of the deadliest cancers in women, with high mortality rates and a lack of effective screening tools. Among all OC subtypes, high-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC), also known as high-grade serous ovarian cancer, is the most common, making up about 75% of epithelial OC cases. N-Glycans may play essential roles in OC development, as they are involved in cell signaling, recognition, adhesion, and differentiation. In this study, we present spatially resolved N-glycan profiling of HGSC reproductive tissues from a triple mutant (TKO) mouse model (n = 6) using matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI MSI). By comparing levels of various N-glycan classes between OC tissues and control tissues (n = 6), we identified potential OC N-glycan biomarkers and developed multivariate statistical models to distinguish HGSC from healthy tissues. Endoglycosidase F3 digestion, followed by a two-step amidation reaction for sialic acid, confirmed that core-fucosylation and α2,6-sialylation were the two most important N-glycan modifications observed in HGSC regions of TKO mice that displayed the most significant differences between controls and TKO. The notable increase in bisecting core-fucosylated N-glycans further supports the hypothesis that protein transport and metastasis are elevated in the later stages of OC. Conversely, the decrease in certain α2,6-sialylated N-glycans suggests potential roles in OC cell signaling, migration, and metastasis, which warrant further validation. Additionally, the rise in high-mannose N-glycans and N-glycan degradation products offered early insights into how abnormal N-glycan levels may contribute to OC progression and disrupt normal cell functions.

papers.title: Sustainable barley starchs-based bioplastics functionalized with Ocimum tenuiflorum extract
papers.abstract: The increasing environmental concerns associated with petroleum-based plastics have accelerated the development of sustainable, biodegradable packaging materials derived from biodegradable and renewable packaging materials with improved functional properties. The study aimed to develop a biodegradable barley starch-based plastic with antimicrobial properties for packaging applications. The novelty lies in using barley as a matrix for making bioplastic functionalized with Ocimum tenuiflorum (holy basil) was developed as an environmentally friendly active packaging material. The bioplastics were prepared using the solution-casting method, with water, glycerin, and vinegar as plasticizers. The effects of adding basil extract on the structural, mechanical, thermal, moisture-management, antibacterial, and biodegradation properties of the bioplastics were systematically studied. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) showed that the bioplastic had a dense and homogenous morphology without significant pores or defects. Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy confirmed the incorporation of basil-derived functional groups into the starch matrix. Thermal analysis showed improved thermal stability with increasing basil extract content. The glass transition temperature (Tg) increased from 65.4°C to 80.2°C, while the total mass loss decreased from 90.86% to 84.94%. The basil-enriched bioplastics also showed a higher residual mass (5.92–6.20%) than the control sample (2.41%), indicating improved thermal resistance. The developed bioplastics showed a bursting strength ranging from 3.5 to 5.14 kg/cm² and controlled moisture absorption. Soil burial testing showed 42% biodegradation after 12 weeks. In addition, the films demonstrated antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus. These findings highlight the potential of barley starch-based bioplastics enriched with holy basil as environmentally friendly materials for active and sustainable packaging applications.

The study aimed to develop a biodegradable barley starch-based plastic with antimicrobial properties for packaging applications. papers.title: Viscoelastic tensile constitutive framework for PVC gels
papers.abstract: Abstract Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) gels are promising electroactive polymers because of their large actuation strains, comparatively low voltage requirements, and tunable mechanical properties through plasticization. However, their viscoelastic tensile response remains largely uncharacterized, limiting the transient and dynamic material descriptions required for multiphysics modelling of electrohydraulic systems such as the Electrohydraulic Actuator Powered by Induced Interfacial Charges (EPIC). This work develops a unified viscoelastic tensile constitutive framework for PVC gels plasticized with dibutyl adipate (DBA) by combining tensile stress relaxation and dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA). Multiobjective optimization using the dynamic non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (DNSGA-II) simultaneously fitted time-domain stress relaxation modulus and frequency-domain storage and loss moduli up to 35 Hz. A 5-term Prony-series was identified as the minimum investigated model order capable of representing all three responses within a 5% normalized mean absolute error criterion. Reduced 2-term and 3-term models accurately represented timedomain stress relaxation, with normalized root mean square errors below 1.60%, but did not reproduce the frequency-domain response. Power-law scaling of the Prony-series moduli with plasticizer content was consistent with similar underlying polymer network structures, while variations in relaxation time scales suggested changes in molecular mobility. The resulting framework provides the time-dependent material description required for coupled multiphysics modelling of PVC gel electrohydraulic actuators.

papers.title: ANALISA KONDUKTIVITAS TERMAL SERAT BATANG JAGUNG SEBAGAI BAHAN ALTERNATIF ISOLATOR PADA ALAT PENUKAR KALOR
papers.abstract: The utilization of agricultural waste as environmentally friendly engineering materials has attracted increasing attention due to the growing demand for sustainable thermal insulation. Corn stalk fiber is a promising lignocellulosic biomass with potential application as a thermal insulating material. This study investigates the effect of material density on the thermal conductivity of corn stalk fiber to evaluate its feasibility as an alternative insulation material for heat exchanger applications. Thermal conductivity was measured using the steady-state radial heat transfer method based on Fourier's law. A total of nine specimens were prepared, consisting of three density levels (100, 150, and 200 kg/m³), each tested at inlet temperatures of 40°C, 60°C, and 80°C. Thermal conductivity was determined from the heat transfer rate, specimen thickness, heat transfer area, and temperature difference across the insulation material. The results showed that thermal conductivity increased with increasing material density. The lowest thermal conductivity, 0.084 W/mK, was obtained at a density of 100 kg/m³ and an inlet temperature of 40°C, indicating the best thermal insulation performance. At densities of 150 and 200 kg/m³, thermal conductivity increases to ranges of 0.113–0.118 W/mK and 0.122–0.125 W/mK, respectively, due to the reduction of air voids within the fiber structure. The influence of testing temperature on thermal conductivity was relatively small compared with the effect of material density. These findings demonstrate that low-density corn stalk fiber offers promising thermal insulation characteristics and has potential for application as a sustainable insulation material to reduce heat loss and improve the thermal efficiency of heat exchanger systems.

papers.title: Enhancing fire survivability of biochar with medium-entropy oxide coatings
papers.abstract: Biochar derived from low-value biomass offers a sustainable platform for lightweight structural and thermal insulation materials; however, its susceptibility to oxidative degradation under prolonged fire exposure limits practical implementation. Here, we report an entropy-engineered ceramic coating strategy to substantially enhance the fire survivability of biochar. Three-metal-element FeMnZn medium-entropy oxide (3ME-MEO) and five-metal-element FeMnZnAlZr MEO (5ME-MEO) coatings were synthesized via a low-temperature, scalable route and uniformly deposited onto porous biochar. Microscopic and spectroscopic analyses reveal homogeneous multielement distributions from the micro- to nanoscale, while the increased compositional complexity of MEO induces greater structural disorder without detectable macroscopic elemental segregation. Under direct ethanol-flame exposure at ~ 1000 °C, pristine biochar suffers severe oxidative degradation, whereas the entropy-engineered coatings effectively preserve the carbon framework. After 20 min, the mass loss decreases from 38.8% for pristine biochar to 23.5% for biochar/3ME-MEO and 18.5% for biochar/5ME-MEO after correcting for coating-derived mass loss. The MEO coatings remain spatially homogeneous after prolonged burning and provide sustained protection against thermal-oxidative attack. Hotplate and modified UL-94-type tests further reveal comparable surface-temperature evolution among the samples despite markedly different degrees of structural degradation. These findings indicate that enhanced fire survivability primarily arises from the protective barrier effect of the MEO coatings, which suppresses oxidative consumption of the carbon framework and mitigates direct flame attack, rather than from thermal insulation.

papers.title: Waste reduction and blue skies: assessing the air quality effects of the Zero-Waste City policy with double machine learning
papers.abstract: Building zero-waste cities is a central policy effort aimed at cutting solid waste at its source and speeding up the green, low-carbon transition of cities, and it bears heavily on the improvement of urban ecological quality. Treating the Zero-Waste City policy (ZWCP) as a quasi-natural experiment, we exploit a 2010–2024 panel of 271 prefecture-level cities together with a double machine learning approach to gauge how the policy shapes urban air quality and through which channels it operates. Three results stand out. First, launching the ZWCP lowers a city's annual mean PM2.5 concentration by approximately 4.6%, thereby delivering a modest but statistically significant association with improved air quality, and this pattern persists across an extensive battery of robustness checks. Second, the channel analysis yields evidence consistent with two potential routes through which the policy may restrain urban air pollution: industrial structure upgrading and green technology innovation. Third, the estimated abatement appears larger in small and medium-sized cities and in cities outside the old industrial bases, although the absence of formal cross-group tests means that these patterns should be regarded as suggestive. Taken together, the paper broadens the strand of work that links environmental regulation to urban air quality and supplies both a theoretical rationale and preliminary empirical evidence for refining ZWCP design and for considering place-specific approaches to green transition.

papers.title: CK2β variants associated with Poirier–Bienvenu neurodevelopmental syndrome differentially affect CK2 holoenzyme assembly and stability
papers.abstract: Introduction Mutations in the CSNK2B gene, which encodes the non-catalytic CK2β subunit of human protein kinase CK2, can cause Poirier -Bienvenu neurodevelopmental syndrome (POBINDS). The CK2 holoenzyme comprises two regulatory CK2β subunits and two catalytic CK2α or CK2α′ subunits. The interaction between CK2β and the catalytic CK2α/α’ subunits influences substrate phosphorylation and protein thermostability. Key structural regions involved in α/β interactions include the αF helix and hairpin loop, whereas β/β dimerization is stabilized by the zinc finger domain. Size-exclusion chromatography, activity assays and isothermal titration calorimetry were employed to investigate holoenzyme assembly and subunit interactions. Negative-stain electron microscopy was utilized to examine the structural integrity of selected holoenzymes. Size exclusion chromatography and isothermal titration calorimetry confirmed that these variants markedly impair holoenzyme formation. However, the zinc-finger variant C137G retains the ability to form intact holoenzymes, as further demonstrated by negative-stain electron microscopy reconstruction. Thermostability analyses using differential scanning fluorimetry further indicated that several disease-associated variants, particularly those with melting temperatures close to physiological temperature, may produce unstable CK2β subunits and thereby impair holoenzyme assembly in vivo. Discussion These findings demonstrate that POBINDS-associated CK2β variants can disrupt CK2 holoenzyme formation and stability, ultimately reducing CK2 activity through distinct molecular effects.

papers.title: Distinct associations of rhizoid-sphere and endophytic bacteria with dominant moss traits along an elevational gradient on Segrila Mountain
papers.abstract: Microbial communities associated with alpine mosses remain poorly characterized in southeastern Tibet, particularly the distinction between bacteria at the rhizoid-soil interface and those inside moss tissues. We used 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing to characterize 36 rhizoid-sphere and 12 endophytic samples from three dominant mosses ( Actinothuidium hookeri , Ptilium crista-castrensis , and Dicranum fuscescens ) across four elevations (3,700–4,300 m) on Segrila Mountain. We combined community analysis, SPIEC-EASI networks, random forests, and path modeling to examine how habitat, elevation, soil properties, and bacterial community attributes were related to moss traits. The endophytic network showed higher clustering (0.665) and modularity (0.84) and a larger proportion of positive partial correlations (94.71%) than rhizoid-sphere’s (0.305, 0.79, and 83.48%). Elevation uniquely explained 25.9% of the variation in rhizoid-sphere bacterial composition ( p = 0.0001), compared with 7.9% for moss species ( p = 0.0093), while neither factor significantly explained endophytic composition (both p > 0.05). Soil properties explained rhizoid-sphere community variation (adjusted R 2 = 0.199, p = 0.001), whereas the endophytic model was nonsignificant (adjusted R 2 = 0.029, p = 0.239). Random-forest models most strongly predicted moss tissue K (LOOCV R 2 = 0.58) and N (LOOCV R 2 = 0.48). In path modeling, rhizoid-sphere Shannon diversity was positively associated with morphology ( β = 0.500, p = 0.0005) and negatively associated with nutrient ( β = −0.263, p = 0.0036). These findings highlight the rhizoid-sphere as an interface linking elevation, soil conditions, bacterial community variation, and moss traits.

papers.title: Governing Artificial General Intelligence in Future Healthcare Institutions: Risk-Adaptive Institutional Authorization for Clinical and Operational Authority
papers.abstract: Increasingly general and agentic artificial intelligence raises an institutional question of authority: which actions may a system perform, how may it combine them, and who may revise or withdraw permission? For prospective artificial general intelligence (AGI), cross-domain planning makes unfamiliar combinations of familiar tasks a central problem of authorization. This article develops a Risk-Adaptive AGI Governance Framework through conceptual synthesis, purposive document comparison, and three constructed scenarios. Four determinants—task risk, demonstrated capability, institutional preparedness, and accountability—inform five authorization gates. The governing rule grants the least authority sufficient for a justified service objective within mandatory constraints. Information, recommendation, and bounded execution permissions can be combined only through additional authorization of their dependencies. A versioned record binds component permissions, configuration, and cross-service ownership; changes to a shared condition reopen affected grants. Administrative scheduling illustrates professional and patient challenges to an otherwise technically eligible grant. Emergency coordination traces partial execution, shared infrastructure failure, unavailable fallback, and conditional restoration. Four testable propositions address risk-sensitive allocation, preparedness, calibrated reliance, and precommitted containment. RAGF connects established lifecycle safeguards to continuing institutional authorization, dispute resolution, and patient remedy. The proposed evaluation agenda examines safety, workflow benefit, equitable access, and the costs of maintaining and withdrawing permission. For future healthcare institutions, preparation for AGI entails an accountable allocation of discretion across services, professionals, and patients.

papers.title: Development of a hybrid formulation combining copper(II) oxide nanoparticles and carbon fiber for polymer-modified asphalt binders
papers.abstract: This study developed a hybrid formulation of copper(II) oxide nanoparticles (nano-CuO) and carbon fiber for a styrene-butadiene-styrene (SBS)-modified asphalt binder. The modifiers were first evaluated separately across physicochemical, rheological, fatigue, and thermal responses to select contents for hybridization. Nano-CuO was added at 2–8 wt% and carbon fiber at 0.1–0.5 wt%. Characterization included X-ray diffraction, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), apparent viscosity, continuous high-temperature performance grade, multiple stress creep recovery (MSCR), linear amplitude sweep, and thermal conductivity. A Derringer-Suich desirability analysis integrated these responses to select the additive contents. Nano-CuO increased the continuous high-temperature grade and thermal conductivity but induced FTIR changes consistent with oxidation of the SBS polybutadiene phase, associated with lower percent recovery (%R 3.2 ). Carbon fiber improved thermal conductivity and the MSCR response without measurable changes in the monitored FTIR indices. The analysis selected 4 wt% nano-CuO and 0.1 wt% carbon fiber. Two hybrids combining 4 wt% nano-CuO with 0.1 wt% (H1) or 0.3 wt% (H2) carbon fiber were evaluated. Relative to the nano-CuO base binder (C4), H1 increased thermal conductivity by approximately 23%, with MSCR parameters within test repeatability and RTFOT-aged fatigue factors statistically indistinguishable from C4 in every strain-amplitude band. Among C4, H1 and H2, only H1 showed no detectable loss relative to the reference binder at high strain amplitudes. H2 achieved a larger conductivity increase (42%) but was the only hybrid whose fatigue factors fell significantly below the reference binder at high strain amplitudes. H1 therefore offered the better overall balance and is recommended for subsequent validation.

papers.title: Heat-Resistant Chitosan-Based Adhesive for Lunar Mare Simulant Brick-to-Fabric Adhesion
papers.abstract: Abstract As lunar exploration advances, the development of in situ resource utilization (ISRU) has become critical for enabling sustained surface operations and reducing payload mass. Lunar regolith-based bricks are promising construction materials for applications such as launch and landing pads, roads, habitat reinforcement, and radiation shielding. However, bonding these lunar bricks to a flexible fabric such as carbon fiber remains a significant challenge due to their very different surface chemistries and mechanical properties. In this study, a fire-resistant adhesive composed of chitosan, acetic acid, and pentaerythritol was developed to bond lunar mare simulant (LMS) bricks to woven carbon fiber fabric. The thermal stability of the adhesive was characterized using thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), while adhesion was evaluated through lap shear and oxygen-methylacetylene-propadiene propane (oxy-MAPP) torch testing. The adhesive maintained structural adhesion under direct flame exposure with no bond delamination, brick displacement, or detachment for any adhesive tested. Despite the front side of the samples reaching extreme temperatures >2200 °C, the bonded brick-to-fabric samples remained intact through both continuous and cyclic flame exposures. These results demonstrate that this simple biobased adhesive provides durable, heat-resistant bonding for lunar brick-to-fabric assemblies.

papers.title: Nanoscale ZnO Coatings on Poly(methyl methacrylate) Submicron Spheres via Low-Temperature Atomic Layer Deposition for Enhanced UV-Blocking Properties
papers.abstract: Abstract Poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA), a synthetic thermoplastic polymer, has been extensively used in our lives due to its advantageous properties such as high transparency, lightweight, and biocompatibility. Although PMMA exhibits great potential in sunscreens, its poor UV-blocking properties hinder its practical applications. In this study, we modified the PMMA submicron spheres (120–150 nm) with nanoscale ZnO using atomic layer deposition (ALD) in a fluidized bed reactor at a low temperature of 40 °C, with diethylzinc (DEZ) and water as precursors. We systematically investigated the ZnO-coated PMMA microspheres using FTIR, XRD, SEM, TEM, XPS, and TG to elucidate the mechanism of nucleation and growth of ZnO. The results revealed that the ZnO deposited was polycrystalline, displaying a granular morphology on the PMMA surfaces. Specifically, a nanoparticle-coated structure was observed after low-cycle ALD, while a conformal nanofilm was formed after high-cycle ALD on the PMMA spheres, suggesting an island growth mode of ZnO. The analysis of the surface chemical species and functional groups via XPS and in situ FTIR indicated that the fast nucleation of ZnO was attributed to trace amounts of hydroxyl groups and hydrogen-bonded water molecules bound on the surfaces of the emulsion-polymerized submicron PMMA spheres. After ZnO coating, the PMMA microspheres exhibited improved UV-blocking performance. The reflectance within the 280–400 nm UV range dropped sharply from ca. 95% (pristine PMMA) to 19% for the PMMA/ZnO composite which had an optical bandgap of 3.36 eV. Meanwhile, the average visible-light reflectance remained above 93%. Moreover, owing to the physical barrier effect of the ZnO coating, the derivative thermogravimetric (DTG) peak temperature increased by 30 °C and the acetone resistance improved. This study not only provides a feasible strategy for modifying polymeric particle surfaces and fabricating organic–inorganic hybrid materials but could also advance the uses of PMMA spheres in high-end cosmetics.

papers.title: Preparation and Characterization of PHBV/PLA/TPS Blends Containing Citric Acid-Modified Thermoplastic Starch
papers.abstract: Abstract The aim of this study was to modify the structural, mechanical, thermal, rheological, and morphological properties of PHBV-based blends through the incorporation of PLA and citric acid-modified thermoplastic starch (TPS). Although PHBV is a biodegradable polymer with environmental advantages, its processing challenges and relatively low mechanical performance limit its practical applications, which can be addressed by blending it with PLA and TPS to tailor the properties of the resulting materials. TPS was prepared by plasticizing corn starch with glycerol and incorporating different concentrations of citric acid (0, 5, and 10 wt %). Subsequently, PHBV/PLA/TPS blends were obtained by extrusion and characterized by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), tensile testing, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), rheological measurements, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The results demonstrated that the addition of citric acid altered the morphology, mechanical properties, and thermal behavior of TPS, while its effects on the PHBV/PLA/TPS blends depended strongly on blend composition. Among the TPS formulations, T5 exhibited the highest tensile strength (9.6 MPa), whereas 40PH/30P/30T0 showed the highest tensile strength among the blends (18.7 MPa). The 40PH/40P/20T10 formulation exhibited the most homogeneous morphology and the highest thermal stability among the ternary blends, with a maximum degradation temperature of 295 °C. Overall, the incorporation of PLA and citric acid-modified TPS enabled the properties of PHBV-based blends to be tailored through changes in composition and TPS modification, demonstrating their potential for the development of biodegradable materials with improved and tunable performance.

papers.title: Oral bacterial lysate treatment for prevention of recurrent wheeze following severe bronchiolitis: protocol for an international multicentre randomised, placebo-controlled trial (BLIPA)
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Bronchiolitis is a common condition caused by a viral acute lower respiratory infection (ALRI) in infants. Severe bronchiolitis requiring hospitalisation is associated with increased risk of preschool wheeze and school-age asthma. Early exposure to microbial products modulating immune system development may help prevent later wheeze. Thus, this study evaluates whether an oral bacterial lysate after bronchiolitis hospitalisation reduces subsequent wheezing episodes. Methods This international multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial tests bacterial lysate (OM85-BV; Broncho-Vaxom®) in infants after hospitalisation for bronchiolitis. Safety and efficacy will be assessed, and a subset will undergo exploratory mechanistic analyses. For 12–24 months post-discharge, parents/guardians will give one capsule of OM85-BV or placebo daily for 10 consecutive days each month. Results The primary endpoint is the number of parent/guardian-reported wheeze episodes 12-months after starting OM85-BV or placebo. Secondary outcomes at 12 or 24-months follow-up include clinical outcomes, parent-proxy quality-of-life scores, incidence of atopy, recurrent wheeze needing asthma medication, wheeze-related hospitalisations, number of ALRI episodes, and mechanistic data on systemic immune pathways and nasopharyngeal and gut microbiota. Conclusions This international multicentre study will determine whether oral OM85-BV given for 10 consecutive days each month for 12–24 months reduces parent/guardian-reported recurrent wheeze episodes post-hospitalisation for bronchiolitis. Trial registration (4) AZNCTR ACTRN12621001556831 (5/10/2021) and clinicaltrials.gov NCT05064631 (20/08/2020). Prospectively Registered. Approval to use the IMP in this clinical trial was provided by the Australian Government Therapeutic Goods Agency under the clinical trials notification scheme (TGA CTN: CT-2021-CTN-02639-1). Impact Our study addresses a large unmet clinical need and research gap related to reducing recurrent wheeze in infants post-hospitalisation for bronchiolitis. If our hypothesis is correct, this study may lead to an implementable intervention to improve health outcomes by reducing recurrent wheeze episodes in infants and young children. Reductions in recurrent wheeze might also reduce the incidence of childhood asthma and improve the lung health trajectories of children hospitalised with severe bronchiolitis.

papers.title: Design and Fabrication of Ag Nanoparticles and Plasma Hybrid Polymer Thin Films for the New LSPR Sensor Application
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Enabling detection of target molecules at low concentration is a key feature in localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) biosensors, which utilizes the remarkable optical properties of gold based metal nanoparticles (NPs). For a schematic studies, we here propose and demonstrate an approach on a low‐cost Ag‐based LSPR platform that combines a nanostructured Ag layer formed from spin‐coated Ag ink and a plasma‐polymer dielectric overlayer (Me‐cyclohexane or Me‐cyclohexane+TEOS) deposited by plasma‐enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) on glass (or flexible polymer) substrates with different thickness layer and particle size. Rather than assuming ideal, monodisperse nanoparticles, the Ag layer is treated as an island/clustered nanostructure whose thickness (32 vs 50 nm) and surface roughness govern the optical response. Using p‐polarized readout, we observe a steeper concentration‐dependent intensity change for the 50 nm Ag nanostructure compared with the 32 nm sample when probing aqueous thioglycolic acid (TGA) and representative organic dyes. In addition, a theoretical calculation utilizing our experimental data carry out for making up some weakpoint especially on refractive index sensitivity (RIS) and figure of merit.

papers.title: Dsg2 truncation causes a severe intestinal epithelial barrier breakdown and alters microbiome and immune response
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) including Crohn’s disease (CD) are characterized by impaired intestinal epithelial barrier (IEB) function. Alterations in the desmosomal cadherin desmoglein 2 (Dsg2) have been linked to loss of IEB and intestinal inflammation in IBD. We investigated the pathogenic impact of a cytoplasmatic-truncating mutation in the desmosomal cadherin desmoglein 2 gene (DSG2) in an IBD patient. Genetic analysis of a CD patient revealed a likely pathogenic DSG2 mutation leading to a truncated protein lacking part of the intracellular domain. Generation of an enterocyte-specific mouse model to recapitulate the human mutation resulted in a lethal intestinal barrier defect which was evident in homozygous but not in heterozygous mice. In vitro, barrier defects correlated with changes in Dsg2 mobility and upregulation of pore-forming tight junction protein claudin-2. Organoids derived from heterozygous Dsg2 truncated mice exhibited increased epithelial susceptibility to proinflammatory cytokines. Bulk RNAseq followed by gene ontology analysis in homozygous mice revealed a skewed IL17/IL23 response overlapping with transcriptional changes in patients with CD. Furthermore, 16S rRNA sequencing revealed alterations in microbiome composition in animals that carried the Dsg2 truncation. In summary, a patient-derived mutation in the DSG2 gene causing cytoplasmic truncation in homozygous state induced a lethal intestinal barrier breakdown in mice paralleled by altered gut microbiota and intestinal immune response.

papers.title: Collagen-Based Tumor Spheroid Model for Investigating Tumor-Macrophage Interactions through Extracellular Matrix Remodeling
papers.abstract: Abstract Macrophages in the tumor microenvironment (TME) can constitute up to 50% of tumor mass and play a critical role in cancer cell proliferation, invasion, and metastasis. While their contribution to extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation through matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) has been explored, the role of other macrophage-derived factors in ECM remodeling and their impacts beyond degradation remain poorly understood. Here, we describe the development of a 3D collagen-based tumor spheroid model to investigate the impact of peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC)-derived macrophages on cancer cell-ECM and cancer cell-macrophage interactions within the TME. We observed that cancer cells stimulated PBMC-derived macrophages into an M2-like phenotype and that tumor spheroid conditioned macrophages (TSCMs) shifted cancer cell populations toward phenotypes with greater invasion distances and reduced circularity, indicative of increased malignancy. Such observations can be explained by macrophage-mediated ECM remodeling. Specifically, we demonstrate that TSCMs secreted a variety of soluble factors that are known to contribute to ECM remodeling. These processes collectively create a tumor-favoring environment by loosening the collagen matrix and aligning fibers that serve as invasion tracks for migrating tumor cells that facilitate cancer cell migration and invasion. This model provides a robust platform to study the interactions between cellular and non-cellular components in the TME and to identify the molecular mechanisms underlying cancer progression. These insights may aid in the development of novel therapeutic strategies targeting macrophagemediated processes in cancer.

papers.title: ATRX loss predicts poor outcomes and sensitizes to TEAD inhibition in soft tissue sarcomas
papers.abstract: ATRX is one of the most frequently altered genes in sarcoma and encodes an ATP-dependent chromatin remodeler implicated in maintaining heterochromatin. However, ATRX alterations have not been leveraged for sarcoma treatment. We observed loss of ATRX protein in 14% of soft tissue leiomyosarcoma (STLMS, n =127), 53% of uterine leiomyosarcoma (ULMS, n = 95), 37% of undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma (UPS, n = 82), and 8% of dedifferentiated liposarcoma (DDLPS, n = 84). ATRX loss was associated with significantly worse outcomes in ULMS, UPS, and DDLPS. ATRX knockout in sarcoma cells increased proliferation in cooperation with TP53 deletion, chromatin remodeling, and enrichment of PRDM4 and NFIX transcription factor motifs. PRDM4 and NFIX knockdown in ATRX -mutant sarcoma lines resulted in reduced proliferation and invasion, suggesting an epistatic relationship. Consistent with the known and re-demonstrated functional relationship between PRMD4 and YAP1, ATRX loss activated YAP1-TEAD signaling, and ATRX -deficient cells and sarcoma xenografts were more sensitive to the TEAD inhibitors VT103 and IAG933. Overall, our results identify ATRX loss as a prognostic factor of worse outcomes, implicate the ATRX-PRDM4-YAP1-TEAD axis as an underlying mechanism, and suggest use of TEAD inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy for ATRX -deficient sarcomas.

papers.title: Experimental and FEM Analysis of the Thermal Performance of Calcium Silicate Boards at High-Temperature Exposure
papers.abstract: Calcium silicate boards are widely used in passive fire protection due to their high-temperature stability and excellent thermal insulation properties. In this study, thermal performance under high-temperature exposure of three commercially available calcium-silicate-based boards with different compositions, densities, thicknesses, and thermal conductivities was experimentally evaluated and complemented by finite element modeling (FEM). The boards were characterized by X-ray fluorescence (XRF), X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) to investigate their composition, thermal stability, phase evolution, and microstructure. High-temperature tests were performed under severe thermal exposure, and temperature evolution on the unexposed surface was monitored. A one-dimensional FEM heat-transfer model employing effective thermophysical properties showed reasonable agreement with the experimental temperature profiles. Under equal-thickness conditions, Skamopro-300 exhibited the lowest unexposed-face temperature, mainly due to its substantially lower effective thermal conductivity, while Promatect-T and Naper-S showed comparatively similar thermal responses. The results demonstrate that combining experimental characterization with FEM provides an effective approach for comparing commercial calcium silicate fireboards and predicting their thermal performance under standardized geometrical conditions.

papers.title: Synthesis and characterisation of borate ester for brake fluid applications
papers.abstract: Abstract Brake fluids are indispensable for ensuring the safety and reliability of automotive braking systems. Despite the increasing adoption of electric vehicles and regenerative braking technologies, conventional hydraulic brake fluids remain critical due to their ability to deliver rapid response times and minimal stopping distances. Among commercial formulations, glycol and borate ester based fluids such as DOT4 are widely used; however, there is limited open-research on the systematic synthesis and detailed characterization of their constituent compounds. In this study, a borate ester was synthesized through the esterification of boric acid with triethylene glycol monomethyl ether (TEGMME) and subsequently char acterized using a suite of physicochemical and spectroscopic techniques. Key perfor mance parameters,including equilibrium reflux boiling point (ERBP), wet ERBP, pH, density, and viscosity,were measured to evaluate the ester’s suitability for brake fluid applications. FTIR and GC-MS analyses confirmed the intended molecular structure and highlighted the presence of higher molecular weight species compared to commercial DOT4 fluids, suggesting potential improvements in thermal stability and performance. The results demonstrate that the synthesized borate ester exhibits excellent thermal stability, favorable rheological properties, and compatibility with established brake fluid specifications. These findings provide valuable insights into the design of advanced brake fluid formulations and establish a foundation for future studies on long-term durability, corrosion resistance, and formulation optimization.

papers.title: Machine learning accurately identifies the fragmentomic signature for DNase1L3 impairment caused by homozygosity for the p.Arg206Cys variant
papers.abstract: DNase1L3 is an endonuclease that fragments DNA during apoptosis and digests DNA from microparticles in plasma, shaping key features of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and maintaining extracellular DNA homeostasis, a process implicated in autoimmunity. We previously showed that homozygosity for the common DNASE1L3 p.Arg206Cys (R206C) variant is associated with a characteristic fragmentomic phenotype and reduced performance of fragmentomics-based cfDNA assays. Here, we investigated whether this phenotype itself can be recognized directly from cfDNA sequencing data using machine learning, thereby avoiding reliance on error-prone genotype imputation. To address this, we re-analyzed low-coverage whole-genome cfDNA sequencing data from 129,676 Non-Invasive Prenatal Tests (NIPT) and validated R206C genotypes in a selection of 169 matching plasma samples. Multiple machine-learning classifiers and unsupervised dimensionality reduction were applied to genome-wide fragmentomic features to identify the R206C-associated fragmentomic phenotype and to evaluate the minimum sequencing input required for accurate prediction. Our models outperformed genotype imputation for the identification of R206C homozygotes. Accurate predictions could be obtained with as few as 1,000 sequenced cfDNA fragments, substantially below the amount of sequencing routinely generated for cfDNA assays. Unsupervised analysis revealed few samples that cluster with homozygotes lack the corresponding genotype, suggesting that similar fragmentomic alterations may also arise through other mechanisms. Conversely, longitudinal follow-up across subsequent pregnancies showed some genetically confirmed R206C homozygotes initially lacked the aberrant fragmentome, but developed it in subsequent pregnancies. These findings show that machine learning enables the accurate identification of the R206C homozygote signature. It thereby provides a practical approach to improve cfDNA-based diagnostics across clinical applications and may serve as a biomarker for future DNase1L3-targeted therapeutic studies. The observed discordance between genotype and fragmentomic signature suggests that several features associated with DNase1L3 dysfunction are not fully explained by the genotype alone.

papers.title: Strain-level variation in Proteus mirabilis chondroitin sulfate degradation kinetics and regulation by urea
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT To establish infection, uropathogens must overcome several host defenses, including the glycosaminoglycan (GAG) layer coating the apical surface of the bladder urothelium. GAGs are thought to protect against urinary tract infections (UTIs) by acting as a barrier to uropathogen adherence. However, the ability of uropathogens to degrade and utilize GAGs, and the contribution of these activities toward UTI progression, are largely unknown. We previously discovered that Proteus mirabilis, a common cause of catheter-associated UTI (CAUTI), degrades the GAG chondroitin sulfate (CS). In this study, we sought to define the kinetics and regulation of CS degradation by diverse urinary P. mirabilis strains. We found variation in CS degradation kinetics between P. mirabilis strains and media types. CS degradation in one isolate, Pm123, was repressed by urea, and this repression was dependent on P. mirabilis urease activity. Complementation of the Pm123 endolyase into urea-insensitive HI4320 resulted in a urea-sensitive CS degradation phenotype, suggesting functional differences between the Pm123 and HI4320 endolyases. Sequence alignment and structural modeling identified two unique mutations within the Pm123 endolyase that may contribute to urea sensitivity. Finally, unlike urea-insensitive P. mirabilis strains, loss of CS lyase activity had no effect on Pm123 virulence in a mouse CAUTI model. Our results suggest that the kinetics and regulation of CS degradation differ between P. mirabilis strains, and regulation by urea in some strains may reduce the contribution of CS degradation to urovirulence during murine CAUTI.

papers.title: YUV20K: a complexity-driven benchmark and trajectory-aware alignment model for video camouflaged object detection
papers.abstract: Abstract The development of video camouflaged object detection (VCOD) is currently constrained by the scarcity of challenging benchmarks and the lack of robustness of models in the face of erratic motion dynamics. Existing methods frequently encounter challenges related to motion-induced appearance instability and temporal feature misalignment, particularly in complex motion scenarios. To address the issue of data bottleneck, we present YUV20K, a pixel-level annotated, complexity-driven VCOD benchmark. It is composed of 24,295 annotated frames, which are organized into 91 scenes and 47 species. It focuses on challenging scenarios, including large displacement motion, camera motion, and four additional complex-motion scenarios. In terms of methodology, a novel framework is proposed, comprising two key modules: motion feature stabilization (MFS) and trajectory-aware alignment (TAA). The MFS module utilizes frame-agnostic semantic basis primitives to stabilize features, while the TAA module leverages trajectory-guided deformable sampling to ensure precise temporal alignment. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves strong performance on existing datasets and establishes a competitive baseline on the challenging YUV20K.

Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves strong performance on existing datasets and establishes a competitive baseline on the challenging YUV20K.

papers.title: In vitro culture and draft genome assembly of Monographella maydis predict a molecular driver of its sexual fitness in maize tar spot disease
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Tar Spot Complex (TSC) is a devastating foliar disease of maize that threatens global food security, causing yield losses of up to 50%. While the disease is initiated by Phyllachora maydis , the “fisheye” necrosis that intensifies disease severity is attributed to Monographella maydis . Historically, the precise role of M. maydis has remained elusive due to a lack of reliable in vitro culture systems and genomic resources. This study reports the first successful isolation and reproducible in vitro culture of M. maydis , identifying V8 agar as an optimal medium for mycelial growth and sporulation. Results Using PacBio long-read sequencing technology, we generated a high-quality 39.8 Mb genome assembly for M. maydis , predicting 10,228 protein coding genes, 227 non-coding RNAs, 175 tRNAs and 45 rRNAs. Functional annotation identified a diverse repertoire of secreted proteins, likely involved in the tar spot disease pathosystem. Phylogenomic analysis confirmed that M. maydis is distinct from P. maydis , supporting a synergistic rather than evolutionary relationship between the two fungi. Furthermore, the identification of a conserved adenosine deaminase-acting-on-tRNA residue (H352) suggests potential for A-to-I RNA editing during sexual reproduction. Finally, we report the use of ITS1 and ITS4 primer pair for successful detection of M. maydis from infected leaf tissues. Conclusion This study establishes the first robust in vitro culture system and high-quality reference genome for Monographella maydis , providing foundational resources for investigating its biology and role in the tar spot disease complex. These genomic and molecular tools will facilitate future studies on fungal pathogenicity, host–pathogen interactions, and the development of improved disease management strategies.

papers.title: ConvNeXt ‐ FD : Fractal Dimension‐Regularized ConvNeXt for Robust Biomedical Image Segmentation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Biomedical image segmentation is a critical task in medical diagnosis and treatment planning, enabling precise delineation of anatomical structures and pathological regions. Despite significant advancements, challenges persist due to the inherent variability, noise and complex morphology present in diverse medical imaging modalities. This paper introduces ConvNeXt‐FD, a novel deep learning architecture for robust biomedical image segmentation, built upon a U‐Net‐like encoder‐decoder framework leveraging the powerful ConvNeXt backbone. Our approach integrates a hybrid loss function combining the Dice coefficient with a boundary‐aware regularization term inspired by a differentiable formulation of fractal dimension, designed to enhance the model's sensitivity to object boundaries and shape fidelity. We rigorously evaluate ConvNeXt‐FD across six distinct biomedical datasets: BUSI (breast ultrasound images), DDTI (thyroid ultrasound images), FluoCells (fluorescent cell images), IDRiD (diabetic retinopathy images for optic disc segmentation), ISIC2018 (skin lesion images) and MoNuSeg (nuclei segmentation). Experimental results demonstrate that ConvNeXt‐FD, particularly when initialized with ImageNet pre‐trained weights, achieves competitive and often superior performance compared to existing state‐of‐the‐art methods across various metrics, including Dice, Jaccard, Accuracy, Sensitivity, Specificity and False Positive Rate. The integration of ConvNeXt as a strong encoder, coupled with the boundary‐aware regularization, proves effective in capturing both high‐level semantic features and fine‐grained boundary details, leading to more accurate and reliable segmentations in challenging biomedical contexts.

papers.title: From K-snack to copolymer: conversion of silkworm pupa oil into poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyhexanoate) by engineered Cupriavidus necator H16
papers.abstract: Abstract Silkworm pupae are continuously generated as a major byproduct of the silk industry and have long been consumed as inexpensive, high-energy snacks in Korea. However, consumer acceptance has become increasingly variable due to their distinctive appearance and odor. Gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) analysis revealed that silkworm pupa oil (SPO) consists of approximately 54% oleic acid, 29% linoleic acid, 17% palmitic acid, and minor amounts of cyclopropane fatty acids. Based on this composition, this study evaluated the feasibility of producing poly(3-hydroxybutyrate- co -3-hydroxyhexanoate) [P(3HB- co -3HHx)] using engineered Cupriavidus necator H16 with SPO as a sustainable substrate. Compared with other carbon sources, SPO supported comparable growth and polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) content, which was 2.64-fold higher than fructose and 1.42-fold higher than bean oil in flask cultures, demonstrating its potential as an efficient substrate. Supplementation with 1.0% fructose as an auxiliary carbon source further increased dry cell weight (DCW) and total PHA accumulation by up to 20%. To improve emulsification, various emulsifiers were screened, and Tween 20 enhanced DCW and PHA yield by 1.4-fold and 1.55-fold, respectively. The resulting film exhibited a tensile strength of 6.0 ± 0.6 MPa and an elongation at break of 53.4 ± 4.6%, and showed approximately 90% degradation after 7 days by Microbulbifer sp. SOL66. Overall, this study demonstrates that SPO is a promising and sustainable carbon source for PHA production, highlighting the valorization of silk industry byproducts into high-value biopolymeric materials.

papers.title: Hirshfeld Surface Analysis, DFT Calculations, Development by 3² Factorial Design, and Evaluation for Solubility and Anticancer Activity of Neratinib–3-Hydroxybenzoic Acid Co-Crystals
papers.abstract: Abstract Objectives Neratinib, a pan-HER tyrosine kinase inhibitor for HER2-positive breast cancer, suffers from extremely poor aqueous solubility (< 0.002 mg/mL), severely limiting oral bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy. This study aimed to develop and optimize neratinib cocrystals using rational co-former selection and factorial design to enhance solubility, dissolution, and anticancer activity. Methods Five potential co-formers were screened at 3 molar ratios (1:1, 1:2, 1:3) using SynthonDock software. Electronic properties and interaction energetics were characterized using density functional theory (DFT) calculations at B3LYP/6-31G(d,p) level. Neratinib–3-hydroxybenzoic acid cocrystals were prepared by solvent evaporation and optimized in 3 2 factorial design using the concentration of co-former (24.8–74.4 mg) and stirring time (30–90 min) as independent variables. The PXRD, FTIR, DSC, SEM and Hirshfeld surface studies were carried out to characterize the compounds. MTT assay was used to evaluate in vitro cytotoxicity against SK-BR-3 cells. Results 3-Hydroxybenzoic acid showed the best binding energy (− 10.05 kcal/mol with a ratio of 1:3) and highest co-crystal score (90.5). Increased reactivity was established using density functional theory (DFT) with the calculation showing diminished HOMO–LUMO gap (0.4324 eV vs 3.3072 eV for pure drug). The 12.4-fold solubility enhancement (0.112 mg/mL vs 0.009 mg/mL) and 4.6 times better dissolution (84.6% vs 18.4% at 60 min) was reached using the third batch PF9 (74.4 mg of 3-hydroxybenzoic acid, 90 minutes.) Cytotoxicity studies showed enhanced anticancer activity (IC 50 = 18.46 µg/mL vs 24.18 µg/mL for pure neratinib) toward HER2-positive breast cancer cells. Conclusion The optimized neratinib–3-hydroxybenzoic acid cocrystal is a clinically relevant pharmaceutical approach to enhance oral bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy in HER2-positive breast cancer for subsequent biological exploration in vivo.

papers.title: Effects of tablet crushing methods on solid-state properties, dissolution behavior, and dispensability of acetaminophen tablets
papers.journal: Journal of Pharmaceutical Health Care and Sciences
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose In clinical practice, tablets are often crushed and administered to patients with dysphagia or children, typically using a mortar and pestle, tablet crusher, or other methods of administration. Clinical tablet crushing may alter the physicochemical properties of drugs; however, the effects of crushing methods on pharmaceutical quality remain unclear. This study aimed to compare three crushing methods available to pharmacists, namely, a mortar and pestle, a tablet crusher, and an oscillatory ball mill (OBM), using the same acetaminophen (AA) tablets, and to relate the resulting solid-state properties to dissolution and to the loss of powder during automatic dividing and packaging, which determines the accuracy of the dispensed dose. Methods We evaluated the physicochemical properties of the crushed samples, including particle size distribution, SEM, PXRD, DSC, FTIR, dissolution, flowability, and dispensability. Results All crushing methods reduced the crystallinity, with OBM causing the greatest solid-state alteration. In contrast, the tablet crusher produced relatively fine particles and showed the most rapid initial dissolution under the experimental conditions. The weight loss during dividing and packaging was 1.0–3.3% with a V-shaped powder dispensing machine under all crushing conditions, whereas with a rotary disk-type machine, it reached 10.0% (tablet crusher, 5 min) and 8.5% (OBM, 5 min). Conclusion The crushing method and crushing time influenced the solid-state properties, dissolution, and packaging loss of AA tablets. No single method was superior in all respects; the method and crushing time should be selected according to the packaging machine used, and prolonged grinding with the OBM should be avoided.

papers.title: Preparation-dependent catalytic performance of magnetic MWCNT–Fe3O4 aerogels in nitroarene reduction by isopropanol-mediated transfer hydrogenation
papers.abstract: In this work, four types (A-D) of magnetic MWCNT–Fe 3 O 4 aerogel catalysts were synthesized using four different preparation methods through the incorporation of Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticles into a chitosan- or PVA-crosslinked carbon nanotube network and applied to the transfer hydrogenation of nitroarenes using isopropanol as a liquid organic hydrogen carrier (LOHC). The structure and properties of the prepared catalysts were characterized by FTIR, XRD, Raman spectroscopy, FESEM, EDS, BET, TGA, contact angle measurements, and VSM analysis. For the selected catalyst (D), the catalytic activity was evaluated for the reduction of nitrobenzene under a nitrogen atmosphere, and an aniline yield of 72% was obtained under the optimized conditions with 20 mg of catalyst, 3 equivalents of NaOH, and 5 mL of isopropanol under reflux conditions. The applicability of the catalytic system was further investigated using 24 nitroarene derivatives, affording moderate to good yields, particularly for halogen-substituted substrates. Furthermore, the catalyst could be readily separated from the reaction medium using an external magnet and reused for four consecutive cycles, exhibiting only a slight decrease in catalytic activity.

papers.title: Hosting displaced medical students in times of crisis: a multi-national qualitative study adapting the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research
papers.abstract: Catastrophic geopolitical conflicts increasingly disrupt the continuity of medical education worldwide, placing immense pressure on clinical training pipelines and forced migration student groups. While short-term, reactive, remote learning models exist, there is a profound lack of evidence-based implementation templates for medical schools within stable host nations to systematically host and integrate displaced clinical student cohorts mid-stream. This study explores the multi-level barriers and facilitators to hosting displaced medical students across diverse international learning environments, seeking to establish a model of educational sanctuary while adapting implementation science theory in crisis contexts. Employing a qualitative multi-site case study design guided by a critical realist ontology, this study analysed 66 semi-structured interviews with displaced Gazan medical students, hosting lecturers, clinical coordinators, and support staff across six national contexts, comprising five physical clinical hosting nations (the United Kingdom, Malaysia, Pakistan, South Africa, and Turkey) and one dedicated remote learning contingency context (Egypt). Transcribed data were analysed using Reflexive Thematic Analysis and mapped onto the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR). The analysis revealed that while restrictive immigration policies, clinical placement caps, and severe cultural distance represent substantial barriers, key facilitators include assessment considerations, flexible placement models, sanctuary institutional cultures, peer networks, and decentralized administrative trust. Strategic administrative approaches, such as considering the classification of displaced students as extended clinical elective visitors rather than full-time matriculants where permitted by relevant immigration, accreditation, institutional, and professional regulations, were perceived by institutional leaders to facilitate accommodating displaced cohorts within legal governance frameworks. This study demonstrates that public sector higher education institutions can act as vital global sanctuary networks to preserve clinical training pipelines. Crucially, the findings propose three exploratory, context-specific adaptations to the 2022 CFIR meta-framework for acute crisis settings: Agile Implementation Over Perfection within the Implementation Process domain, Protective Leadership Shielding within the Inner Setting domain, and Bidirectional Boundary Subversion at the Inner/Outer Setting interface. These exploratory, context-specific observations offer preliminary insights for adapting CFIR construct interpretations from stable clinical settings to dynamic public sector responses during complex humanitarian emergencies.

The analysis revealed that while restrictive immigration policies, clinical placement caps, and severe cultural distance represent substantial barriers, key facilitators include assessment considerations, flexible placement models, sanctuary institutional cultures, peer networks, and decentralized administrative trust. This study demonstrates that public sector higher education institutions can act as vital global sanctuary networks to preserve clinical training pipelines.

papers.title: Multiplexed Bioorthogonal Imaging through Affinity Hierarchies in a Supramolecular Host
papers.abstract: Abstract Bioorthogonal chemistry has transformed molecular imaging by enabling highly selective synthetic labeling of biomolecules in their native habitats. Despite its remarkable success, the chemical space available for multiplexed bioorthogonal imaging remains fundamentally constrained by the limited repertoire of mutually orthogonal reactions. Herein, we expand this chemical space by introducing affinity encoding, a bioorthogonal multiplexing strategy in which molecular identity is encoded through programmable differences in binding affinity rather than reaction orthogonality. Using the synthetic host cucurbit[7]uril (CB[7]), we establish a single-host, multiguest framework that enables dynamic and reconfigurable multiplexed imaging through affinity-programmed host–guest exchange. By exploiting the hierarchical binding affinities of structurally distinct guest molecules, we achieve selective fluorophore displacement, enabling fluorescence erasure from lower-affinity targets while preserving higher-affinity host–guest assemblies intact. Subsequent recomplexation of the liberated lower-affinity binding sites with a spectrally distinct CB[7]–fluorophore conjugate enables programmable signal reassignment for multiplexed imaging in cells as well as in live tissues. Moreover, affinity encoding operates orthogonally to established covalent bioorthogonal chemistries, enabling four-color multiplexed imaging by combining affinity- and reaction-based encoding. Collectively, our results establish affinity encoding as a new scaling dimension for bioorthogonal multiplexing, providing a dynamically reconfigurable framework for high-dimensional fluorescence imaging.

papers.title: Strength and network evolution of waste glass powder activated by rice husk ash-derived sodium silicate
papers.abstract: Abstract Under the condition of an approximately constant NaO equivalent, with waste glass powder as the sole precursor, rice husk ash-based sodium silicate combined with NaOH was used to prepare rice husk ash-based sodium silicate-activated glass powder cementitious materials (RAGP) with moduli of 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0. Compressive strength, XRD, FTIR, and XPS analyses were performed to characterize the strength development and silicon-oxygen network evolution at 7 d and 28 d. The results show that the 7 d compressive strength decreased from 31.4 MPa to 29.6 MPa as the modulus increased; at 28 d, RAGP-1.5 achieved the highest compressive strength of 39.6 MPa, corresponding to an increase of 31.1%. Compared with the raw glass powder, the centroid of the amorphous diffuse peak of the hardened RAGP shifted toward higher angles by 2.13°–2.33°, while the centroid difference among the different mix proportions did not exceed 0.19°, indicating that alkali activation altered the amorphous scattering environment of the glass powder without inducing a resolvable crystalline phase transformation. The main Si-O-T band of all specimens was located at 973–981 cm and did not exhibit a consistent shift with curing age. In addition, the bridging oxygen ratio at 7 d decreased from 55.38% to 50.40% as the modulus increased; at 28 d, the bridging oxygen ratio of RAGP-1.5 reached 63.25%, an increase of 10.47% relative to 7 d, consistent with the ranking of compressive strength. A higher NaOH proportion was favorable for early-age depolymerization of the glass network, whereas the later-age strength depended on the balance between continued glass dissolution and polycondensation of soluble silicon; within the present mix design range, the activator composition with a modulus of 1.5 yielded the highest 28 d compressive strength and the largest increment in bridging oxygen.
papers.summary: Abstract Under the condition of an approximately constant NaO equivalent, with waste glass powder as the sole precursor, rice husk ash-based sodium silicate combined with NaOH was used to prepare rice husk ash-based sodium silicate-activated glass powder cementitious materials (RAGP) with moduli of 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0. Compressive strength, XRD, FTIR, and XPS analyses were performed to characterize the strength development and silicon-oxygen network evolution at 7 d and 28 d. The results show that the 7 d compressive strength decreased from 31.4 MPa to 29.6 MPa as the modulus increased; at 28 d, RAGP-1.5 achieved the highest compressive strength of 39.6 MPa, corresponding to an increase of 31.1%.

papers.title: Efficient Long-Wavelength Through-Space Charge-Transfer Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence in Conformationally Adaptive Emitters without Conformational Locking
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Through-space charge-transfer thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TSCT-TADF) emitters often employ conformationally constrained donor–acceptor architectures to control through-space electronic coupling, particularly for long-wavelength emission. Here, we report conformationally adaptive orange-to-red TSCT-TADF emitters based on an S-shaped donor−π–acceptor−π–donor framework composed of phenoxazine donors, xanthene linkers, and a dibenzo[a,j]phenazine acceptor. Structural and NMR analyses reveal substantial conformational mobility, while systematic conformational searches and excited-state calculations identify thermally accessible conformers with distinct donor–acceptor geometries and excited-state characteristics. Comparative studies with reference compounds and fragment-resolved transition-density analysis show that the xanthene linker primarily acts as a conformational regulator and that the low-energy CT states have predominant TSCT character with only minor linker involvement. Temperature-dependent early-time photoluminescence measurements reveal continuous spectral relaxation in fluid toluene that slows upon cooling and is absent in rigid Zeonex and mCBP hosts, providing strong evidence for structural relaxation following photoexcitation within a pre-existing conformational ensemble. The emitters exhibit orange-to-red TADF with reverse intersystem crossing rates on the order of 105–106 s–1. Organic light-emitting diodes employing these emitters show electroluminescence at 598–624 nm, external quantum efficiencies up to 14.9%, and limited efficiency roll-off over a broad luminance range. These results demonstrate that efficient long-wavelength TSCT-TADF can be realized without permanent conformational locking and establish a framework for understanding the interplay between ground-state conformational heterogeneity and excited-state structural relaxation.

papers.title: Twisting the pseudo–magnetic field lattice in periodically strained graphene
papers.abstract: Periodic deformations flatten electronic bands of graphene which could host strongly correlated electrons similar to those observed in twisted graphene bilayers. The most spectacular effects of strong correlations like superconductivity or magnetism have however not yet been observed despite several experimental attempts. Here, we use tight-binding calculations to investigate the effect of twisting the periodic strain lattice with respect to the atomic lattice. We find that misaligning the two lattices kills the band flattening. We also report on the universal behavior of the band flattening by periodic strain which is controlled by a single parameter, a pseudo-magnetic field flux. Our study strongly suggests that controlling the twist of the strain lattice is essential to unlock the potential of periodic strains in graphene.

papers.title: Experimental and nonlinear constitutive damage model for sandstones after high-temperature treatment
papers.journal: Bulletin of Engineering Geology and the Environment
papers.abstract: Abstract Understanding the changes in rock engineering properties after heating is vital, as high underground temperatures have contributed to disasters. Therefore, this study investigated the engineering properties of sandstone after high-temperature treatment to understand the thermo-mechanical behavior of these sandstones for long-term underground mine and tunneling safety and maintenance. Investigating the strength, damage, and failure characteristics of rock under unconfined compressive testing, X-ray diffraction, and scanning electron microscopy is crucial to mitigating underground rock hazards. The results show that temperature played a significant role in the evolution of compressive strength, deformation modulus, and damage variable in the sandstones. The peak strength of the sandstones decreases with increasing temperature, while the damage variables increase. In addition, based on Lemaître’s strain equivalence principle, a nonlinear constitutive model for sandstone was developed for high-temperature conditions. Results obtained under different high-temperature conditions were used to validate the model. The proposed model shows excellent agreement with the experimental results across all temperatures ( R 2 > 0.998) and outperforms selected existing models in fitting the present dataset.

papers.title: Using midfacial CT to design patient-matched, 3D printed nasal splints: a retrospective study
papers.abstract: Background: Skin cancers on the nose are common in Australia and are often reconstructed with a full-thickness skin graft. Skin grafts on the nasal alar are prone to failure. We hypothesise that this is due to the mobility of the alar and we believe that patient-matched intranasal splints have the potential to support the alar during graft healing and improve graft take. This study aims to characterise nasal morphology in southeast Queenslanders affected by skin cancers, define the input modalities required to design patient-matched intranasal splints, and establish the workflow for the manufacture of these splints. Methods: A series of 200 computed tomography (CT) scans were investigated and segmented into 3D models. They were then classified into groups according to nostril shape using a modified system derived from the literature. Statistical shape modelling was applied to each group to generate a design envelope of noses representative of our cohort. Results: Participants were aged 16–97 years. A design envelope of six nose shapes was generated. These six nose shapes will be used as a basis to design and create patient-matched intranasal splints that will stabilise the nasal alar with the intention of improving graft take. Conclusion: This study demonstrates that statistical shape models can be generated for a given nasal morphology known to be common in a target population. The results of this study will be used to support a future randomised controlled trial testing the safety, tolerability and efficacy of these nasal splints.

papers.title: Why the educational disadvantage policy fails. A case study of the Netherlands
papers.abstract: For over half a century, the Dutch Ministry of Education has been implementing policies aimed at combating educational disadvantages linked to the socio-economic circumstances in which children grow up. The focus is on all children who meet the relevant disadvantage criteria, whether they have developmental delays or not. This policy has by now cost around forty billion euros. Unfortunately, student performance continues to decline. This in-depth literature review describes the manner in which those billions are disbursed to school boards and municipalities, and the way in which they are deployed. In view of this failure of a group-oriented approach, a plea is made for an individual-oriented approach. In contrast to the preventive group approach, the individual-centered approach focuses on the actual developmental delays of individual children and is more remedial in nature.

papers.title: Trusted Intelligent Sensing for Sport–Medicine Integrated Physical Activity Interventions: A Framework and Research Agenda
papers.journal: Journal of Public Health and Preventive Medicine
papers.abstract: Physical inactivity is among the largest modifiable contributors to the global burden of cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, and several cancers, yet one in three adults worldwide still does not meet minimum activity recommendations (Guthold et al., 2024). Sports promotion and medical care have historically operated as separate systems: the sports sector delivers activity opportunities without clinical follow-up, while the medical sector treats the consequences of inactivity without prescribing exercise as a therapy. “Sport–medicine integration” — the deliberate coupling of physical-activity promotion with clinical and public-health pathways — is now a stated policy goal, but its delivery has been limited by the lack of trustworthy measurement and feedback between the two sectors. This Perspective argues that high-assurance intelligent sensing — wearable inertial and photoplethysmographic sensors, on-device activity recognition, and privacy-preserving data pipelines — is the missing technical layer that can make sport–medicine integration operable. We define six requirements for “high assurance”: clinical-grade accuracy across populations, transparent and human-auditable algorithms, privacy-preserving data handling, fairness across demographic groups, regulatory validity, and a closed-loop feedback path back to both the user and the clinician. We propose a four-layer framework — sensing, assurance, prescription, and feedback — and map the current evidence against it. The field’s priority is not more activity trackers but prospective, population-validated intervention trials in which sensing data drive tailored exercise prescriptions and are evaluated against health outcomes rather than step counts alone.

papers.title: Structure-function analyses of the O2-dependent dimer-monomer transition in the FNR transcription factor
papers.journal: JBIC Journal of Biological Inorganic Chemistry
papers.abstract: About 2,5 billion years ago, oxygenic photosynthesis favored the evolution of gene expression regulatory strategies to respire atmospheric O 2 in many anaerobic organisms. One such strategy was the evolution of the Fumarate Nitrate Reduction (FNR) regulator from a cAMP-binding transcription factor. The activity of FNR is regulated by a [Fe 4 S 4 ] cluster-dependent dimer-monomer transition. The dimeric FNR responds to O 2 through cluster degradation, which causes monomerization and loss of binding to its palindromic DNA receptor sites. Despite extensive structural and functional characterization, the molecular mechanism underlying signal transmission from the cluster to the DNA-binding domain and the dimer interface remains unclear. Here, we used a series of specific variants to explore this process both functionally, through stopped-flow and in vivo activity tests, and structurally, by exposing FNR crystals to O 2 and three-dimensionally determining its effects. The emerging picture consists of three clearly interconnected major steps: cluster degradation, breaking of two intermolecular salt bridges, and bending and separation of the two dimerization α-helices. We also performed a preliminary analysis of FNRs belonging to different bacterial classes and concluded that their variable cysteine-based cluster coordination motifs might influence signal transmission.

We also performed a preliminary analysis of FNRs belonging to different bacterial classes and concluded that their variable cysteine-based cluster coordination motifs might influence signal transmission.

papers.title: From plasticization to anti-plasticization: the critical role of residual solvent and thermal history on CO2 transport in 6FDA polyimide membranes
papers.journal: Frontiers in Membrane Science and Technology
papers.abstract: This study investigates the profound impact of residual solvents and thermal history on the CO 2 /CH 4 and CO 2 /N 2 separation performance of 6FDA-based polyimide membranes by providing a comprehensive understanding of how solvent-polymer-penetrant interactions dictate macroscopic separation efficiency. Dense 6FDA-DAM membranes were cast using three solvent molecules with varying boiling points (NMP, DMF, and THF) and subjected to distinct annealing protocols (sub-boiling, supra-boiling, and near the glass transition temperature, T g ). Experimental evaluations underscore the persistent nature of solvent entrapment; achieving a completely solvent-free matrix is practically unattainable, as solvent molecules become structurally locked within the polymer chains depending on the evaporation kinetics. These trapped solvents act as plasticizers, expanding fractional free volume and increasing permeability at the expense of selectivity. Conversely, precise thermal treatment near T g significantly tightens polymer chain packing, effectively doubling CO 2 /CH 4 selectivity, with a considerable drop in CO 2 permeability, as the minute amount of remaining trapped solvent begins to act as an anti-plasticizer. To elucidate these macroscopic findings, molecular simulations were performed to capture the coupled effects of the residual solvent and CO 2 on rigid (6FDA-DAM) and flexible (6FDA-ODA) polyimide matrices. The computational models emphasize that structural alterations are driven by the combined presence of both CO 2 and the trapped solvent, rather than the isolated effect of the solvent. This reveals a direct competition between CO 2 and the solvent for preferential sorption sites, primarily nitrogen in the imide group and ether linkages. Furthermore, fractional free volume (FFV) analyses identified a critical transition threshold (1–2 wt% solvent content) where this combined interaction reverses the matrix behavior from synergistic plasticization to anti-plasticization with the decrease of residual solvent content. By detailing the dependence of gas transport properties on both specific solvent selection and thermal treatment, this dual-methodological work establishes a new fundamental perspective for optimizing the fabrication of high-performance polyimide membranes.

This reveals a direct competition between CO 2 and the solvent for preferential sorption sites, primarily nitrogen in the imide group and ether linkages. By detailing the dependence of gas transport properties on both specific solvent selection and thermal treatment, this dual-methodological work establishes a new fundamental perspective for optimizing the fabrication of high-performance polyimide membranes.

papers.title: From Pure Inorganic to Hybrid Structure: Rational Design and Knoevenagel Reaction Performance of Polyoxovanadate Catalysts
papers.abstract: Abstract The type of transition-metal center and bound organic ligands serve as critical regulators for the catalytic properties of polyoxovanadate (POV) clusters in organic transformations. Herein, a series of pure inorganic POVs with distinct transition-metal ions, namely [M(H2O)4][β-VIV14Sb8O40(OH)2(H2O)]·6H2O (M = Co (1), Ni (2), Zn (3)) were hydrothermally synthesized. By further introducing the 5,5′-mbpy (5,5′-dimethyl-2,2′-dipyridyl) organic ligand into the identical metal centers, corresponding inorganic-organic hybrid POVs [M(5,5′-mbpy)2(H2O)]2[β-VIV14Sb8O42(H2O)]·3H2O (M = Co (4), Ni (5), Zn (6)) were successfully synthesized. These compounds were characterized by infrared spectroscopy (IR), single crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and thermogravimetric analysis (TG). Their catalytic activities were systematically evaluated for the Knoevenagel condensation of benzaldehyde and malononitrile. Compound 4 demonstrated superior catalytic performance, affording nearly quantitative benzaldehyde conversion (>99%) with >99% selectivity within 90 min at room temperature. Five successive recycling experiments confirmed its excellent reusability and cycling stability. This work demonstrates that both transition-metal identity and organic-ligand incorporation can effectively tune the catalytic efficiency and structural robustness of POV clusters in Knoevenagel condensation.
