papers.title: Transformer architectures scaling laws and in context learning in foundation models
papers.abstract: Transformers have evolved from a sequence-to-sequence architecture for machine translation into a general computational framework underlying large language, vision, speech, multimodal, scientific, and decision-making systems. This critical narrative review synthesizes the field along four connected axes: architectural evolution and attention efficiency; neural scaling laws across parameters, data, compute, and inference-time computation; mechanisms and evaluation debates surrounding in-context learning and emergent reasoning; and the expansion of Transformer systems across modalities and application domains. We move beyond a paper-by-paper chronology by comparing architectural choices under explicit constraints of context length, memory bandwidth, training compute, inference latency, data availability, and task structure. Particular attention is given to sparse and IO-aware attention, multi-query and grouped-query attention, mixture-of-experts routing, multimodal integration, and Transformer–state-space hybrids. We reconcile the Kaplan and Chinchilla scaling formulations with later replication and inference-aware analyses, and distinguish training-time scaling from test-time compute scaling. For in-context learning, we synthesize evidence concerning induction heads, implicit task inference, pre-training data composition, and the debate over metric-dependent emergence. The review also broadens application coverage to speech and audio processing, UAVs and autonomous systems, cybersecurity and intrusion detection, communications and networking, and time-series forecasting, in addition to scientific discovery, software engineering, healthcare, and education. Quantitative comparison tables are restricted to studies reporting results on common datasets and metrics, while explicitly noting differences in training protocols and computational budgets. We conclude that progress is increasingly determined not by parameter count alone, but by joint optimization of architecture, data quality, inference compute, hardware efficiency, and deployment constraints.

papers.title: Inflammatory and extracellular matrix pathways in the association between heart failure and lung cancer risk
papers.abstract: Aims Heart failure (HF) has been associated with an increased risk of incident lung cancer (LC), but the molecular mechanisms underlying this association beyond shared risk factors remain poorly characterised. This study aimed to investigate whether plasma protein-derived biological pathway activities are associated with mediation of the HF–LC association in a large, population-based cohort. Methods and results We conducted a retrospective analysis of 438,892 UK Biobank participants. Time-varying Cox proportional hazards models assessed the association between HF and incident LC. A sex-stratified multiple mediation analysis was performed in the proteomic subcohort ( n = 40,988), using pathway activity scores derived from 2,921 plasma proteins. Over a median follow-up of 13.1 years, HF was significantly associated with an increased risk of LC in both men (HR 1.32; 95% CI 1.11–1.56) and women (HR 1.39; 95% CI 1.09–1.76), with significant effect modification by sex ( P for interaction <0.001). In the prevalent-HF mediation cohort, inflammatory and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling pathways collectively accounted for 56.4% of the total effect in men and 41.1% in women. Key mediating pathways included collagen degradation and innate immune activation via Toll-like receptors in men, and inflammatory cytokine signalling and TNF receptor binding in women. Conclusion HF is associated with an increased risk of developing LC. This association is statistically consistent with mediation by systemic inflammatory and ECM remodelling pathways, with notable sex-specific differences. These findings support the hypothesis that HF is associated with a systemic milieu consistent with a pro-tumorigenic state, providing exploratory mechanistic insight into reverse cardio-oncology.

Methods and results We conducted a retrospective analysis of 438,892 UK Biobank participants.

papers.title: Exploratory Flexural and Compressive Response of Hot-Pressed Composites Made from Source-Sorted Recycled Plastic and Eucalyptus Wood Particles
papers.abstract: This exploratory study investigated hot-pressed composites prepared from source-sorted, nominally HDPE-designated post-consumer plastic and screened Eucalyptus wood-processing particles at 0, 10, 20, and 30 wt.% wood content. Polymer identity was assigned from collection/sorting records, not confirmed by spectroscopy or thermal analysis. Three flexural subspecimens were sectioned from one plate for each composition; independent compression-batch replication was not established. The recorded peak nominal flexural stress decreased from 23.30 ± 1.55 MPa for the unfilled control to 21.92 ± 1.73, 18.30 ± 2.78, and 11.81 ± 0.52 MPa, respectively. Peak nominal compressive stresses were 15.78 ± 1.55, 9.16 ± 0.56, 13.05 ± 2.78, and 11.48 ± 0.91 MPa, giving a non-monotonic descriptive pattern. Relative to the unfilled control, the 10 wt.% mixture retained 94.1% of peak nominal flexural stress and 58.0% of peak nominal compressive stress; the corresponding values at 20 wt.% were 78.5% and 82.7%. A weighting sensitivity analysis shows that the preferred composition depends on the relative importance of the two loading modes. Original modulus estimates based on a fixed 10–20 N load window were excluded from engineering conclusions. The measurements describe within-campaign, specimen-level performance and do not establish standardized strength, batch reproducibility, or product suitability.

papers.title: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy plus PD-1 blockade for locally advanced gastric cancer: Clinical outcomes and CD103+CD8+ T cells as a response-associated biomarker
papers.abstract: Introduction Programmed death-1 (PD-1) inhibitors combined with chemotherapy are established for advanced gastric cancer, but their role in the neoadjuvant treatment of locally advanced gastric cancer (LAGC) remains incompletely defined. Biomarkers associated with pathological response are also needed to improve patient stratification. Methods This retrospective cohort included 144 patients with LAGC who received neoadjuvant chemotherapy plus a PD-1 inhibitor followed by curative-intent surgery between June 2021 and December 2025. Pathological and radiographic responses, survival, surgical outcomes, and treatment-related adverse events were evaluated. Multiplex immunofluorescence was performed in paired tumor specimens from an exploratory subset of 36 sintilimab-treated patients. Multivariable logistic and Cox regression analyses were used to assess factors associated with pathological response and survival. Results The pathological complete response (pCR) and major pathological response (MPR) rates were 18.0% and 36.0%, respectively, and the R0 resection rate was 95.0%. The 1-year overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) rates were 86.9% and 77.4%, respectively. Grade 1–2 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 91.7% of patients and grade 3 events in 30.6%; no grade 4 or 5 events occurred. PD-L1 CPS ≥1 was independently associated with a higher likelihood of MPR (adjusted OR for non-MPR, 0.31; 95% CI, 0.13–0.70; P = 0.006), but was not independently associated with OS or DFS. Baseline intratumoral CD103 + CD8 + T-cell density was numerically higher in responders than in non-responders, but this difference was not significant after false discovery rate correction (adjusted P = 0.0662). Paired analyses showed a greater treatment-associated increase in CD103 + CD8 + T-cell density among responders, whereas no statistically significant difference in CD103 - CD8 + T-cell density was observed between response groups. Conclusion In this retrospective surgical cohort, neoadjuvant chemotherapy plus PD-1 blockade was associated with encouraging pathological response rates, a high R0 resection rate, and manageable toxicity. Higher PD-L1 expression was associated with pathological response but not survival. Exploratory paired-tissue findings suggest that treatment-associated increases in intratumoral CD103 + CD8 + T-cell density may represent a response-associated immune feature requiring prospective validation.

papers.title: HER2 expression and clinicopathological correlates across immunohistochemical phenotypes of urothelial carcinoma: a retrospective single-center study
papers.abstract: Background Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is a treatment target in urothelial carcinoma (UC), but the features of tumors with HER2 overexpression are not well defined. This study evaluated the clinicopathological factors related to HER2 expression and compared its frequency and tumor characteristics among immunohistochemical (IHC) phenotypes. Methods This retrospective study enrolled 280 patients with pathologically confirmed UC at our institution between 2021 and 2025. Tumor sections were evaluated for HER2, CK5/6, and CK20 expression by IHC. Tumors were grouped as HER2 IHC 0/1 + or 2+/3+, and were classified as luminal, basal, double-positive, or double-negative based on CK5/6 and CK20 expression. Factors related to IHC 2+/3 + expression were assessed by univariable and multivariable logistic regression. Results HER2 IHC 2+/3 + staining was observed in 191 tumors (68.2%). HER2 IHC 2+/3 + was associated with age > 60 years, high-grade histology, abnormal p53 expression, Ki-67 index ≥ 30%, and IHC phenotypes (all P < 0.05). In multivariate analysis, luminal type (OR=3.848, P < 0.001), double-positive type (OR=3.429, P = 0.021), and age > 60 years (OR=1.888, P = 0.033) remained independently associated with HER2 IHC 2+/3 + . Conclusions HER2 IHC 2+/3 + expression was common in UC and was associated with age, histologic grade, Ki-67 index, abnormal p53 expression and IHC phenotypes. These findings describe differences in HER2 expression across CK5/6- and CK20-defined IHC phenotypes.
papers.summary: Background Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is a treatment target in urothelial carcinoma (UC), but the features of tumors with HER2 overexpression are not well defined. Tumor sections were evaluated for HER2, CK5/6, and CK20 expression by IHC. Results HER2 IHC 2+/3 + staining was observed in 191 tumors (68.2%).

papers.title: Effects of Cooling Rate and Fiber Loading on the Non‐Isothermal Crystallization of Short‐Carbon‐Fiber‐Reinforced PEEK
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The non‐isothermal crystallization behavior of short‐carbon‐fiber‐reinforced PEEK (SCF/PEEK, 0–30 wt%) was investigated by differential scanning calorimetry at cooling rates of 5–40°C/min and analyzed using the Jeziorny‐modified Avrami model. Crystallinity decreased monotonically with both increasing cooling rate and SCF content, falling from 36.5% to 18.1% for the 30 wt% composite at the highest cooling rate. The Avrami exponent n declined from 3.27 (neat PEEK, 5°C/min) to 2.09 (30 wt% SCF, 40°C/min), indicating increasingly restricted crystal development under faster cooling and higher fiber loading. SEM revealed diminishing matrix continuity and reduced inter‐fiber spacing at high SCF loadings, suggesting geometrical confinement of the PEEK matrix. Although fiber surfaces may locally promote heterogeneous nucleation, the present results provide no direct evidence that SCF increases the overall crystallinity of the matrix; the suppression of crystallization is therefore attributed primarily to restricted crystal development under rapid cooling and high fiber loading. These findings provide practical implications for fused deposition modeling (FDM) of SCF/PEEK components, where processing‐related cooling conditions strongly influence the crystallinity of the printed matrix.

papers.title: An integrated computational framework for thermomechanical assessment of ball grid array layouts in a 3D semiconductor package using COMSOL and ANSYS
papers.abstract: Ball Grid Array (BGA) topology affects the thermomechanical reliability of advanced 3D semiconductor packages, specifically regarding heat transfer paths, stress distributions, and package deformation, yet conventional single-response metrics do not account for interconnect utilization and design trade-offs. This study develops an integrated computational framework combining topology-optimized hybrid meshing to achieve mesh independence, benchmark model reconstruction, cross-platform verification between COMSOL Multiphysics and Ansys Mechanical to ensure numerical consistency, and coupled Thermomechanical Analysis (TMA) across nine selected BGA configurations ( P 1 – P 9 ). For these configurations investigated under relatively high heat generation rates, COMSOL Multiphysics and Ansys Mechanical show relative differences below approximately 3.5%. Interconnect-utilization-aware performance indices are introduced by incorporating the number of BGA solder joints into conventional thermomechanical response quantities. Although higher BGA densities generally improve conventional thermal and structural performance, their advantages diminish when interconnect utilization is considered. Within this case study, intermediate layouts reduce the proposed performance indices by up to 53% and 31%, while the corresponding conventional thermomechanical responses deteriorate by only 5.2% and 1.8%, respectively. The proposed framework supports the comparison of the investigated BGA layouts in terms of thermomechanical performance and interconnect utilization, providing a basis for future multi-objective optimization of heterogeneous semiconductor packages.

papers.title: Prevalence of cardiometabolic multimorbidity and associated factors among adults in Türkiye
papers.abstract: Background: Cardiometabolic diseases remain a major public health problem in Türkiye, yet national evidence on them is limited. Aim: To determine the prevalence of cardiometabolic multimorbidity and its associated factors among adults aged ≥40 years in Türkiye. Methods: We collected data on cardiometabolic multimorbidity among 9525 individuals aged ≥40 years from the 2019 Türkiye Health Survey. We analysed the data using SPSS version 24.0, using chi-square test to assess the association between categorical variables and cardiometabolic multimorbidity, and univariable and multivariable logistic regression to evaluate the strength of associations between the independent variables and cardiometabolic multimorbidity. P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results: The prevalence of cardiometabolic multimorbidity was 23.4%. Being female (aOR = 1.52, 95% CI: 1.34–1.72), older age (≥70 years; aOR = 7.97, 95% CI: 6.64–9.57), having a higher body mass index (aOR = 1.09, 95% CI: 1.07–1.10), and alcohol use (aOR = 1.24, 95% CI: 1.08–1.34) were associated with increased odds of cardiometabolic multimorbidity. Physical activity (aOR = 0.71, 95% CI: 0.63–0.80) and medium (aOR = 0.76, 95% CI: 0.63–0.90) or high education levels (aOR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.67–0.98) were protective factors. Conclusion: The high prevalence of cardiometabolic multimorbidity indicates the need for targeted strategies to prevent and better manage cardiometabolic health among this population of adults in Türkiye.

papers.title: Quantum Information Dynamics of the Source and the Placed Source: Lindblad Dynamical Scission, Von Neumann Entropy Production, and Landauer-Bounded Quantum-Classical Transduction
papers.abstract: The endogenous source and the placed source are formulated as complementary finite quantum preparation models on a chemical-label space and a registry space of $l-1$ bits. A rank-one-jump Lindblad lift of an explicit fifteen-state reaction--transport network reproduces its classical populations and gives exact off-diagonal damping rates. We characterize the persistent coherence between absorbing sinks, prove scission when the initial cross-sink block vanishes, and obtain an all-state trace-norm bound after adding explicit sector monitoring. For the stated benchmark rates, bulk-start retention is $(10000/10001)^2$. Registry randomization is implemented by complete dephasing followed by uniform flips, equivalently the replacement channel $A\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}(A)I/2^{l-1}$; an $X$-only twirl retains classical information. The controlled family of independent-contact Gibbs states has fidelity $p^{l-1}$ and classical Holevo capacity $(l-1)[1-H_2(1-p)]$, whereas each fixed-target replacement channel has zero input capacity. Under equal degenerate endpoint Hamiltonians and complete isothermal resource accounting, preparation obeys $W\ge k_BT[(l-1)\ln2-S(\rho)]$. We derive the nonnegative bias threshold for a prescribed fidelity and separate it from the total preparation work. The unitary agreement transform makes the registry a noiseless subsystem under collective site flips; longitudinal phase noise instead preserves only its diagonal pointer algebra. An independent registry bit-flip model gives a distinct transit-survival formula. Finite verification and scoped Lean certificates support the algebraic construction, while calibrated rates, differential Stark response, bath correlations and gate-cycle energetics define the requirements for a molecular realization.

papers.title: Synthesis of a nitrogen rich covalent organic polymer for naproxen adsorption from aqueous solutions
papers.abstract: The synthesis of a novel nitrogen-rich covalent organic polymer (NR-COP, 7) via Schiff-base condensation and its application for naproxen (NPX) removal from aqueous solutions are reported. The synthesized polymer was characterized using FT-IR, XRD, SEM, EDS, TEM, TGA, and BET analyses. The effects of pH (3–10), contact time (10–150 min), adsorbent dosage (5–15 mg), initial NPX concentration (10–100 mg/L), and temperature (25–45 °C) on adsorption performance were systematically investigated. The optimal conditions were identified as pH 6, 25 °C, a contact time of 90 min, an adsorbent dosage of 10 mg, and an initial NPX concentration of 40 mg/L. Adsorption equilibrium data were better fitted by the Langmuir model than by the Freundlich model, with an R² value of 0.9947. The adsorption kinetics followed the pseudo-second-order model, yielding a maximum adsorption capacity of 135.14 mg/g. Thermodynamic analysis indicated that NPX adsorption onto NR-COP (7) is spontaneous and exothermic. The combination of favorable adsorption capacity, thermal stability, and reusability highlights the potential of this nitrogen-rich polymer as an effective adsorbent for NPX removal from aqueous media. Its nitrogen-containing functionalities may further contribute to adsorbate–adsorbent interactions, supporting its potential application in the treatment of pharmaceutical-contaminated water. .

papers.title: High tissue factor (CD142) expression identifies a poor-prognosis subgroup of esophageal and esophagogastric junction adenocarcinoma
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Tissue Factor (TF/CD142) is an emerging antibody–drug conjugate (ADC) target, but its prevalence, prognostic value and molecular context in adenocarcinoma of the esophagus (EAC) and esophagogastric junction (EGJ) remain uncharacterized. Methods TF immunohistochemistry was scored by H-score (0–300) on a tissue microarray of 1,120 resected EAC/EGJ adenocarcinomas (1996–2020); the 1,006 assessable primary tumors formed the analysis cohort. Tumors were graded TF-negative (≤ 10), TF-low (11–100) or TF-high (> 100) and related to clinicopathologic features, tissue compartment, neoadjuvant therapy, HER2, Claudin 18.2 (CLDN18.2), MET, mismatch-repair (MMR) status and overall survival. Primary tumors and lymph-node metastases were compared within patients. Results TF was positive in 486 of 1,006 tumors (48.3%) and high in 225 (22.4%). TF-positive tumors were more often pT3–4 ( p < 0.001) and node-positive ( p = 0.002), and TF grade agreed moderately between paired primary tumors and lymph-node metastases ( n = 247; κ 0.57 at H-score > 100) without a systematic shift ( p = 0.91). TF was independent of HER2 ( p = 0.80) and MMR status ( p = 0.14), inversely associated with CLDN18.2 (TF-high vs. TF-negative: 12.8% vs. 30.2%; p < 0.001) and positively with MET overexpression (8.6% vs. 1.0%; p < 0.001). Over a median follow-up of 67 months (749 patients, 428 deaths), the survival detriment was confined to TF-high tumors (median overall survival 19.3 vs. 36.8 and 42.2 months; p < 0.001). Adjusted for age, pT, nodal status and neoadjuvant therapy, TF-high remained adverse (HR 1.67, 95% CI 1.32–2.11; p < 0.001) whereas TF-low did not (HR 0.97; p = 0.83). The TF-high association held with TF as a continuous variable (HR 1.11 per 50 points; p < 0.001) and after adjustment for treatment era, margin, grade and lymphovascular invasion. TF positivity was similar in treatment-naïve and in residual post-neoadjuvant tumors ( p = 0.89), but TF-high concentrated in poorly regressed tumors (29.2% vs. 11.6%; trend p < 0.001). Conclusions TF is expressed in nearly half of EAC/EGJ adenocarcinomas and at high level in about one quarter, where it is independently associated with shorter overall survival. TF expression remains prevalent in residual tumors after neoadjuvant therapy and marks a compartment distinct from HER2 and CLDN18.2 and enriched for MET. TF-high is a candidate biomarker for prospective trials of TF-directed ADCs, in which its predictive value and the H-score > 100 threshold need testing.

papers.title: Formaldehyde-Free Melamine-Glutaraldehyde Resin Microspheres for Metal Ion Removal from PGME/PGMEA Photoresist Thinners
papers.abstract: Abstract Melamine-formaldehyde (MF) resin microspheres show great promise as high-performance adsorbents for the purification of wet electronic chemicals. However, their reliance on formaldehyde introduces severe toxicity risks and leads to free aldehyde leaching that contaminates the purification process. In this work, glutaraldehyde was employed to completely replace formaldehyde for the preparation of melamine resin microspheres via a facile suspension polymerization process. The preparation parameters (such as feed molar ratio, polymerization temperature, and the oil–water ratio) were systematically optimized to regulate the morphology, particle size, and specific surface area. The physicochemical properties of the as-prepared microspheres were comprehensively characterized via scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), nitrogen adsorption–desorption isotherms, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and swelling resistance tests. The results indicate that the optimized glutaraldehyde-cross-linked melamine resin microspheres exhibit a regular spherical morphology, a narrow particle size distribution, adequate thermal stability for engineering applications, and a low swelling ratio in wet electronic chemical media without leaching of free glutaraldehyde. The adsorption of Cu, Fe, and Ti ions in a propylene glycol methyl ether/propylene glycol methyl ether acetate (PGME/PGMEA) photoresist thinner was investigated via isotherm, kinetic, and cyclic reusability studies. The adsorption data are well fitted by the Langmuir–Freundlich isotherm and pseudo-second-order kinetic models, revealing a mixed monolayer-multilayer chemisorption mechanism. The maximum adsorption capacity for various ions ranged from 4405.21 to 5298.43 μg/g, and the microspheres maintained a decrease in adsorption efficiency of no more than 15.8% after five regeneration cycles. This work offers a green, scalable synthesis strategy and sheds light on the advanced purification of high-purity wet electronic chemicals.

papers.title: Hydrogen-Bond-Regulated PAN/PTFBZ Nanofibrous Composite Barriers for Flame-Resistant Thermal Runaway Protection
papers.abstract: Electrospun polymer barriers are attractive for lightweight thermal protection in compact lithium-ion battery (LIB) devices, but their limited flame resistance and structural stability under thermal abuse restrict their practical use. Herein, a hydrogen-bond-regulated nanofibrous composite barrier was developed by incorporating trifluoromethyl-modified benzoxazine (TFBZ)-derived components into a polyacrylonitrile (PAN) matrix. The benzoxazine-derived phenolic hydroxyl groups could interact with the nitrile groups of PAN through O-H···N≡C hydrogen bonding, contributing to improved interfacial compatibility and fibrous-network stabilization while retaining the processability of PAN. Thermogravimetric analysis showed that PAN/PTFBZ retained 96.1% of its mass at 300 °C, compared with 75.8% for pure PAN. Cone calorimetry showed that the total heat release and total smoke production were reduced by 64.9% and 45.1%, respectively, and the limiting oxygen index (LOI) increased from 18% to 31%. In battery-level thermal abuse tests, the time to complete thermal runaway (TR) increased from 1068.7 ± 14.6 s to 1884.7 ± 44.2 s, corresponding to 76.4% delay. These results suggest that interfacial hydrogen-bonding regulation, together with the ─CF3-modified benzoxazine-derived structure and compact char formation, contributes to improved flame resistance, structural retention, and battery-level thermal-abuse protection.

papers.title: Catalytic and Hydrophobic Modification of Ammonium Perchlorate by Co3O4/PTFE for Solid Propellant Applications
papers.abstract: Ammonium perchlorate (AP) is a widely used oxidizer in composite solid propellants, but its high decomposition temperature and hygroscopicity limit energy utilization and moisture resistance. Here, AP/Co3O4 and AP/Co3O4/PTFE composite particles were prepared by physical mixing and solvent-antisolvent methods. Structural characterization revealed changes in the composite morphology and confirmed the presence of PTFE in the ternary composites. Ground Co3O4 markedly promoted AP decomposition, and the optimized AP/Co3O4/PTFE-2 composite exhibited a DSC high-temperature decomposition peak at 309.0 °C (20 °C/min) and an apparent activation energy of 131.67 kJ·mol−1, compared with 450.6 °C and 196.10 kJ·mol−1 for pure AP. PTFE modification increased the water contact angle from 16.81° to 101.02° and reduced the 72 h moisture uptake from 0.31 to approximately 0.01 wt%. These results demonstrate a dual-functional strategy that combines efficient thermal decomposition catalysis with markedly improved moisture resistance for AP-based energetic materials.

papers.title: Pharmacological Mechanisms and Emerging Therapeutic Applications of Metformin
papers.abstract: Metformin is one of the most widely used medications for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus. Its principal glucose-lowering properties are related to the inhibition of hepatic gluconeogenesis and enhancement of peripheral insulin sensitivity. At the same time, growing data indicate that metformin might affect the intestines, gut microflora, cell metabolism, inflammation, oxidative stress, and autophagy. The present review aims to discuss the pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics of metformin, its clinical applications, adverse effects, and future perspectives. Special focus is made on the possible cardiovascular protective, anti-inflammatory, anticancer, anti-ageing, and polycystic ovary syndrome properties of metformin. The current evidence base allows asserting that metformin is well-established for type 2 diabetes mellitus, preventive treatment of prediabetes in selected populations, and management of certain metabolic disorders in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS). Nevertheless, there is not enough evidence for using metformin as a means of cancer and cardiovascular disease prevention, as well as healthy ageing. Patient-specific factors, dosing, and exposure can be considered as possible causes for different results of treatment. In general, metformin is still one of the key medicines for metabolic disorder treatment, while well-conducted randomized clinical trials are required to validate its new indications and promote personalized treatment approaches.

papers.title: Rapid semi-analytical evaluation of transient heat conduction integrals for prescribed surface-temperature strips
papers.abstract: Abstract Rapid and accurate thermal analysis is essential for parametric design sweeps and rapid thermal assessment in electronic packaging, including the prediction of finite-pulse integrated thermal deficit and thermal response time. These engineering quantities involve time-integrated functionals of transient temperature fields, which ultimately reduce to definite integrals containing the lower incomplete gamma function. For arbitrary surface-temperature profiles, however, no general closed-form evaluation exists for such integrals. This paper proposes a rapid semi-analytical method for transient heat conduction in a semi-infinite substrate subject to prescribed surface-temperature profiles. The method first derives a family of closed-form identities that express a structured class of these integrals in elementary functions. A semi-analytical scheme is then developed by replacing the nested double quadrature with two single quadratures, substantially reducing the per-point computational cost. Using Taylor and Chebyshev expansions, the scheme is further extended to arbitrary analytic or continuous surface-temperature profiles. Four boundary profiles, uniform, linearly graded, quadratic, and Gaussian, demonstrate the method for thermal deficit evaluation and response-time prediction. For the uniform case, the semi-analytical scheme agrees with an independent direct double-quadrature benchmark, with an average relative difference below $$10^{-9}$$ 10 - 9 , while being 36 to 40 times faster at comparable accuracy. These results confirm that the method provides a practical reduced-order tool for parametric design sweeps and rapid thermal assessment in semi-infinite substrates.

These results confirm that the method provides a practical reduced-order tool for parametric design sweeps and rapid thermal assessment in semi-infinite substrates.

papers.title: Stimuli-Responsive Copper Modified Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles as Smart Antimicrobial Delivery System for Antimicrobial Applications
papers.abstract: The emergence of multidrug-resistant pathogens poses a significant challenge to conventional antimicrobial therapies and underscores the urgent need for innovative therapeutic strategies using highly efficacious and less toxic antimicrobial compounds, as well as more targeted antimicrobial delivery strategies to prevent uncontrolled release, which contributes to the rise of drug resistance. In this study, the design and synthesis of copper-modified mesoporous silica nanoparticles (Cu-MSNs) were described as a stimuli-responsive, smart antimicrobial delivery system incorporating carvacrol as a bioactive alternative to conventional antibiotics. The Cu-MSNs exhibit high surface area, tunable pore size, and efficient carvacrol loading. Copper ions embedded within the silica matrix provide intrinsic antimicrobial activity and may enhance the antimicrobial effect of carvacrol. Poly(2-(dimethylamino) ethyl methacrylate) (PDMAEMA) brushes were anchored on Cu-MSNs via surface-initiated atom transfer radical polymerization (SI-ATRP). The PDMAEMA brushes provided stimuli-responsive behavior, enabling pH- and temperature-dependent modulation of carvacrol release. The successful synthesis of Cu-MSN-PDMAEMA has been confirmed by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), elemental analysis (EA), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Moreover, stimuli-responsive behavior was confirmed using dynamic light scattering (DLS) experiments, demonstrating the pH- and temperature-dependent response of the PDMAEMA brushes. Finally, the carvacrol release behavior was studied at different pH values by using a sensitive paper-based electrochemical sensor. The multifunctional nanoplatform exhibited antimicrobial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria as well as antiviral activity against representative enveloped and non-enveloped viral models. This synergistic design combines the benefits of a natural antimicrobial agent, intrinsic metallic activity, and smart polymer regulation, offering an strategy to enhance efficacy while minimizing off-target effects. Release studies demonstrated pH-triggered carvacrol delivery, with enhanced release under acidic conditions, confirming the gating function of the PDMAEMA brushes, highlighting the potential of these particles as an antibiotic-free alternative for preventing microbial infections while mitigating the development of antimicrobial resistance (AMR).

papers.title: Effects of Vacuum and Modified Atmosphere Packaging on Physicochemical and Microbiological Quality of Cooked Squid Stuffed with Sticky Rice During Refrigerated Storage
papers.journal: ASEAN Journal of Scientific and Technological Reports
papers.abstract: Stuffed squid with sticky rice (Tupa Sutong) is a traditional seafood product from southern Thailand with limited refrigerated shelf life because of rapid microbial spoilage and quality deterioration. This study evaluated the effects of atmospheric packaging (AP), vacuum packaging (VP), and modified atmosphere packaging (MAP; 50% O₂, 25% CO₂, and 25% N₂) on the physicochemical and microbiological quality of cooked stuffed squid during refrigerated storage (4 ± 2 °C) for 24 days. Changes in hardness, pH, total volatile basic nitrogen (TVB-N), trimethylamine nitrogen (TMA-N), thiobarbituric acid (TBA), and total viable count (TVC) were determined throughout storage. Storage time significantly affected all quality parameters (p 0.05). Samples stored under AP deteriorated most rapidly, showing faster increases in TVB-N, TMA-N, TBA, and TVC, accompanied by a greater reduction in texture quality. Both VP and MAP delayed quality deterioration by slowing microbial growth and chemical changes during storage. Based on the microbiological acceptability limit, the shelf life of the product was 12, 18, and 21 days under AP, MAP, and VP, respectively. Among the packaging systems evaluated, VP provided the greatest extension of refrigerated shelf life while maintaining the physicochemical and microbiological quality of cooked stuffed squid with sticky rice. These findings provide useful information for selecting appropriate packaging systems for the commercial production and distribution of this traditional seafood product.

papers.title: Comparison of three occlusal splint material systems manufactured by conventional, subtractive, and additive techniques
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To compare the thermal-viscoelastic behavior, hygroscopic properties, color stability, and surface morphology of three commercial occlusal splint material systems produced by conventional heat polymerization, CAD/CAM milling, and 3D printing. The null hypothesis was that the three material systems would not differ in thermal-viscoelastic behavior, hygroscopic properties, or color stability. Surface morphology was assessed qualitatively as a complementary outcome. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Heat-polymerized polymethyl methacrylate (HEC), CAD/CAM-milled polymethyl methacrylate (CAD-M), and a 3D-printed photopolymer resin (3DP) were evaluated. Dynamic mechanical analysis was performed to determine glass transition temperature (Tg), tan δ, and thermal heterogeneity (n = 5). Water sorption (WS), solubility (SL), and color change after coffee immersion (ΔE00) were assessed (n = 8). Surface morphology was qualitatively analyzed by atomic force microscopy and scanning electron microscopy. RESULTS: Significant differences were observed among the material systems for thermal and hygroscopic outcomes. CAD-M presented the highest mean Tg (149.58 ± 0.95 °C), the lowest water sorption (18.76 ± 0.56 µg/mm³), the lowest solubility (2.59 ± 0.48 µg/mm³), and a ΔE00 of 2.29 ± 1.20 after 7 days of coffee immersion. Conversely, 3DP showed the lowest Tg (83.18 ± 7.87 °C), highest WS (35.12 ± 0.82 µg/mm³), highest SL (6.16 ± 0.40 µg/mm³), greatest color change, and a more irregular surface morphology. CONCLUSIONS: The three evaluated commercial material systems differed in thermal-viscoelastic behavior, hygroscopic properties, color stability, and surface morphology. Among the specific systems tested, CAD-M showed the most favorable overall laboratory profile. Because each manufacturing approach was represented by a single commercial material with a distinct composition, these differences cannot be attributed exclusively to the manufacturing route. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Under the in vitro conditions tested, the milled material system showed a higher glass transition temperature and lower water sorption, solubility and coffee-induced discoloration than the 3D-printed system. Whether these laboratory differences translate into differences in the clinical performance of occlusal splints was not assessed in this study.

papers.title: Predicting animal movement metrics across the species range for landscape-scale applications
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Understanding animal movement across broad ecological contexts is essential for guiding management decisions in natural resource and animal disease management. However, most movement studies collect data over small spatial extents, which challenges using the data for landscape-scale management applications. Methods We collated relocation data from 564 wild pigs spanning 25 studies across 10 states in the United States. We derived net and daily displacement distributions for individuals in each of 4 seasons. We fit gamma distributions to displacement distributions and derived mean and dispersion parameters as metrics of displacement magnitude and variation. We modeled mean and dispersion variables using gradient-boosted regression, including landscape and weather predictors, and predicted daily and net displacement distributions across the species range. We used integrated step selection analysis to estimate habitat selection for wild pig groups sharing a common composition of habitat availability across the studied populations. Results Female average ( ± 95% confidence interval) net displacement means varied by season, peaking in Jul-Sept at 1,152 ± 140 m along with daily displacement mean distances of 650 ± 41 m. Average net displacement means for males peaked in Oct.-Dec. at 1,651 ± 160 m with daily displacement mean distances of 1,092 ± 95 m. Extreme net displacement values ranged up to 9,649 m and 4,080 m for male and female, respectively, and extreme daily displacement distribution means of 6,616 m for males, and 3,855 m for females. Almost half of the individuals included a similar composition of habitat availability, regardless of study site location. Herbaceous wetland was the most consistently favored land type and was available for more than 70% of all individual pigs across all studies. Preference for other land types depended strongly on habitat availability. Conclusions By comparing movement and habitat selection across a large geographic extent, our work provides new insights about the environmental drivers and limits of wild pig movement behavior. Our workflow digests variation wild pig movement distributions and habitat selection into parameters that can be used to predict movement on heterogeneous landscapes for downstream applications such as invasive species elimination campaigns or disease management.

papers.title: Finite-bias Coulomb blockade thermometry
papers.abstract: Coulomb blockade thermometers (CBTs) are versatile and, in principle, primary thermometers operating down to the micro-Kelvin range but bias heating spoils the thermometry and the primary mode. Here, we introduce a method to extract the CBT electron temperature in the presence of heat created by an arbitrary bias voltage, and without assumptions on the heat flow mechanisms. The charging energy is extracted with high precision and without any other knowledge, thus making true primary thermometry possible. The experiment also reveals a subtle dependence of the charging energy on phonon temperature below 100 mK likely due to the amorphous AlO$_x$ tunnel junctions.

papers.title: The role of nMOFs in anticancer combinations of photodynamic therapy and immunotherapy
papers.abstract: Nano Metal–Organic Frameworks (nMOFs) have emerged as a versatile class of porous materials with significant potential in biomedical applications, particularly in cancer treatment. This review explores the pivotal role of nMOFs in facilitating the combina-tion of photodynamic therapy (PDT) and immunotherapy (IMT), focusing on their unique capabilities to synergistically enhance therapeutic outcomes. By serving as effi-cient photosensitizer and immunotherapy drug carriers nMOFs serve as immune re-sponse modulators and enable targeted tumour destruction through reactive oxygen species generation while simultaneously stimulating antitumor immunity. The com-bination of nMOF-based PDT and immunotherapy represents a promising strategy for more effective, personalized cancer treatments. This article highlights recent progress, challenges, and future perspectives in leveraging nMOFs for the synergistic cancer therapy landscape.

papers.title: Enhanced apoptotic effects of nano-encapsulated curcumin and capsacin: synthesis, characterization and anticancer activity in HepG2, MCF7, and A549 cells
papers.journal: Beni-Suef University Journal of Basic and Applied Sciences
papers.abstract: Abstract Curcumin and capsaicin are natural compounds with known therapeutic potential but limited clinical utility due to poor solubility and bioavailability. In this study, nanoformulations of curcumin and capsaicin were developed using the thin-film hydration method and characterized by transmission electron microscopy (TEM), dynamic light scattering (DLS), zeta potential, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). The nanocapsules demonstrated enhanced physicochemical stability, with capsaicin nanoparticles averaging ~ 49 nm and curcumin ~ 76 nm. Cytotoxicity assays in HepG2 (Human hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer)), MCF-7 (Human breast adenocarcinoma), and A549 (Human lung adenocarcinoma epithelial) cell lines revealed potent anti-proliferative effects, especially when both nanoparticles were combined, indicating a synergistic interaction. Gene expression analysis showed upregulation of pro-apoptotic markers ( p53 and Bax ) and downregulation of anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 , confirming apoptosis induction via the p53/BAX/BCL2 pathway. These findings highlight the potential of nano-curcumin and nano-capsaicin as effective, complementary anticancer agents and support their further development for biomedical applications.

The nanocapsules demonstrated enhanced physicochemical stability, with capsaicin nanoparticles averaging ~ 49 nm and curcumin ~ 76 nm. These findings highlight the potential of nano-curcumin and nano-capsaicin as effective, complementary anticancer agents and support their further development for biomedical applications.

papers.title: Loss mechanisms in cryogenic microwave epitaxial AlN resonators
papers.journal: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics
papers.abstract: Abstract Epitaxial aluminum nitride (AlN) thin-film bulk acoustic resonators (FBARs) enable low-loss filtering for future 6G systems. They also provide a compact approach for qubit sensing at cryogenic temperatures. However, these devices are rarely characterized systematically from room temperature to cryogenic temperatures, and the mechanisms that limit their cryogenic performance remain unclear. In this work, we study a 15.6 GHz epitaxial AlN FBAR from room temperature to cryogenic temperatures to identify losses from the AlN film and those introduced by the electrodes, anchors, and other device layers. Small-signal RF measurements from 294 K down to 6.5 K show an increase in the unloaded Qₘₐₓ from 245 to 1729. A temperature-dependent model that includes phonon–phonon scattering, thermoelastic damping, dielectric loss, electrical loss, and anchor loss helps explain the measured Q(T) trend and identifies a transition from the Landau–Rumer to the Akhiezer regime near 270 K. The model indicates that acoustic energy leakage through the anchors and electrical loss set upper bounds on Q. Energy transfer from the main resonant mode to spurious acoustic modes can also lower the measured Q. Improving anchor isolation, suppressing spurious modes, and reducing electrode loss, including through superconducting electrodes, increase the cryogenic Q. These results guide the design of higher-Q acoustic resonators for high-frequency 6G filters and cryogenic quantum-microwave circuits.
papers.summary: Abstract Epitaxial aluminum nitride (AlN) thin-film bulk acoustic resonators (FBARs) enable low-loss filtering for future 6G systems. The model indicates that acoustic energy leakage through the anchors and electrical loss set upper bounds on Q. papers.title: Cross‐Linked Poly(Styrene‐Co‐Styrene Sulfonate) Membranes: Effect of Crosslinking on Proton Conductivity and Physicochemical Properties
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT In the present study, cross‐linked poly(styrene‐co‐styrene sulfonate), poly(Sty‐co‐StyS) membranes are prepared using divinylbenzene (DVB) cross‐linker at different weight percentages via free‐radical polymerization in order to achieve desirable proton conductivity and mechanical properties for proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolyzer applications. The role of crosslinker in the membrane is also investigated by conducting a comparison study using the membrane without cross‐linker. The cross‐linked poly(Sty‐co‐StyS) membrane exhibits enhanced thermal stability compared to the non‐cross‐linked membrane as revealed by thermal analysis. The sulfonated copolymer showed good solubility and film formation ability in a suitable solvent and composition. The proton conductivities of all the synthesized membranes range between 10 −3 and 10 −2 S/cm, and the other physico‐chemical properties of the membranes were also studied. Among all the membranes, the cross‐linked poly(Sty‐co‐StyS) membrane with 1% crosslinker showed the proton conductivity as high as 1.57 × 10 −2 S/cm, water uptake of 38.2%, and ion exchange capacity of 2.7 mmol/g and excellent thermal stability up to 450°C.

papers.title: Formation of gradient residual stress in ultrasonic vibration-assisted end grinding inconel 718: microscopic mechanism and modeling
papers.journal: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
papers.abstract: Abstract Residual stress (RS) on machined surfaces critically influences in-service performance. However, the underlying microscopic physical mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. The plastic deformation behavior under different parameters in ultrasonic vibration-assisted end grinding (UVAEG) was systematically investigated by RS characterization, in-situ grinding force measurement, and subsurface microstructure observation. An evaluation method for RS on machined surfaces was proposed. A prediction model for RS on machined surfaces was established based on dislocation pile-up theory. The microscopic mechanism of RS formation was analyzed. The effects of spindle speed and grinding depth on plastic deformation depth and the formation of gradient RS were also systematically studied. The results show that surface RS is positively correlated with dislocation density. The residual stress induced by grinding primarily originates from local stress fields generated by microstructural defects within the material. A larger plastic deformation depth is favorable for the formation of a deeper RS affected layer. Lower spindle speed and larger cutting depth can generate higher grinding forces, thereby promoting dislocation multiplication and migration, increasing the degree of lattice distortion and the depth of the affected layer, and consequently resulting in higher residual stress and a deeper affected layer. This study elucidates the microscopic mechanisms underlying internal stress formation at machined surfaces and provides a theoretical basis for optimizing machining processes to control material performance effectively.

This study elucidates the microscopic mechanisms underlying internal stress formation at machined surfaces and provides a theoretical basis for optimizing machining processes to control material performance effectively.

papers.title: EFT validity and truncation uncertainty from few nuisance parameters
papers.abstract: A bstract An observable in an Effective Field Theory (EFT) is an expansion in a set of small parameters, no different than any other perturbation series. Truncating such a series expansion leaves the leading dropped term as the dominant source of error, and that term itself contains a calculable portion. We explore the partial calculation of this next-order error, available at dim-6 2 in SMEFT with no additional tools needed to simulate it, and explore how to efficiently use that partial calculation to model the next-order uncertainty in full using a minimal number of nuisance parameters. This estimate of the uncertainty of the EFT signal rate naturally imposes EFT validity by ensuring that bounds are driven by kinematic regions where truncation uncertainties are parametrically smaller than the signal. We incorporate the calculable dim-6 2 piece into the signal and cover the remaining higher-dimension uncertainty with a small set of nuisance parameters derived from a scan over Wilson-coefficient values. Our algorithm to determine the relevant nuisance parameters and distributions is automation-friendly and applies to arbitrary truncation choices. We then provide multiple examples of its implementation in high-energy collider processes focused on SMEFT truncated at 𝒪(Λ −2 ), where the dim-6 2 piece is used to estimate the full 𝒪(Λ −4 ) dependence. In the examples considered here the reduction of nuisance parameters is appreciable, generically reducing the nuisance parameter count by an order of magnitude compared to naïve estimates.

papers.title: Fractional quantum ferroelectric control of spin-valley locking and valley Hall effects in altermagnetic monolayer Cr 2 S 2
papers.abstract: Fractional quantum multiferroics, arising from the coupling between fractional quantum ferroelectricity (FQFE) and altermagnetism (AM), provide a promising platform for nonvolatile control of momentum dependent spin splitting in systems with zero net magnetization. However, extending this FQFE-AM coupling to valley degrees of freedom and Berry curvature driven valley Hall effects remains largely unexplored. Here, using first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that monolayer Cr2S2 realizes a two dimensional FQFE-AM platform with two switchable FQFE states connected by composite symmetry operations combining a fractional lattice translation with time reversal or parity-time reversal. We show that FQFE switching reverses the AM spin-polarized band structure and interchanges the spin characters of the X and Y valleys without rotating the Néel vector, thereby enabling polarization switchable spin-valley locking. Moreover, the two FQFE states exhibit reversed Berry curvature distributions, which, together with the switched spin-valley locking, enable polarization controlled valley Hall effects under both electron and hole doping. These results demonstrate a symmetry based mechanism for nonvolatile electrical control of AM spin splitting, spin-valley locking, and valley Hall effects, offering a general route toward low-power valleytronic devices based on FQFE-AM coupling.

papers.title: Organic condensation derived from different volatility parameterizations and its implications for ambient nanoparticle growth
papers.abstract: Abstract. Atmospheric new particle formation (NPF) supplies up to half of global cloud condensation nuclei, yet the growth of sub-15 nm nanoparticles—the stage most vulnerable to scavenging—remains poorly constrained, largely because the volatility of oxygenated organic molecules (OOMs) is highly uncertain. Using a purpose-built laminar flow reactor that isolates particle–particle coagulation from OOM condensation, we show that six of seven widely used OOM volatility parameterizations substantially overestimate nanoparticle growth rates, with the largest bias under the high-NOx conditions. A recent parameterization constrained by ambient organic aerosol volatility reproduces our laboratory observations across diverse OOM precursors, seed sizes (3–5 nm), and NOx regimes. By applying this laboratory-validated framework to NPF events at Lake Tai, China, in summer 2023, OOM and H2SO4 condensation explain about 53 % of the observed 3–15 nm growth rate, leaving a residual that persists even at the upper bound of measurement uncertainty. Together, our laboratory experiments and field observations provide strong evidence that particle coagulation and vapour condensation alone cannot account for ambient nanoparticle growth, revealing a clear gap in our understanding of this process. This gap may point to additional processes, not yet accounted for in current frameworks, that could contribute to nanoparticle growth in polluted atmospheres, or it may reflect uncertainties in other parameters.

papers.title: Architectured AlN/Al composites produced by material extrusion and pressure infiltration: processing–structure–property relationships
papers.abstract: Abstract This work presents a hybrid manufacturing route combining material extrusion of porous AlN preforms with pressure-assisted aluminum infiltration for the fabrication of architectured AlN/Al composites. Porous AlN preforms were produced by Material Extrusion (MEX) Fused Granulate Fabrication (FGF), followed by debinding and sintering to obtain an interconnected ceramic framework. The porous AlN line infill structures were subsequently infiltrated with molten aluminum alloy under pressure, resulting in a dense interpenetrating ceramic–metal composite. Physical parameters and the microstructural evolution throughout the processing route was investigated using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS), and X-ray computed tomography (XCT). Microstructural observations confirmed homogeneous aluminum distribution and a well-defined AlN/Al interface throughout the composite. Tomographic analysis revealing a final composite containing 75.4 vol.% AlN and 24.6 vol.% Al. The overall porosity determined by X-ray tomography and microstructural analysis was approximately 0.68 vol.%. Thermomechanical characterization showed stable behavior up to 500°C, with coefficients of thermal expansion ranging from 11.6 to 12.9 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹ after thermal stabilization. Compression testing revealed moderate anisotropy associated with the printed architecture, with average compressive strengths of 511 MPa and 567 MPa in the XY and Z directions, respectively.

papers.title: Physics-informed symbolic regression for predicting the glass transition temperature of alkali borate glasses
papers.abstract: The glass transition temperature ( T g ) of alkali borate glasses is strongly composition-dependent and difficult to predict from first principles due to the structural complexity of the boron network. Here, we apply physics-informed symbolic regression (combining evolutionary search with physically meaningful descriptors) to derive an interpretable closed-form expression for T g for the x M 2 O ⋅ ( 100 − x ) B 2 O 3 glass family, with M = Li, Na and K, and x expressed in mol%, followed by extrapolation to M = Rb and Cs. The resulting model achieves a root mean square error of 14–16 K while maintaining clear physical interpretability, explicitly capturing the interplay among T g , structural dissociation energy, and network packing. Critically, models built on the Rigid Unit Packing Fraction (RUPF) yield substantially more realistic T g predictions than those using the conventional Atomic Packing Fraction (APF), as APF overestimates structural rigidity at intermediate compositions. The fitted dissociation energies are further validated against the revised Makishima–Mackenzie model, confirming that the inferred parameters are physically consistent, not merely statistically effective, within the alkali borate family. Finally, Monte Carlo uncertainty quantification reveals that prediction uncertainty is highest in the compositional regions associated with the boron anomaly, directly linking model limitations to a known structural transition in these glasses. This result highlights the potential of physics-informed symbolic regression as a transparent and interpretable alternative to black-box models for property prediction in glass systems.

papers.title: Hamiltonian Two-Way Coupling of Nonlinear Waves and 3D Flows
papers.abstract: Simulating large-scale free-surface flow by coupling a localized 3D fluid solver to a cheaper 2D surface model has long faced a mismatch in wave dynamics: efficient 2D wave models used in graphics are typically either linear or non-dispersive. These models are fast, simple, and accurate for calm, small-amplitude seas, but coupling them to strongly nonlinear 3D solvers produces visible reflections and artifacts at the 2D-3D interface. We address this problem by introducing a nonlinear and dispersive 2D wave model based on the canonical Zakharov formulation. Its Hamiltonian structure enables canonically consistent two-way coupling, allowing information to pass smoothly across the 2D-3D interface. Our 2D solver reduces mean wave-height error by factors of 1.7–5× relative to SWE, BEM, and Airy baselines while running more than 10 3 × faster than BEM; it achieves greater nonlinear accuracy and coupling fidelity than SWE and Airy, with minor losses in speed and stability. Coupling it with a 3D Navier-Stokes solver yields a full system that suppresses visible seam artifacts across a range of experiments, including dispersion-matching and Kelvin-wake tests, and runs over 4× faster than a full-domain GPU NB-FLIP simulation.

Our 2D solver reduces mean wave-height error by factors of 1.7–5× relative to SWE, BEM, and Airy baselines while running more than 10 3 × faster than BEM; it achieves greater nonlinear accuracy and coupling fidelity than SWE and Airy, with minor losses in speed and stability. Coupling it with a 3D Navier-Stokes solver yields a full system that suppresses visible seam artifacts across a range of experiments, including dispersion-matching and Kelvin-wake tests, and runs over 4× faster than a full-domain GPU NB-FLIP simulation.

papers.title: High-efficiency iodine capture in waste biomass-based activated carbon: Effects of biomass types on iodine adsorption and its mechanism
papers.abstract: Abstract The generation of radioactive iodine isotopes during nuclear energy utilization can cause serious harm to the ecological environment and public safety. While porous activated carbon shows promise for iodine capture, balancing its adsorption performance with production costs is a central challenge that hinders its practical adoption in nuclear waste management and emergency response. In this study, porous activated carbons were prepared from agricultural wastes such as rice straw, corn stover, soybean straw, rapeseed straw, and rapeseed cake through hydrothermal carbonization and KOH activation methods. The results showed that the porous activated carbon derived from rapeseed cake (RS) had the highest specific surface area (2025 m 2 /g), with iodine adsorption capacities of 5078 mg/g for iodine vapor, 1128 mg/g for iodine in cyclohexane solution, and 2187 mg/g for iodine in aqueous solution. The adsorption of iodine vapor and iodine in aqueous solution was primarily attributed to the micropores and mesopores of the ACs, while iodine adsorption in cyclohexane solution was predominantly governed by micropores of the ACs. Moreover, the adsorption behavior of ACs followed pseudo-second-order kinetics and Langmuir isotherm models, indicating that the adsorption process was primarily physical adsorption. These results provide a theoretical basis for the further design and development of adsorbents for iodine capture from nuclear waste and nuclear accidents, as well as for the high-value utilization of agricultural waste.

papers.title: Effects of recycled PET aggregate size and replacement level on hot mix asphalt performance
papers.abstract: Abstract The increasing accumulation of plastic waste has intensified the need for sustainable reuse strategies in construction materials. This study investigates the feasibility of using recycled polyethylene terephthalate (rPET) from post‑consumer bottles as a partial replacement for natural aggregates in hot mix asphalt (HMA) using the dry mixing method, emphasizing the influence of particle size and replacement level on HMA performance. rPET particles with natural‑aggregate‑like physical characteristics were produced and sieved into standard size fractions to function as rPET aggregates. The adhesion behavior and mechanical properties of rPET aggregates were evaluated and compared with limestone aggregates used in this study under different temperature conditions. HMA performance was assessed through dynamic creep tests (flow number and permanent deformation) at 40 °C, and moisture susceptibility and indirect tensile fatigue tests at 25 °C. To investigate the effect of particle size, 10% of natural aggregates (by volume) were replaced with rPET aggregates in five size ranges from ≤ 0.3 to 19 mm, and the most effective range was used to determine the optimum replacement level. The results showed that at medium-to-high temperatures, rPET had better interfacial adhesion with bitumen than with limestone, and rPET aggregates performed better in the LAA and AIV tests. Optimal performance was achieved using 4.75–12.5 mm rPET aggregates, where 18% replacement increased creep resistance by 57% and reduced moisture susceptibility by 7%, while 16% replacement improved fatigue life by 295%. These findings demonstrate that rPET aggregates provide an environmentally sustainable alternative for enhancing HMA performance.

papers.title: Effect of calcium carbonate on the thermodynamics and kinetics of lead sulfide carbothermic reduction
papers.abstract: Abstract The effect of calcium carbonate on the thermodynamics and apparent kinetics of lead sulfide (PbS) carbothermic reduction was investigated in the PbS–Na 2 CO 3 –C and PbS–Na 2 CO 3 –CaCO 3 –C systems at 800–1100 °C. Thermodynamic analysis included Gibbs free energy calculations and multiphase equilibrium modeling, while kinetic behavior was evaluated through time-resolved gas analysis and TG–DTG–DSC measurements. Equilibrium calculations revealed predominant Na 2 S formation in the CaCO 3 -free system and CaS formation in the CaCO 3 -containing system. At 800 °C, the calculated equilibrium amount of metallic lead increased from 804.29 to 999.83 mol upon CaCO 3 addition, based on 1000 mol of initial PbS. Sodium carbonate remained largely unconsumed in the CaCO 3 -containing system. Experimental results demonstrated a pronounced temperature-dependent effect of CaCO 3 . At 800 °C, the apparent reaction extent (α app ) was 70.6% with CaCO 3 and 74.9% without it. At 900, 1000, and 1100 °C, α app reached 96.4%, 97.9%, and 99.5%, respectively, in the CaCO 3 -containing system, accompanied by higher apparent reaction rates. The corresponding apparent activation energies were 32.0 and 52.9 kJ·mol − 1 , indicating stronger temperature sensitivity with CaCO 3 addition. These findings demonstrate that CaCO 3 modifies sulfur distribution and the apparent kinetic behavior of PbS-containing systems.

papers.title: Lightweight and anisotropic polyimide-based composite foams for efficient flame retardancy, thermal insulation and electromagnetic interference shielding applications
papers.abstract: There is a growing need for lightweight porous materials that combine cushioning and shock absorption, high-temperature fire protection, thermal insulation and electromagnetic properties in extreme engineering environments. Herein, a simple strategy was employed to combine polyimide foam (PIF) and silica aerogel (SiA) to prepare a series of polyimide/silica aerogel (PI/SiA) composite foams with anisotropic structure and properties. The anisotropic micrometer-scale foam pore structure and the three-dimensional nano “pearl-necklace-like” porous structure collectively constructed the hierarchical porous structure, endowing PI/SiA composite foams with enhanced mechanical and thermal properties. The unique anisotropic porous structure conferred PI/SiA composite foams with improved mechanical strength in the vertical direction and superior mechanical flexibility in the horizontal direction. In addition, the prepared PI/SiA composite foams exhibited outstanding thermal stability and self-extinguishing flame retardancy, with an initial thermal decomposition temperature and a limiting oxygen index reaching as high as 587.7℃ and 67.7%, respectively, demonstrating promising application prospects in high-temperature fire protection fields. The PI/SiA composite foams also displayed excellent thermal insulation and anisotropic thermal management performance, with a low thermal conductivity of 0.0275 W/(m·K) and a large surface temperature difference of 131.9℃. Moreover, the high-temperature pyrolysis residue of PI/SiA composite foams (i.e., PIC/SiA composite foams) exhibited anisotropic electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding performance, with the EMI shielding effectiveness and specific EMI shielding effectiveness in the horizontal direction reaching as high as 50.5 dB and 10194.0 dB/(g/cm 2 ), respectively. Thus, polyimide-based composite foams with excellent mechanical, thermal and electromagnetic properties hold broad application prospects in extreme environments.

papers.title: Improved prediction model for compressive strength of self-compacting concrete incorporating fly ash and tuff powder at different curing ages
papers.abstract: Tuff powder (TP), an abundant mineral additive in Xizang, China, offers a cost-effective and performance-enhancing alternative to fly ash (FA). To quantify their cementitious characteristics, eight groups of mortars with varying FA and TP contents at different curing ages were tested for compressive strength to derive cementitious coefficients. Additionally, nineteen groups of SCCs with different water-to-binder ratios, superplasticizer contents, TP and FA contents, sand ratios, and gravel contents were examined to develop an improved compressive strength prediction model. The model’s accuracy was further verified using five groups of SCCs prepared with additional modifiers and aggregates of different types, contents, and gradations. Results indicate that the cementitious coefficients of TP and FA align with their intrinsic cementitious properties. The improved model shows strong agreement with experimental results for compressive strengths at 3 and 7 d, and demonstrates superior accuracy for 28-day predictions compared to the original model, effectively capturing the synergistic effects of FA and TP. Furthermore, a mix design method integrating the improved model with paste rheology theory is proposed to predict both compressive strength and workability of SCC.

papers.title: Optimization of a Laccase Biosynthesis and Mediator System: A Potential Headway for Sustainable Microplastic Degradation
papers.abstract: Abstract The global accumulation of microplastics has become a critical environmental challenge due to their persistence, widespread distribution, and adverse effects on ecosystems and human health. Although enzymatic degradation has emerged as a sustainable alternative to conventional physicochemical remediation methods, the practical application of laccase (Lac) remains constrained by low enzyme productivity, limited stability, high production costs, and insufficient activity towards recalcitrant non-phenolic polymers such as polyethylene and polystyrene. Furthermore, current studies are often fragmented, focusing on either enzyme production or degradation performance, while lacking an integrated assessment of catalytic optimization, mediator systems, scalability, and environmental sustainability. This review provides a critical and comprehensive evaluation of recent advances in optimizing Lac biosynthesis and laccase-mediator systems (LMS) for microplastic degradation. Unlike previous reviews, it integrates developments in strain engineering, heterologous expression, protein engineering, omics-guided process optimization, enzyme immobilization, mediator selection, and techno-economic considerations within a single framework. Particular attention is given to how LMS expands the oxidative capacity of Lac towards resistant plastic polymers and to the evidence required to distinguish surface modification from true polymer depolymerization. Current evidence suggests that combining optimized Lac production, suitable mediators, and advanced immobilization strategies can substantially enhance catalytic efficiency, operational stability, and process feasibility. However, challenges remain regarding degradation-product toxicity, mediator recovery, standardization of degradation assessment, and large-scale implementation. Future research should focus on pilot-scale validation, comprehensive ecotoxicological assessment, standardized life-cycle assessment, and integrated techno-economic analysis to identify environmental trade-offs associated with enzyme production, mediator utilization, and degradation-product management. Collectively, this review provides a forward-looking framework for advancing laccase-based technologies toward sustainable and scalable microplastic remediation.

papers.title: Ethyl acetate extract of Tinospora crispa alleviates osteoarthritis by suppressing ERK1/2-mediated MMP13 transcription and cartilage degradation
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic degenerative joint disorder characterized by inflammation, oxidative stress, and cartilage destruction, resulting in pain, locomotor dysfunction, and substantial health burdens in both humans and animals; however, safe and effective long-term therapeutic strategies remain limited. Tinospora crispa (TC) is a traditional ethnomedicine with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, yet its therapeutic effects and underlying mechanisms in OA remain unclear. LC‒MS analysis revealed 11 main compounds in the TC extract. The network pharmacology results revealed that MMP9, MMP13, TNF, and MAPK signaling pathway components were key candidate targets of TC for the treatment of osteoarthritis. This study demonstrated that TC extract alleviated OA in mice subjected to destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM) surgery by reducing pain-related sensitivity, inhibiting osteophyte formation and preventing cartilage matrix degradation. In vitro experiments demonstrated that TC extract inhibited chondrocyte apoptosis and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, downregulated the expression of inflammatory cytokines and genes involved in extracellular matrix degradation, and suppressed MMP13 promoter activity. RNA-seq analysis indicated that the TC extract suppressed ERK1/2 pathway activity, which was subsequently confirmed by western blotting. Syringic acid (SA), a major active compound of TC extract, was also shown to inhibit ROS production, downregulate the expression of inflammatory cytokines and extracellular matrix degradation-related genes, and suppress MMP13 promoter activity in vitro. Finally, western blotting and dual-luciferase assays revealed that TC extract and SA inhibited MMP13 transcription by suppressing ERK1/2 signaling, revealing the mechanism by which they alleviate OA.

papers.title: Direct detection of omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acid incorporation into cells by surface analysis using water cluster secondary ion mass spectrometry imaging
papers.abstract: Water cluster ion beam secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) was used to investigate the fate of essential fatty acids (linoleic acid, LA, and alpha-linolenic acid, ALA) in hormone-receptive (MCF7) and triple-negative (MDA-MB-231) breast cancer cell lines and MCF7 spheroids. SIMS has historically produced low yields of intact lipid signal. However, here, a water gas cluster ion beam (GCIB), that significantly enhances intact ion detection compared to conventional atomic/small cluster ions, was used. In addition to increased molecular signals, the water GCIB produces fragment ions with ratios related to positional isomerism of glycerophospholipids that provided additional direct insights into membrane chemistry. The results show that both cell lines take up both fatty acids and that this uptake leads to an apparent replacement of one fatty acid chain on the different lipids in the cells predominantly in the sn-2 position. The appearance of polyunsaturated triacylglycerides signals indicated that PUFA availability was not the limiting factor here. SIMS imaging of spheroids exposed to the LA and ALA fatty acids showed similar changes in the lipid profile localized to a region of approximately 50-100 µm around the edge of the spheroid.

papers.title: β-cyclodextrin encapsulation of Heracleum persicum essential oil for improved stability, controlled release, and food-related biological applications
papers.abstract: Heracleum persicum essential oil (HPEO) exhibits antioxidant and antibacterial activities, but its application is limited by volatility, poor aqueous solubility, and low stability. To address these limitations, HPEO was encapsulated in β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) to form inclusion complexes (HPEO/βCD-ICs). Three HPEO/β-CD mass ratios (10:90, 15:85, and 20:80, w/w) were investigated to evaluate the effects of formulation composition on encapsulation performance and physicochemical characteristics. The resulting HPEO/βCD-ICs exhibited mean hydrodynamic diameters of 397 to 593 nm and polydispersity index values below 0.3. The 15:85 formulation was selected for further investigation based on its highest zeta potential (+ 58.3 ± 1.95 mV), together with an acceptable particle size and encapsulation efficiency. FT-IR spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, and thermal analyses provided complementary evidence supporting inclusion-complex formation and changes in thermal stability following encapsulation. Encapsulation improved the preservation of antioxidant activity during 30 days of storage under light and dark conditions. Moreover, encapsulation reduced the minimum bactericidal concentrations against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus . HPEO release increased with temperature and relative humidity (RH), reaching 28.1% after 15 days at 40 °C and 75% RH. Release kinetics were generally well described by the Weibull model. Overall, β-CD inclusion complexation represents a promising approach to improving the storage stability and antibacterial performance of HPEO, supporting further investigation of its potential applications in food preservation and active packaging.

papers.title: Detection of field parasitism of the invasive spotted lanternfly (Lycorma delicatula) by native North American wasps using molecular tools
papers.abstract: Abstract The management of invasive pest species frequently involves biological control to suppress the expanding pest populations. Although introduced natural enemies have been favored, the role of native fauna should not be overlooked. The spotted lanternfly ( Lycorma delicatula White; Hemiptera: Fulgoridae) is an invasive, polyphagous plant pest that has rapidly spread across eastern USA over the past decade. Biological control efforts of this pest largely focus on imported parasitoids, but there is increasing evidence of native wasps attacking spotted lanternfly eggs in the USA. To obtain a more accurate estimate of parasitism by one native wasp, Anastatus reduvii (Howard) (Hymenoptera: Eupelmidae), we developed a duplex real-time PCR (qPCR) assay capable of detecting A. reduvii DNA in spotted lanternfly eggs. In silico analysis and non-target testing using three additional Anastatus spp. and five potential host species indicated a low likelihood of false positive amplification. We applied the qPCR assay to spotted lanternfly eggs with parasitoid emergence holes collected from 11 locations in southeastern Pennsylvania, USA that encompass over 6000 km 2 . The assay detected more A. reduvii attacks than Sanger sequencing with universal primers (73 vs . 13 detections, respectively). This new monitoring tool enhances the detection and quantification of parasitism by native wasps, which—with new associations with the invasive pest through host adaptation—may contribute to meaningful biotic resistance and offer potential opportunity for conservation or augmentative biological control.

papers.title: PREPARATION, CHARACTERIZATION AND IN VITRO DRUG RELEASE OF POLY (LACTIC-CO-GLYCOLIC ACID) MICROSPHERES LOADED WITH 5-FLUOROURACIL
authors: P. Ramakrishna*1, S. Krian1, Y. B. Nagamani2, K. Chandra Rekha3
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) is one of the most commonly used anti-cancer drugs to treat colorectal, breast, gastric, pancreatic and skin cancer. The clinical application in humans, however, is restricted because of its fast metabolism, short biological half-life, systemic toxicity, and lack of selectivity towards tumor tissues. PLGA microspheres have been a focus of considerable interest for using as biodegradable drug delivery systems that deliver a sustained and controlled release of drugs. In the present research, 5-FU loaded PLGA microspheres have been prepared by a double emulsion solvent evaporation (W/O/W) method. The prepared microspheres were subjected to particle size analysis, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), X-ray diffraction (XRD), encapsulation efficiency, drug loading and in vitro drug release studies. The prepared microspheres were found to have spherical shape with smooth surfaces and average sizes of 18-42 µm. Both the encapsulation efficiency of the drugs ranged from 55% to 76%, which depended on the polymer concentration. An in vitro release study showed an initial burst release, followed by a sustained release for 10 days. The drug release was found to be in good correlation with Higuchi diffusion kinetics (R² > 0.98). The results show that PLGA microspheres are potential carriers for the sustained delivery of 5-FU.
